Infinitus operates no public developer portal and publishes no OpenAPI: every API endpoint requires an authenticated customer account. It is SOC 2 Type II certified and signs HIPAA Business Associate Agreements. The company is backed by GV and Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Lena Health
providers.description: Lena Health is a Houston, Texas healthcare technology company founded in the Texas Medical Center that combines AI agents with human care navigators to deliver care coordination at scale. Its LenaConnect platform handles routine patient outreach calls, appointment scheduling and coordination, payer and provider hold times, automatic call documentation, EHR integration, and resource and referral management, so human navigators can focus on building trust with patients. Lena offers fully managed care navigation services covering Chronic Care Management (CCM), Transitional Care Management (TCM), rising-risk care management, and annual wellness visits, and works with health plans, accountable care organizations (ACOs), health systems, provider groups, care management providers, and community organizations. The company reports retrospective matched-cohort results of 29% fewer unplanned readmissions, 42% fewer ED visits, and $3,116 saved per patient within 180 days. Lena Health is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, and publishes a trust center. Lena Health is a Techstars portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment; the platform is delivered as a managed service with EHR integration handled through engagements.

providers.name: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources
providers.description: FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) is a platform specification developed by HL7 that defines a set of capabilities for use across the healthcare process, in all jurisdictions, and in many different clinical and administrative contexts. It standardizes how electronic health information is exchanged between systems via REST APIs.

providers.name: Axxess
providers.description: Home health, hospice, and private duty software with REST APIs for managing patient plans of care, visit documentation, billing, scheduling, and OASIS assessments. Axxess provides certified EHR technology with FHIR-compliant interoperability, supporting data exchange across care settings via HL7, TEFCA, FHIR, HITRUST, and HIPAA standards.

providers.name: Guardhat
providers.description: Guardhat (now operating as Aatmunn) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform serving more than 250 companies across oil & gas, utilities, logistics and warehousing, chemicals, mining, infrastructure, and manufacturing. Its SPANR platform is a unified intelligence layer that collects data from connected safety devices and wearables, normalizes it into a single source of truth, applies business logic, and surfaces insights through a suite of applications for digital safety inspections, lone worker safety, gas detection, human condition monitoring, control access zoning, and asset tracking. Originally known for connected hard hats and wearable safety technology, the company rebranded from Guardhat to Aatmunn. Guardhat is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. This profile has been enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or OpenAPI surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Legacy
providers.description: Legacy is a United States direct-to-consumer male fertility company offering at-home sperm testing and sperm cryopreservation without a clinic visit. Customers order a collection kit online, provide a sample at home, and return it by free overnight shipping to Legacy's CLIA-certified, CLEP-approved laboratory, where results appear in a private client dashboard within 48 hours of receipt. Services span basic, standard, and advanced semen analysis (count, concentration, motility, morphology, and Halosperm sperm DNA fragmentation), STI testing, multi-year sperm storage bundles, and male fertility supplements. Legacy serves people trying to conceive and those preserving fertility ahead of a vasectomy, testosterone therapy, gender-affirming care, cancer treatment, or military deployment, and is in-network with selected insurers and employer fertility benefit programs. Legacy publishes no public developer API; its notable machine-readable surface is a first-party llms.txt written for AI answer engines.

providers.name: Magical
providers.description: Magical is an AI-agent platform that automates repetitive administrative and operational workflows without requiring API integrations, instead driving the same web applications and databases a human worker would use. Originally known for its cross-application autofill and text-automation product, Magical has focused on healthcare operations, deploying specialized AI agents for patient access, revenue cycle management, prior authorizations, referrals, benefits verification, records requests, revenue integrity, and payment posting across EHR and payer systems such as Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, Availity, and major insurers. Agents can be deployed individually or combined into autonomous suites, with the company reporting high task accuracy and multi-week deployment timelines. Magical is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock, and SV Angel. Notably, Magical operates through user-interface automation ("no APIs or integrations are required") rather than by exposing a public developer API.

providers.name: Ambience
providers.description: Ambience Healthcare builds an AI operating system for healthcare that reduces clinician administrative burden and protects revenue integrity at the point of care. Its ambient AI platform performs real-time medical encounter transcription, clinical note generation, integrated clinical documentation improvement (CDI) with ICD-10 coding suggestions, and EHR patient-context enrichment across more than 100 specialties in outpatient, emergency, and inpatient settings. The platform integrates directly with major EHRs including Epic, Oracle Cerner, and athenahealth. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Francisco, Ambience is backed by roughly $370M in funding, including a $243M Series C co-led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Oak HC/FT. Ambience exposes a gated Integration API (documentation and access granted on request via emr-integration@ambiencehealthcare.com) rather than a public self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Dentrix
providers.description: Dentrix is a dental practice management platform from Henry Schein One, used by dental offices to manage patients, scheduling, clinical charting, treatment planning, insurance, and billing. Dentrix exposes third-party integration APIs through two distinct channels. The original Dentrix Developer Program (DDP, launched 2012) targets the on-premise Dentrix desktop application: integrations run locally against the office's Dentrix database over password-protected ODBC connections, stored procedures, table views, and DLL functions (authenticated via a RegisterUser call) - it is NOT a public REST/cloud API, and cloud integrations require a locally installed desktop agent. The newer Dentrix Ascend API Exchange (launched July 2023) is a cloud, REST/JSON API over HTTPS secured with OAuth 2.0 on the SOC 2 Type II Dentrix Ascend platform, exposing patient, scheduling, claims, and inventory data. Both channels are partner-gated: access requires an application, a signed agreement, and paid developer fees. There is no public self-serve API key or published OpenAPI, so the APIs below are modeled from Henry Schein One's public developer materials rather than an official machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Forus
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company operating a network that connects physicians, pharmacies, payers, and biopharmaceutical companies to accelerate patient access to prescribed medicines. Its platform automates the administrative work between a clinical decision and treatment initiation: insurance prior authorization, AI-generated denial appeals, financial-assistance enrollment, benefit verification, and pharmacy fulfillment routing. Forus is embedded in physician workflows across most U.S. zip codes and is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. It offers no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Huel
providers.description: Huel (a contraction of "Human Fuel") is a British nutritionally-complete food company founded in June 2015 by Julian Hearn with nutritionist James Collier, headquartered in Tring, Hertfordshire, and operating offices in the UK, US and Europe. It sells plant-based, nutritionally complete powders, ready-to-drink shakes, hot and savoury instant meals, bars and supplements direct to consumers in more than 100 countries, reporting GBP 214 million of revenue in FY2024. Danone SA agreed to acquire Huel in March 2026 in a deal reported at roughly EUR 1 billion / USD 1.1 billion. Huel is a direct-to-consumer commerce and subscription business, not an API provider: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract. Its storefront runs as a Next.js application on Vercel in front of a Shopify commerce backend; the only anonymously callable machine-readable surface observed on a Huel-controlled host is the standard Discourse platform REST API served by its North American customer community at discourse.huel.com.

providers.name: Koda Health
providers.description: Koda Health is a Houston-based digital health company whose AI-enhanced patient decision support platform digitizes serious illness planning for health systems, health plans, and value-based care organizations. Its two solutions — Advance Care Planning (ACP) and Kidney Action Planning (KAP) for chronic kidney disease — walk patients through video-guided, interactive goals-of-care conversations and produce legally compliant advance directives, medical power of attorney, and POLST/DNR documents with digital signing and notarization across all 50 states. Completed plans are pushed into the provider's EMR through an integration Koda states meets HL7 FHIR standards, and can be shared with care teams, payors, and family. KodaCares adds human Patient Advocates for complex cases. Koda publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; its API host (api.kodahealthcare.com) is a closed backend serving the app, and EMR interoperability is delivered through partner and health-system integrations rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Medigate
providers.description: Medigate was a healthcare IoT / connected-medical-device cybersecurity company (headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, backed by Partech and others) that built the first security platform dedicated to healthcare IoT — device discovery, risk assessment, and clinically-aware network segmentation for hospitals. Claroty completed its acquisition of Medigate on 2022-01-10 and folded the product into "Claroty xDome for Healthcare"; the standalone brand is retired and medigate.io now redirects to claroty.com. A residual customer-facing REST API remains live at api.medigate.io (with a password-gated interactive reference at api.medigate.io/docs) that integrations use to pull device inventory, device groups, and device risk scores.

providers.name: CarMD
providers.description: CarMD specializes in automotive diagnostics and insights. The CarMD vehicle API is a user-centric and affordable way to access API services for your vehicle. The vehicle data API provides a wide range of services, from displaying code definitions and vehicle images to predicting upcoming issues.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Quartet Health
providers.description: Quartet Health is a value-based behavioral healthcare enablement and delivery platform that identifies, engages, and connects patients with mental health services across 39 states. It serves health plans, health systems, and community mental health centers with care coordination, patient-to-provider matching, and direct delivery of behavioral health care through its own medical group, focused on whole-person care for individuals with serious mental illness and other behavioral health needs. Quartet was acquired by NeuroFlow. Added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile; the public site exposes no developer or API surface, but does publish a substantive security and compliance program.

providers.name: AiVF
providers.description: AIVF develops AI-powered software for in vitro fertilization (IVF) clinics, embryology laboratories, and patients. Its EMA platform applies computer vision and machine learning to embryo evaluation (AIVF Day-3 and Day-5), genetics, outcomes analytics, and clinic-patient communication to improve embryo selection and IVF success rates, alongside ART Compass by AIVF for fertility-lab benchmarking. AIVF holds a CE mark and names ISO 27001, ISO 27799, ISO 13485, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance; in the US an AI component is an investigational device. AIVF was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API — this profile captures the company's identity, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Clara 2
providers.description: Clara is an AI-powered primary care and longevity practice, founded by the team behind Circle Medical and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and A.Capital. Clara pairs deep clinical AI with board-certified clinician review: it securely imports and analyzes a patient's medical records, surfaces health trends, assists with symptom assessment, medication refills, lab ordering, and longevity/biomarker goals, and routes every medical recommendation to a licensed clinician for review and approval before it reaches the patient. The company operates as a fully licensed primary care practice across all 50 U.S. states and is a HIPAA-covered entity. Clara is a consumer telehealth product (subscription plans on askclara.com) and currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity, trust, and compliance surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Disclo
providers.description: Disclo is a workplace-accommodations software platform that powers end-to-end management of ADA, FMLA, and state-leave requests, medical-certification verification, and the interactive accommodation process for employers. The HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant portal automates accommodation workflows and compliance documentation, adds AI-assisted medical-certification review (Disclo Verify) and candidate accommodations for recruiting (Disclo Hire), and integrates with 50+ HRIS and ATS systems. Disclo is a private B2B SaaS company backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst; it operates a secure customer portal (secure.disclo.com) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. Access is enterprise, demo/sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Mabel
providers.description: Mabel is a healthcare technology company (Irvine, California; backed by 500 Global) that helps Medicare accountable care organizations (ACOs) enroll and engage beneficiaries. Its platform is a market leader in voluntary alignment, used by roughly one in three ACOs, and spans four core solutions: Voluntary Alignment (campaign execution, response processing, analytics, and compliance auditing for LEAD, ACO REACH, and GUIDE programs), Health Surveys (social determinants of health screenings, NPS, and custom surveys with CMS-formatted reporting), Beneficiary Notifications (compliance notices via email, mail, or SMS with audit-ready tracking), and Letters From Your Doctor (provider-based outreach for enrollment, surveys, and appointments). Mabel is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. No public developer API or SDK surface is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, compliance posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Nilo Health
providers.description: Nilo Health (nilo.health) is a Berlin-based employee mental health platform that helps businesses support their workforce's mental well-being. Founded in 2019 by Ines Raeth, Catalina Turlea and Jonas Keil, nilo gives teams access to 500+ psychologists for 1:1 video counseling in 50+ languages, alongside self-guided digital programs, group roundtables, and an HR analytics dashboard. It is delivered to employers as a company benefit (SaaS) rather than through a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. nilo integrates with HR platforms such as Personio and Lano via partner marketplaces, and publishes a trust center citing ISO/IEC 27001. The company is backed by Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio company.

providers.name: Rivet Health
providers.description: Rivet Health is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for healthcare providers, spanning practices, specialty groups, and hospitals. Its software brings together three core modules: Revenue Diagnostics (AI-driven revenue forecasting, real-time reporting, and denial prevention), Payer Performance (contract management, payer benchmarking, and fee-schedule administration), and Patient Pricing (automated patient cost estimates and No Surprises Act Good Faith Estimates). Rivet describes itself as an agnostic platform that integrates with 30+ practice-management systems, EHRs, and clearinghouses — including Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, Veradigm, ModMed, Greenway Health, Nextech, Availity, and Change Healthcare. The company is backed by Menlo Ventures. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation; integrations are delivered through its partner network. Rivet publishes a trust center documenting SOC 2 and HIPAA posture.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Agilemd
providers.description: AgileMD is a clinical decision support company that embeds real-time predictive analytics and evidence-based clinical pathways directly into hospital electronic health record (EHR) workflows such as Epic and Cerner. Its FDA-cleared eCART Clinical Deterioration Suite continuously scores patient risk from nearly 100 real-time variables — labs, vital signs, and nursing assessments — to help care teams recognize deteriorating patients earlier, while its Clinical Pathways product standardizes evidence-based order sets, documentation, and protocols across care settings. AgileMD is used across 400+ hospitals by more than 150,000 clinical users and has processed millions of patient encounters. The company is backed by Y Combinator, MATTER, and Rock Health.

providers.name: Aidoc
providers.description: Aidoc is a clinical artificial intelligence company whose aiOS platform runs, orchestrates, and governs FDA-cleared clinical AI across health systems. Its modules span radiology, cardiology, neurovascular, and vascular care — detecting acute findings (stroke, pulmonary embolism, brain aneurysm, incidental findings) and coordinating care teams at the point of care. aiOS is a vendor-neutral platform that runs both Aidoc and third-party algorithms and integrates into existing hospital IT stacks (PACS, EHR, mobile) using standard healthcare interoperability protocols (DICOM, HL7, FHIR) rather than a public developer REST API. Aidoc reports adoption across more than 1,600 medical centers worldwide. Surfaced as a general-catalyst portfolio company and enriched here for security posture, interoperability conformance, and identity; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: Anthem
providers.description: Anthem, Inc. (now operating as Elevance Health) is one of the largest health benefits companies in the United States, serving members through affiliated Blue Cross and Blue Shield health plans across multiple states including California, New York, Virginia, Georgia, and others. Anthem provides health insurance, pharmacy benefits, and behavioral health services to over 40 million members. Under CMS interoperability rules (CMS-9115-F), Anthem offers FHIR- based Patient Access and Provider Directory APIs.

providers.name: Curebase
providers.description: Curebase is a San Francisco-based clinical trials technology company (founded 2017) that provides a modern, AI-native eClinical platform for sponsors, CROs, biotechs, MedTech companies, and research sites. The platform unifies the full trial lifecycle in one system: ePRO/eCOA (electronic patient-reported and clinical outcome assessments), eConsent (digital informed consent), EDC (electronic data capture), patient recruitment and screening, participant engagement and retention tooling, and site management. Curebase also ships Sitebase, a free eClinical suite for research sites, and Hope, a conversational AI voice agent. It supports decentralized and hybrid trial models natively. Curebase is a private, venture-backed company (Series B led by Industry Ventures; investors include GGV Capital, Acrew, Gilead, and others). It is SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant. Curebase does not publish a public developer API or API documentation; integration is handled through enterprise engagements.

providers.name: Force Therapeutics
providers.description: Force Therapeutics is a healthcare technology company providing a digital patient-engagement and remote-monitoring platform for surgical and musculoskeletal care. The platform delivers personalized patient education, automated collection of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs), preoperative optimization, postoperative recovery management, direct patient messaging, and actionable clinical insights for hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and private practices. Force integrates with major EHR systems (Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, NextGen) through the Redox Connection Network and FHIR/HL7-based workflows rather than a public developer API. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant, hosted on Amazon Web Services, and backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Lighten
providers.description: Lighten Platforms, Inc. is a San Mateo, California healthcare AI company building an AI-native platform for clinical evidence curation from electronic health record (EHR) data. Its 360° EHR Curation Platform reasons over unstructured clinical notes together with structured records to reconstruct complete patient journeys, applying clinically validated quality assurance at the variable, patient, and cohort level rather than relying on model accuracy metrics alone. On top of that curation layer Lighten delivers Apps & Insights for patient finding and HCP targeting, longitudinal patient journeys, and market intelligence, plus a "Beyond Claims" offering that integrates curated EHR signal with claims data for broader coverage. The company serves life sciences, health systems, data and analytics consultancies, and investors, and was founded by Xinkun Nie, PhD. Lighten publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: Lively
providers.description: Lively is a fintech-healthtech company that provides modern, cloud-based Health Savings Accounts (HSA) alongside Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA), COBRA, and commuter benefits for individuals, families, employers, benefits administrators, and third-party administrators. Lively pairs interest-bearing and investment-enabled HSAs (via a Schwab Health Savings Brokerage Account and a guided HSA portfolio) with an employer dashboard for contributions and administration, positioning itself around transparent, zero-hidden-fee pricing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures and GGV Capital, Lively integrates with benefit administration platforms and third-party administrators but does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through its sales and partnerships channels. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Lively's public web surface.

providers.name: MeetAsh
providers.description: Ash (MeetAsh / Ash Wellness) is a New York-based health technology company, founded in 2019, that powers white-label at-home health testing programs for health plans, digital health companies, and public health organizations. Through a single, developer-friendly REST API integration, partners can trigger test kits, manage shipping logistics, and securely transmit results back into an EHR or patient portal across a national network of CLIA- and CAP-certified laboratories. Ash offers 120+ at-home diagnostic panels (hormone, cancer, allergy, STI, chronic condition, and infectious-disease testing with self-collected blood, stool, urine, saliva, and swab samples), care-gap-closure programs for HEDIS measures, kitting and fulfillment, physician-of-record services, and real-time reporting dashboards. The platform is fully HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, with enterprise-grade encryption protecting PHI. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network; the developer documentation is partner-gated (password protected).

providers.name: Glass Health
providers.description: Glass Health is a San Francisco-based clinical AI company founded in 2021 by Dereck Paul (CEO) and Graham Ramsey (Head of Product) that builds an AI clinical decision support (CDS) and ambient scribing co-pilot for physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, residents, and medical students. The Glass platform combines large language model reasoning with curated, physician-reviewed clinical guidelines to generate ranked differential diagnoses, evidence-based assessment and plans, chart summaries, and direct answers to clinical questions ("Consult"), all delivered with inline citations. Glass also provides ambient scribing that listens during patient encounters and generates History and Physical notes, progress notes, discharge summaries, and patient-facing instructions, plus EHR integration via SMART on FHIR to pull demographics, problem lists, medications, laboratory values, vital signs, imaging, and encounter data into the workflow. Glass offers a tiered SaaS plan (Lite free tier, Starter at $20/month, Pro at $90/month, Max at $200/month) along with iOS and Android apps, and a public Glass Developer API ($250/month minimum, token-metered beyond the floor) that exposes the same clinical AI agent — Consult, Differential Diagnosis, Assessment and Plan, and Scribing endpoints — for third-party healthcare products. Glass is backed by Breyer Capital and graduated from Y Combinator's W23 batch, with roughly $6.5M in total disclosed funding. The provider does not publish an open OpenAPI specification or open-source SDKs; integration details are gated behind the developer portal and an enterprise contact at enterprise@glass.health.

providers.name: RealWear
providers.description: RealWear builds rugged, hands-free head-mounted and assisted-reality wearable computers (the Navigator series and HMT-1) for frontline and industrial workers in energy, manufacturing, field service, and utilities. Its Android-based devices are operated entirely by voice through the on-device WearHF service, which turns any Android app's touch controls into voice commands and can be tuned with WearML voice directives placed in UI metadata — so there is no separate SDK to install. RealWear now also ships Ari, a voice-first AI assistant (Ari OS and the Ari Cloud dashboard) with Microsoft connectors (Teams, Outlook email and calendar, contacts, Copilot), skills, and cross-session memory. Developers extend the platform with native Android, Unity, React Native, Cordova, Xamarin, and HTML apps plus custom Ari skills. This profile was surfaced as a Foundry Group portfolio company and enriched from RealWear's public developer surface.

providers.name: Boat Lifestyle
providers.description: boAt (legal entity Imagine Marketing Limited) is an India-based consumer electronics brand founded in 2016 by Aman Gupta and Sameer Mehta, selling wireless earbuds, headphones, smartwatches, home audio and mobile accessories. Its direct-to-consumer storefront at boat-lifestyle.com runs on Shopify and exposes a real, anonymous agent commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP 2026-04-08) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a live MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp serving 13 catalog, cart, checkout and order tools over JSON-RPC, published agent instructions at /agents.md and /llms.txt, and Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect discovery. There is no first-party developer program, no OpenAPI, and no partner API portal — the machine-readable contract is the MCP tools/list manifest, which is platform-provided by Shopify rather than authored by boAt.

providers.name: Carecloud
providers.description: CareCloud (NASDAQ: CCLD, formerly MTBC) is a cloud-based healthcare technology company serving 45,000+ providers with an integrated platform spanning electronic health records (EHR), practice management, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient experience tools, and AI-driven clinical documentation (cirrusAI). Its Connector product delivers healthcare interoperability with FHIR and C-CDA data exchange across labs, EHRs, immunization registries, and diagnostics. CareCloud is Drummond-certified ONC Health IT and Surescripts-certified, publishes HIPAA compliance content, and operates a developer portal (AWS API Gateway) at developer.carecloud.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Change Healthcare
providers.description: Change Healthcare was one of the largest healthcare technology and clearinghouse companies in the United States, moving eligibility, claim, remittance and prior-authorization transactions between providers and payers over X12 EDI. UnitedHealth Group acquired it in October 2022 and folded it into Optum, and the brand has since been retired: www.changehealthcare.com redirects to business.optum.com, developers.changehealthcare.com redirects path-for-path to developer.optum.com, and the apis.changehealthcare.com API gateway is decommissioned and documented by Optum as "an old domain and no longer supported". The Change Healthcare Medical Network APIs — Eligibility v3, Professional Claims v3, Institutional Claims v1, Claim Status v2, Claims Responses and Reports v2, Attachments, PayerList v1 and Prior Authorization v1 — are still operated and documented, but on Optum infrastructure and under Optum hosts.

providers.name: Sword
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital health company delivering AI-powered virtual care for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain, pelvic health, and injury prevention. Founded in 2015 in Portugal by Virgilio Bento, Sword pairs licensed physical therapists with motion-sensor and computer-vision technology so members can complete clinically supervised physical therapy from home. Its platform spans an enrollment platform, a treatment platform, a mobile application backed by a mobile API, a file-exchange platform for enterprise clients, and an AI care system. Sword serves 1,000+ enterprise and health-plan clients across three continents, is backed by investors including General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, and Transformation Capital, and maintains SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 13485, HIPAA, GDPR, and Cyber Essentials compliance. Sword does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its identity, status, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: House Rx
providers.description: House Rx is a healthcare technology company that equips independent specialty and community clinics to run in-house, medically integrated dispensing pharmacies. Founded in 2021, its cloud platform — built by specialty pharmacists and physicians — supports the full specialty-medication workflow: prior authorization, financial counseling and copay assistance, fulfillment tools, scalable patient outreach and messaging, real-time operational analytics, and EHR integration so physicians and pharmacists collaborate on patient care. House Rx is SOC 2 compliant and backed by First Round, Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Maverick Ventures, 1984 Ventures, and Character Ventures. House Rx does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Unmind
providers.description: Unmind is a workplace mental health platform that supports employees, develops leaders, and strengthens organisational performance through therapy, coaching, manager training, crisis care, an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), wellbeing content, insights and assessments, and Nova, an AI wellbeing coach. Customers include Uber, MLB, Samsung, British Airways, Diageo, and the NHS. Unmind publishes no public developer API; api.unmind.com is a private Apollo GraphQL backend serving its own apps.

providers.name: KRY
providers.description: KRY is a Swedish digital healthcare provider headquartered in Stockholm that operates internationally under the Livi brand. It delivers primary care through video and chat consultations with doctors, nurses, psychologists, physiotherapists, dietitians and midwives via its iOS and Android apps, and also runs physical primary care centres (vardcentraler), child health clinics and midwifery clinics across Sweden. KRY operates as Kry in Sweden (kry.se) and Norway (kry.no) and as Livi in the United Kingdom (livi.co.uk) and France (livi.fr). Services span digital consultations, prescription renewal, medical certificates, vaccination and testing, mental health programmes, occupational health for employers, and regional public healthcare contracts. KRY publishes no public developer program, partner API or SDK surface; the platform is consumer- and clinician-facing, so this profile captures the company identity plus its legal and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: Tendo
providers.description: Tendo is a healthcare software company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith (previously of Veeva Systems and Instructure) and headquartered in the Philadelphia area. Tendo builds a cloud, purpose-built healthcare platform and a suite of applications that connect patients, clinicians, providers, and caregivers across the care journey — spanning digital patient engagement, quality and clinical documentation improvement, hospital quality rankings analytics, and the Care Connect marketplace for employers, providers, and patients. The company raised a $50M Series B led by Lux Capital (with General Catalyst). Tendo runs public trust and status surfaces (a SafeBase trust center with SOC 2 and HIPAA, an Atlassian Statuspage) but does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI; API integration is delivered under private partner agreements. Surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TransCrypts
providers.description: TransCrypts is a blockchain-based identity and credential verification platform that lets individuals own, encrypt, and share verified records — employment and income history, background checks, and (with HIPAA certification) health and education credentials — directly with employers, background checkers, and other verifiers. Encrypted data is stored off-chain while cryptographic hashes are anchored on-chain, so users can prove authenticity without exposing personal data. The company reports 5M+ verifications across 4M+ users and 450+ enterprise clients, and connects to HR and payroll systems such as ADP, BambooHR, and Namely. It raised a $15M seed round led by Pantera Capital, with Techstars, Lightspeed Faction, Alpha Edison, Motley Fool Ventures, Mark Cuban, and Protocol Labs participating.

providers.name: AccessHope
providers.description: AccessHope is a Los Angeles-area health benefits company, founded in 2019 and wholly owned by City of Hope, that delivers remote cancer expertise as an employer-sponsored benefit. Its subspecialist teams review a member's pathology, imaging, molecular testing and treatment plan against the latest evidence from a coalition of National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers — City of Hope, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Emory Winship, Fred Hutch, Johns Hopkins Kimmel, Northwestern Medicine Lurie, and UT Southwestern Simmons — and return guidance to the member's own local oncologist rather than moving the patient. AccessHope reports roughly 9 million covered members across 700+ employer and health-plan clients, including 70+ Fortune 500 companies. Delivery is business-to-business: employers, benefits consultants, health plans and navigation partners onboard through an eligibility file feed and an implementation-managed workflow, while members and clinical staff use credentialed web portals. AccessHope publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Ellipsis Health
providers.description: Ellipsis Health is a healthcare AI company that has established the human voice as a vital sign for mental health, using clinically validated vocal-biomarker technology, natural language processing, and acoustic models to identify, measure, and monitor the severity of depression and anxiety from short samples of natural speech. Its flagship product, Sage, is an emotionally intelligent, agentic AI care manager that conducts 24/7 patient-engagement calls for health plans, health systems, specialty care, and pharma, handling program enrollment, benefits verification, clinical assessments and surveys, and care coordination. Sage is powered by Ellipsis' patented Empathy Engine, trained on millions of live clinical patient calls, and runs on HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant infrastructure. Ellipsis Health integrates with health plans and systems such as Cigna, and exposes a private partner API (used by partners like Augmedix) rather than a public developer platform. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and CVS Health Ventures.

providers.name: Nolla Health
providers.description: Nolla Health is a Norway-born, AI-powered telehealth and dermatology company that entered the U.S. market with a $4.5M seed round led by General Catalyst and set up its headquarters in New York City. After treating more than 50,000 patients in Europe and becoming one of Norway's top-five medical apps, Nolla launched an AI-guided skin and acne care platform across 40+ U.S. states. The service pairs proprietary AI symptom assessment with clinician-in-the-loop oversight: patients complete a guided chat, a licensed U.S. medical provider reviews and approves every diagnosis and prescription, and topical medications are shipped directly to the patient. Nolla operates as a consumer-facing product (per-consultation and a monthly subscription) rather than an API provider, and publicly states HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

providers.name: Omni Network
providers.description: Omni Network is a crypto interoperability protocol that makes the entire multi-chain ecosystem feel like a single chain for users and developers. Its core product, SolverNet, is a network of solvers that fulfill cross-chain intents on a user's behalf, letting a dApp deployed on one chain be used by people whose funds live on another. Developers integrate SolverNet through the Omni SDK (the @omni-network/core and @omni-network/react TypeScript packages) to bridge, swap, deposit, and bundle arbitrary contract calls across any supported chain from a single frontend. The project is built on a Go/Cosmos-SDK monorepo with Solidity contracts and ships the OMNI ERC-20 token on Ethereum L1. In 2026 the company rebranded from Omni to Nomina, consolidated on Ethereum, and now also operates Nomina, a unified trading terminal for power users trading perpetual futures across decentralized exchanges. It is backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, Two Sigma, Spartan Group, and Vessel.

providers.name: Ritten
providers.description: Ritten is a cloud-based electronic medical record (EMR), CRM and revenue-cycle platform built specifically for behavioral health and substance-use treatment organizations - detox, residential, PHP/IOP, and outpatient providers. Its browser-based product covers clinical documentation (group and individual notes, AI-assisted charting), scheduling, revenue-cycle management (claims, billing, authorizations), a HIPAA-compliant patient portal, treatment planning, compliance tooling (audit trails, signature routing), and outcomes reporting. Ritten publishes a public REST contract for integrating partners - the Ritten External API - documented with an OpenAPI 3.1.0 definition covering 56 paths, 71 operations and 93 schemas across patients, contacts, CRM cases, programs, facilities, organizations, tasks, encounters, forms, insurance payers, users and a 17-operation insights and reporting family, plus six webhook events. Authentication is OAuth 2.0 client_credentials with a required X-Ritten-Tenant header selecting the clinic instance; credentials are provisioned by Ritten to partners rather than self-service. Ritten is built for HIPAA-regulated and 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality requirements with role-based access controls and audit logs, and supports operational integrations for e-prescribing, labs, eligibility/billing clearinghouses, and telehealth. Backed by 8VC and Threshold Ventures; based in Philadelphia, PA.

providers.name: Simpatico Project
providers.description: Simpatico Project (유쾌한프로젝트, Yukwaehan Project Co., Ltd.) is a Korean B2B mental-wellness startup, backed by 500 Global, whose product Clify (클라이피, "Climb & Clarify") is an AI-based integrated mental-care and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) solution for individuals and companies. Clify uses a patented multimodal algorithm to fuse Face & Voice biosignals — blood-flow changes, micro-expressions and voice characteristics — into a roughly one-minute mental-state diagnosis (stress, anxiety, depression, burnout) that it claims exceeds 90% accuracy, and rolls the results up into an organization insight dashboard for HR (company-wide mental trends, high/low-risk teams, usage). Personal mental data is processed on-device and de-identified so it is never shared with the employer, and the company states it holds ISO 27001. Product surfaces include FAV (the Face & Voice AI diagnosis engine), an EAP counseling center, and the Clify organization-insight analytics. The public presence (clify.co.kr, an imweb-built marketing and account site) exposes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Abridge
providers.description: Abridge provides enterprise-grade generative AI for clinical conversations, transforming patient-clinician interactions into contextually aware, clinically useful, and billable AI-generated notes. Its Contextual Reasoning Engine powers ambient documentation embedded directly in the Epic EHR (Abridge Inside), with deployments across more than 100 health systems including Mayo Clinic, UPMC, Kaiser Permanente, Johns Hopkins, and Duke Health. Abridge reaches third-party developers and EHR partners through Epic's Partners and Pals program rather than a public, self-service developer API.

providers.name: Attuned Intelligence
providers.description: Attuned Intelligence is a healthcare voice AI company that automates hospital and community health center call centers with supervised, EHR-integrated Voice AI Agents. Its agents answer every patient call instantly and in the caller's language, resolve needs end-to-end (appointment booking, medication refills, triage routing), and provide real-time human oversight with transcripts and reporting so automation stays safe and auditable. Founded in 2024 by leaders from DeepMind, Google Health, AssemblyAI, and DocuSign, the company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $13M in funding backed by Threshold Ventures, and serves customers including Cambridge Health Alliance and Lowell Community Health Center. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. Attuned publishes no first-party developer/product API; its Wix-hosted marketing site exposes a generic hosted Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content and business details.

providers.name: CaaMTech
providers.description: CaaMTech is a pharmaceutical drug discovery company in Issaquah, Washington, founded by Dr. Andrew Chadeayne, engineering next-generation psychedelic-inspired small-molecule therapeutics for mental health conditions. It synthesizes and characterizes novel tryptamines, screens natural and synthetic compounds for safety and efficacy, publishes fundamental crystallographic and pharmacological research, and builds a patent portfolio around the results. CaaMTech operates no developer program and publishes no product API; the only machine-readable surface on caam.tech is the standard WordPress REST API that serves the company site, which does make its research updates, pages and media programmatically readable without credentials, alongside an authenticated WordPress MCP adapter endpoint.

providers.name: EDDA Technology
providers.description: EDDA Technology, Inc. is a Princeton, New Jersey medical imaging software company behind the IQQA platform for computer-assisted radiology and surgery. IQQA delivers 3D quantitative image analysis, automated segmentation and volumetric measurement over CT and MR studies, supporting pre-surgical planning and simulation, intra-operative guidance and monitoring, post-operative follow-up evaluation, and clinical training across liver, lung, kidney and interventional oncology. Products include IQQA-BodyImaging, IQQA-Guide, IQQA-Chest, IQQA-Liver, IQQA-Liver Function, IQQA-eQMR and the IQQA-eFusion edge-AI surgical navigation system. The company is FDA cleared and CE marked under EU MDR 2017/745, and raised a US$150 million round led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 with OrbiMed participation in April 2021. EDDA publishes no developer API for IQQA — it is regulated medical device software deployed on-premises in hospitals — so the only public API surface catalogued here is the WordPress REST API serving eddatech.com content.

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: Patientdesk.ai
providers.description: Patientdesk.ai (Patientdesk AI, Inc.) is a California-based, Y Combinator-backed company building an AI-native operating system for dental practices. Its 24/7 AI phone receptionist handles inbound and outbound patient calls, appointment scheduling, real-time insurance verification during the call, automated payment collection and debt follow-up, intake, reminders, and lead generation. The product integrates directly with major dental practice management systems (Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, Curve Dental, and others) to book patients straight into a clinic's calendar. Patientdesk.ai is HIPAA compliant, follows SOC 2 security standards, supports multiple languages, and is offered on month-to-month contracts. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer/API surface (OpenAPI, docs, SDKs) is currently published; the company exposes a marketing site and a provider-authored llms.txt.

providers.name: 23andMe
providers.description: 23andMe is a consumer genetics company founded in 2006 that sells saliva-based DNA test kits and returns ancestry composition across 4,500+ regions, DNA relative matching, FDA-cleared genetic health predisposition and carrier-status reports, pharmacogenetics, polygenic risk scores, wellness and trait insights, plus a Total Health tier adding exome sequencing, biannual blood testing and genetics-informed telehealth. It is now operated by the 23andMe Research Institute, a non-profit, following the company's 2025 Chapter 11 bankruptcy; the canonical consumer domain migrated from 23andme.com to 23andme.org, which serves the company's llms.txt, trust center and shop. 23andMe published a scope-gated OAuth 2.0 Personal Genome API at api.23andme.com but closed general third-party developer access in September 2018. It still markets API and raw-data integration through the 23andMe Marketplace as a partner arrangement, though no machine-readable contract, API reference, pricing or rate limits are published publicly, and the developer portal host answers a Cloudflare bot challenge to anonymous requests.

providers.name: Carepatron
providers.description: Carepatron is a cloud-based healthcare practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, health coaches, nutritionists, and other practitioners. It brings client records, appointment scheduling and online booking, telehealth, AI-assisted clinical notes and documentation, and billing/invoicing with insurance claims into one workspace, and markets HIPAA/SOC/GDPR compliance across 100,000+ clinicians in 120+ countries. As of this review Carepatron does NOT publish a documented public developer API - its pricing page lists "API (coming soon)" on the Advanced plan, and there is no developer portal, API reference, published base URL, OpenAPI definition, or SDK. Third-party connectivity today is limited to a handful of native integrations (Zoom, accounting software, Google Tag Manager). The APIs listed below are logical/product-area groupings modeled from Carepatron's own feature set; their endpoints are NOT documented and are marked as modeled, not confirmed.

providers.name: Cognoa
providers.description: Cognoa is a pediatric behavioral health company in Palo Alto, California building digital diagnostics and therapeutics for early childhood development, starting with autism. Its flagship product, Canvas Dx, is an FDA-authorized Software as a Medical Device that aids clinicians in diagnosing or ruling out autism spectrum disorder in children aged 18 to 72 months, combining a caregiver questionnaire, short home videos scored by credentialed human video analysts, and a healthcare-provider questionnaire into a machine-learning classifier that returns Positive, Negative, or Indeterminate. Canvas Dx is delivered as an iOS/Android caregiver app plus a prescriber web portal at app.cognoa.com; Cognoa ships no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Equip Health
providers.description: Equip Health is a virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment provider founded in 2019 by Kristina Saffran and Erin Parks. Equip delivers 100% remote, insurance-covered care for all eating disorder diagnoses — anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder (BED), ARFID, atypical anorexia, and OSFED — using Family-Based Treatment (FBT) and other evidence-based approaches. Every patient is matched with a five-person care team: a therapist, medical provider, dietitian, family mentor, and peer mentor. Equip serves patients across the United States with no waitlist, publishes an extensive library of clinical and recovery articles, partners with providers and health plans, and operates a patient portal at my.equip.health. This profile catalogs Equip's public web, legal, security, and content surfaces; Equip publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program at this time.

providers.name: ExaCare AI
providers.description: ExaCare AI is a post-acute and senior care operations platform that applies AI to admissions, referral management, prior authorization, and reimbursement workflows across skilled nursing, home health, hospice, and assisted living providers. It reads inbound referral and admissions packets, extracts clinical and payer data, and automates the back-office work of accepting and reimbursing patients, with integrations into referral platforms, hospital systems, and EHRs. ExaCare is a private company backed by Insight Partners; it ships a customer web application and a Vanta-hosted Trust Center (HIPAA) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Findoctave
providers.description: Findoctave (operating as Octave) is a mental health care provider offering virtual and in-person therapy across 20+ U.S. states. Services include individual, couples, and family therapy, DBT, and specialized centers of excellence for perinatal and postpartum health, LGBTQIA+ (queer resiliency), trauma, and women's emotional health. Octave is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Shield of California, BCBS plans, Health Net, and others) and publishes a therapist directory, cost calculator, and getting-started flow through its consumer website. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; Octave exposes no public developer API, so this profile is a company identity record rather than an API listing.

providers.name: HealthVerity
providers.description: HealthVerity is a United States life-sciences data platform, headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, that operates what it describes as the nation's largest real-world data (RWD) ecosystem - more than 150 billion de-identified transactions covering over 330 million U.S. patients across 75-plus data sources spanning medical and pharmacy claims, labs, and EHR (following its integration of Symphony Health). Its products are organized around the IPGE framework (Identity, Privacy, Governance, Exchange) and include HealthVerity Marketplace (verified RWD datasets), Identity Manager and Census (privacy-safe probabilistic identity resolution that replaces PII with a universal HealthVerity ID / HVID), Governance Manager, HealthVerity FLOW, and eXOs (an AI-native real-world-evidence agent). HealthVerity is a HIPAA-aligned, tokenization-and-de-identification company serving pharma, payers, and government - not a self-serve, standards-based clinical interoperability vendor. Unlike EHR and FHIR-network players, it exposes no public developer portal, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, and no downloadable OpenAPI; the only vendor-named programmatic surface is the gated, enterprise HealthVerity Identity API for real-time de-identification, described conceptually on the Identity Manager product page but without public reference documentation, base URL, or self-serve onboarding.

providers.name: 9am Health
providers.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: BoaConsulta
providers.description: BoaConsulta is a Brazilian digital-health platform, founded in 2012 and part of the Pixeon healthtech group, that connects patients, health professionals, and institutions. It pairs a free B2C marketplace for booking in-person consultations, teleconsultations, exams, and vaccinations with a full B2B/SaaS practice-management system (150+ integrated modules covering smart scheduling, electronic health records, telemedicine, financial management, TISS insurance billing, inventory, and automated reminders). The platform reports more than 58,000 health professionals, 1.7 million registered patients, and over 2 million appointments, with LGPD-compliant end-to-end encryption and daily automated backups. It has no public developer API; this profile is enriched from BoaConsulta's own public surfaces (llms.txt, status page, help center, blog, and legal pages).

providers.name: Latent
providers.description: Latent (Latent Health) is an enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform for health systems, built around a clinical agentic engine that reads the chart, reasons over payer policy and drug labels, and acts inside the electronic health record. The platform spans four modules — Identify (care-gap identification, eligibility screening, site-of-care routing), Access (prior authorization, clinical review, appeals generation, benefit routing, payer outreach), Capture (340B eligibility auditing, leakage analytics, financial dashboards), and Engage (patient outreach, queue management, outcomes analytics). Latent is chart-native and EHR agnostic, integrating with Epic, Cerner and others, and is used by more than 45 health systems including Ochsner Health, MetroHealth, Yale New Haven Health, St. Luke's Health System and Henry Ford Health, serving over two million patients annually. Founded by Sriram Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, the company has raised $80M from Spark Capital, Transformation Capital, McKesson Ventures, Conviction, General Catalyst and Y Combinator. Latent publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its integration surface is delivered through EHR-native deployment with health-system customers, and its security posture is published on a Vanta-hosted trust center with HIPAA-compliant data handling.

providers.name: Sword Health
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital musculoskeletal (MSK) and virtual physical-therapy company that pairs licensed clinicians with an AI Care platform (programs including Thrive for MSK, Bloom for pelvic and women's health, Move, and Mind for mental health, with the Phoenix AI care specialist and the Sword Intelligence division). Founded in Portugal in 2015, it sells to employers, health plans, and governments rather than to individual developers. As of this enrichment pass Sword Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its digital surface is member/clinician apps and employer client portals. Real public surfaces captured here are its trust center (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR), legal pages, newsroom, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
providers.description: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a global pharmacy-led health and wellbeing enterprise operating in more than 25 countries, with pharmacy chains Walgreens in the US and Boots in the UK, pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution through Alliance Healthcare, and specialty pharmacy operations. WBA operates as a Fortune 100 company and global healthcare platform, leveraging data science, AI, and digital health technologies to serve patients, customers, and health systems. While WBA's primary developer APIs are offered through the Walgreens Developer Program, the enterprise also uses healthcare data platforms for population health management, specialty pharmacy integration, and digital health services.

providers.name: Headway
providers.description: Headway operates a national mental-health care platform that connects patients, therapists and psychiatrists, and insurance companies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Headway builds the first asset-free national network of behavioral-health providers who accept insurance, handling insurance credentialing, claims management, payments, and scheduling for clinicians while letting patients search for in-network providers, book appointments online, and see costs up front. The company partners with 45+ major insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Oxford, UnitedHealthcare, Oscar) and, as of 2026, powers 600,000+ appointments per month across all 50 states. Headway is backed by a16z, Thrive, Accel, GV, Spark Capital, and Forerunner. It maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance. Headway does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Machinify
providers.description: Machinify is an AI-powered healthcare payment integrity platform that streamlines and automates payment processes for health plans. Its products - Coordinate (claims coordination), Subrogate (subrogation management), Audit (payment audit), Pay (payment processing), and Pharmacy (pharmacy payment integrity) - run on a unified data layer that combines claims and medical records, healthcare foundation models trained on billions of data points, and task-specific AI agents with continuous-improvement feedback loops. Machinify reports 85+ customers including 18 of the top 20 US health plans, coverage of 270 million member lives, and more than $6B in annual cost avoidance and recoveries. The company is backed by Battery Ventures and GV. Machinify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference.

providers.name: Dentsply Sirona
providers.description: Dentsply Sirona is the world's largest manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, providing comprehensive solutions for dentists, dental laboratories, and dental specialists worldwide. The company exposes developer integrations through DS Core, an open cloud platform, and through the Dentsply Sirona Imaging modality API for intraoral imaging hardware.

providers.name: Theator
providers.description: Theator is a surgical intelligence platform that turns minimally invasive surgical video into structured, actionable intelligence. The company processes operative video footage into procedural insights, outcomes data, and surgery-to-text documentation for three audiences: surgeons seeking objective performance feedback, hospital and health-system executives tracking outcomes and efficiency, and revenue-cycle teams improving documentation and coding. Theator is a healthcare technology company backed by Insight Partners and partners with AWS and Oracle Health. It maintains a formal security and compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) published via its trust center. No public first-party developer API, SDK, or documentation surface has been identified; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Viome
providers.description: Viome (Viome Life Sciences) is a health technology company founded in 2016 by Naveen Jain that uses metatranscriptomic RNA sequencing — a technique originally developed for biodefense at Los Alamos National Laboratory — combined with artificial intelligence to measure active gene expression across the gut microbiome, oral microbiome, and human cells. From at-home stool, saliva, and finger-prick blood samples the company produces over 50 health scores across eight categories (BioAge, Gut Health, Oral Health, Energy, Inflammaging, Mood/Memory/Focus, Immunity, and Heart and Metabolic Health), personalized food recommendations across more than 370 foods, and custom-blended precision supplements and biotics. Products include the Full Body Intelligence, Gut Intelligence, and Oral Health Intelligence tests plus the CancerDetect saliva screening test for oral and throat cancer. Viome operates in over 100 countries, publishes peer-reviewed research in NPJ Genomic Medicine, iScience, and Microbiome, and runs a Life Sciences research division. Viome publishes no public developer API or machine-readable API contract; its consumer app at my.viome.com is served by an undocumented private backend, and the only agent-facing artifact the company publishes is a curated llms.txt.

providers.name: Virgo
providers.description: Virgo builds AI foundation models for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, targeting gut-mediated diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. Its flagship model, EndoDINO, was trained on the largest known endoscopy dataset (130,037 videos / ~3.5 billion frames), and EndoML is the GI-specific tooling environment for building clinical and research workflows on top of it. Virgo Cloud provides video capture and management for endoscopy procedures, while Virgo Trials accelerates clinical trials with automatic data capture, endoscopic scoring, placebo-response prediction, subgroup identification, and AI biomarker discovery. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Basata
providers.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Bevel
providers.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Chefaa
providers.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

providers.name: Radial Analytics
providers.description: Radial Analytics (Radial) is a Concord, Massachusetts healthcare technology company providing an AI/ML-powered clinical decision-support platform for the value-based care market. Its HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified software helps ACOs, hospitals, health systems, payers, and Medicare Advantage plans account for millions of clinical, claims, and quality datapoints to improve patient outcomes while reducing cost of care. Products include Radial Care, ACO Compare, Opportunity Navigator, decision-support modules, care pathways, and TEAM bundles. The company was founded by MIT PhDs Thaddeus Fulford-Jones and Eric Weiss and is backed by Initialized Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: RapidClaims
providers.description: RapidClaims is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) company building autonomous AI agents for medical coding and claims. Its platform automates medical coding (RapidCode), value-based-care coding and risk adjustment (RapidVBC), denial management and revenue recovery (RapidRecovery), and a unified revenue cycle platform (RapidRCM) for FQHCs, community health centers, ACOs, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals, and management services organizations. The company emphasizes a healthcare-grade security and compliance posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, 256-bit encryption). RapidClaims is backed by Accel and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Artera
providers.description: Artera is a healthcare technology company providing an AI-powered patient communication and engagement platform used by hospitals, health systems, and medical practices to unify how they reach and care for patients. The platform orchestrates SMS, voice, email, and chat across the patient journey — appointment scheduling and reminders, patient intake, payments, referral management, care-gap closure, prescription refills, multilingual engagement, and after-hours call routing and triage — increasingly through agentic AI. Artera connects to the EHR and patient-facing vendors via API, FHIR, and HL7v2 integrations with major systems including Epic, Oracle Health, MEDITECH, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, Veradigm, NextGen, Greenway, ModMed, AdvancedMD, and Netsmart. The company maintains a strong security and compliance posture (SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, FedRAMP, HIPAA). It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Parachute Health
providers.description: Parachute Health is the leading digital platform for durable medical equipment (DME), home medical equipment, and medical supply ePrescribing. Clinicians eSign and submit DME orders in seconds, and the platform coordinates in real time across a network of 3,000+ supplier locations, 270,000+ eSigning clinicians, and 70,000+ facilities in all 50 states. Parachute integrates with EHR/EMR systems (athenahealth, PointClickCare, Epic, and others) using HL7 2.x and FHIR interfaces, and offers prior-authorization automation, health-plan workflows, and value-based-care coordination. Integration is delivered as private, partner-provisioned EMR/HL7/FHIR interfaces rather than a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Aware Health
providers.description: Aware Health is an AI-powered musculoskeletal (MSK) care platform that helps employers, health plans, and brokers reduce MSK spend while preventing orthopedic surgeries and chronic pain. The company pairs licensed clinicians (physical therapists and health coaches) with an AI "Predict" engine to triage, navigate, and manage musculoskeletal conditions virtually, and reports reducing MSK costs by roughly 30%. Its platform spans MSK care, chronic care, surgery decision support, member navigation, analytics, and an employer dashboard, delivered via web and an iOS app. Aware Health is a Techstars portfolio company and has raised seed funding (including a $3M round led by Boomerang VC with Bright Ventures). This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Aware Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Cleerly
providers.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Eden Health
providers.description: Eden Health was a primary and virtual care company that delivered app-based medical care, behavioral health, and care navigation to employers and their employees, integrating with health systems and insurers (backed by Insight Partners). It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public marketing site is no longer reachable over TLS, but its primary backend service — the "Grdn" (Guardian) API at api.edenhealth.com — still serves a Swagger 2.0 description covering patients, appointments, membership, documents, care teams, and clinician tooling.

providers.name: FirstVet
providers.description: FirstVet is a digital veterinary care company offering 24/7 online video consultations with licensed veterinarians for dogs, cats, and other pets. Founded in Sweden, FirstVet operates a consumer telehealth platform across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States, providing virtual vet appointments, healthy pet checkups, follow-up care, and triage guidance on whether a case needs an in-clinic referral. The company partners with pet insurers and employers to offer covered or subsidized access to its subscription-based virtual care. FirstVet is a portfolio company of Creandum. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; FirstVet publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Halo Health (Symplr)
providers.description: Halo Health, now part of symplr and marketed as symplr Clinical Communications, is a HIPAA-compliant clinical communication and collaboration platform for healthcare organizations. It provides role-based secure messaging, voice communication, critical alert and clinical-alarm notification, and on-call schedule management so care teams can coordinate around patients. The platform integrates with hospital EHR and clinical systems using healthcare interoperability standards - HL7 ADT for patient admit/discharge/transfer events, HL7 ORU for laboratory and radiology results, and SMTP for alerts such as sepsis notifications - rather than through a documented public developer REST API. symplr acquired Halo Health to extend its healthcare operations software portfolio, and the product now sits alongside symplr's broader workforce, compliance, and provider-data solutions.

providers.name: Hello Heart
providers.description: Hello Heart is a digital health company that combines a mobile app, connected blood-pressure monitors, a smart pill box, and the Nia AI assistant (trained on ACC/AHA guidelines) to help people proactively manage cardiovascular health. Sold primarily to employers, health plans, unions, and public-sector benefits programs as a covered heart-health benefit, the platform pairs self-monitoring with clinically-grounded, "safe AI" coaching to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiac risk.
