Hello Heart is HITRUST CSF certified, SOC 2 Type 2 audited, NIST CSF aligned, and HIPAA compliant, with data encrypted in transit and at rest and stored within U.S. borders. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture.

providers.name: Imagen
providers.description: Imagen (Imagen Technologies) is an AI-enabled, sub-specialized diagnostic imaging partner for independent practices, hospitals, and health systems. It combines in-clinic imaging equipment, FDA-cleared AI algorithms, and a 24/7 teleradiology network of fellowship-trained, board-certified specialists to deliver rapid, accurate radiology interpretations, plus advanced analytics for care-gap identification. Imagen operates across 23 states, serving roughly 3.5 million patients, and is backed by GV and Threshold Ventures. The company publishes a security program covering SOC 2 Type II, the HITRUST CSF, and HIPAA. Imagen Technologies exposes no public developer API surface at this time. (Note the distinct namesake company Imagen AI, imagen-ai.com, an AI photo-editing product that does publish an API and SDK.)

providers.name: Plume Health
providers.description: Plume Health (Plume) is a telehealth company delivering gender-affirming care to transgender and gender non-conforming people across the United States. Through a mobile app and licensed clinicians, Plume provides gender-affirming hormone therapy (estrogen and testosterone), mental health support, medical letters for surgery and identification changes, and everyday clinical care, all on a monthly membership subscription. Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, Plume operates as a HIPAA-covered, LegitScript-certified consumer healthcare provider. It is a consumer-facing care service and does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: QUIBIM
providers.description: QUIBIM is a healthcare AI company that unlocks medical imaging data to improve patient outcomes through quantitative imaging biomarkers and radiomics. Its cloud-based, tissue-agnostic platform ingests, harmonizes, and analyzes imaging data (MRI, CT, PET) to extract automated radiomics and deep-learning imaging biomarkers that support clinical decision-making and biopharma drug development. Regulated clinical products include QP-Prostate, QP-Brain, QP-Liver, QP-Breast, QP-Lung, and the QP-Insights multi-omics platform, several of which are CE and UKCA marked and integrate with hospital PACS systems. QUIBIM is ISO 27001:2022 certified and HIPAA and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; QUIBIM publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Sage Care
providers.description: Sage Care (sagecare.ai) builds an AI-native, HIPAA-compliant software platform made exclusively for home care agencies. Its product bundles an AI receptionist, a purpose-built CRM, an AI notetaker and a clinical scribe that automate the intake, referral, scheduling and documentation work that home care operators handle every day. Sage Care integrates with existing home care management systems such as WellSky and AxisCare rather than replacing them, and ships native iOS and desktop applications for caregivers and office staff. The company is backed by General Catalyst and surfaced through its portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Sage Care publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation — it is an application vendor rather than an API provider, so this profile captures company identity and security/compliance posture only.

providers.name: 98point6 Technologies
providers.description: 98point6 Technologies is a Seattle-based digital health software company, founded in 2015, that builds and licenses a cloud-based virtual care platform to health systems, payers and virtual care providers. After selling its own care-delivery division in 2023 it operates purely as a licensed software provider. The platform combines an AI-driven Automated Assistant for patient intake and visit documentation, a web-based Clinician Console with automated clinical decision support, and a white-labeled patient application, covering both asynchronous and real-time (messaging, audio, video) care. It advertises HL7 and FHIR based EMR integration with Epic and Cerner, SSO for patient login, and an SDK for building a fully branded patient experience, but that integration surface is delivered under a licensing agreement, so no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published publicly.

providers.name: Caresyntax
providers.description: Caresyntax is a surgical intelligence company that builds a vendor-neutral, enterprise-scale data platform for the operating room. Founded in 2013 in Berlin and now dual-headquartered in Berlin and San Francisco, it captures video, audio, image, device, EMR, financial and outcomes data from inside and around the OR and applies AI analytics to it — delivering pre-operative workflow optimization, real-time intraoperative decision support, and post-operative clinical safety, quality and utilization insights. The platform pairs the PRIME365 vendor-neutral OR / medical-device integration layer with the qvident surgical performance-management and analytics suite, and is deployed in more than 4,000 operating rooms worldwide. Caresyntax sells to hospitals and surgery centers, MedTech manufacturers and insurers, and integrates with EMR, PACS and scheduling systems. It operates an API gateway at api.caresyntax.com, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract — integration is delivered through enterprise and partner engagements.

providers.name: Dialogue
providers.description: Dialogue is a leading Canadian virtual healthcare and employee wellness provider operating an Integrated Health Platform that delivers primary care, mental health support, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP), and wellness programming to members through a single mobile and web application available 24/7/365. The company serves more than 52,000 Canadian organizations — including Sun Life, National Bank of Canada, Via Rail, Lightspeed, and Samsung — connecting employees and their families with multidisciplinary care teams of nurses, physicians, and mental health specialists. Dialogue is a consumer-facing digital health application; it does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Eleos Health
providers.description: Eleos Health is the most widely adopted AI platform in behavioral and community-based healthcare. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, Eleos delivers purpose-built AI workflow agents that span clinical documentation, compliance, and revenue cycle management. The platform embeds directly inside providers' existing web-based electronic health records (EHRs) via a lightweight browser extension for both in-person and telehealth sessions, turning ambient session capture or quick text summaries into structured, payer-ready progress notes and cutting documentation time by roughly 70%. Eleos Compliance reviews every note against common risk areas (note cloning, empty notes, interventions, progress mentions, action plans, and the golden thread), and its revenue cycle tooling automates eligibility checks and claim protection. Deployed across 120+ care organizations in 30+ states, Eleos integrates without custom API builds; it is backed by Menlo Ventures and Greenfield Partners.

providers.name: Limbic
providers.description: Limbic is a clinical AI company for mental healthcare, founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York with a London engineering base. Its two products — Limbic Access, a Class IIa (UKCA) medical device for conversational patient intake, assessment and clinical decision support, and Limbic Care, an AI companion delivering guided CBT and on-demand support between therapy sessions — are embedded by health plans, health systems, behavioral health providers and NHS Talking Therapies services. Both are built on the proprietary "Limbic Layer", a clinical reasoning layer that sits between the user and a large language model to enforce validated clinical guidance. Limbic Access embeds into a provider website with a small script snippet rather than a public developer API; the company publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI definitions or SDKs, and integrates with EHR and patient management systems through customer engagements. Research code accompanying its peer-reviewed studies (including work published in Nature Medicine) is open on GitHub.

providers.name: Notable
providers.description: Notable is an intelligent-automation company purpose-built for healthcare, applying AI agents to administrative and operational workflows across patient access, revenue cycle management, care operations, and contact-center automation. Its platform pairs a library of prebuilt AI Agents with Flow Builder, a low-code interface for designing, training, and deploying automations, Sidekick, a human-in-the-loop AI co-pilot for clinically complex work such as prior authorization, and Flow AI, a conversational assistant for workflow builders. Integration runs bi-directionally against Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, MEDITECH, athenahealth and eClinicalWorks over a mix of FHIR APIs, HL7 interfaces, RPA and third-party APIs. Notable reports deployment at 12,000+ sites of care serving 38M+ patients, with customers including Intermountain Health, MUSC Health, CommonSpirit Health and CityMD, and is backed by ICONIQ Growth, Greylock, F-Prime, Oak HC/FT, Maverick Ventures and 8VC. Notable publishes no public API contract; its developer documentation sits behind customer SSO. This profile is enriched from the company's public trust, security, and llms.txt surfaces.

providers.name: TytoCare
providers.description: TytoCare is an AI-powered remote physical examination and virtual care company. Its FDA-cleared handheld examination device and Home Smart Clinic / Pro Smart Clinic platforms let clinicians remotely examine heart, lungs, ears, throat, skin, and temperature, serving 240+ healthcare organizations and 1.6M+ patients. TytoCare publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs — EHR and telehealth integrations are delivered through private partner channels. An Insight Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Novoic
providers.description: Novoic is a London-based clinical AI company building speech biomarkers for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment. Its technology analyzes how people speak - acoustic and linguistic patterns - to screen for subtle cognitive change in about ten minutes on any smart device. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

providers.name: UptimeHealth
providers.description: UptimeHealth is a healthcare operations platform for managing medical equipment service, compliance documentation, and facility maintenance across dental, medical, and veterinary practices from a single dashboard. The platform tracks devices, automates compliance tasks and logs, and coordinates repair service requests, reporting 73,000+ devices protected across 6,000+ facilities. UptimeHealth publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation — its platform (uptimecontroller.com) is a closed SaaS application.

providers.name: Md Ally
providers.description: MD Ally is a New York-based digital health company that integrates telehealth into the 911 emergency response system. Its platform lets emergency dispatchers route low-acuity, non-emergency callers to a virtual care tier, connecting patients with telehealth clinicians, in-network resources, and social services instead of dispatching EMS or defaulting to an emergency-room visit. MD Ally works with public safety agencies and payers to expand traditional two-tier dispatch models, reduce unnecessary ambulance transports and ER visits, and improve patient navigation. Backed by General Catalyst and Techstars.

providers.name: Nitra
providers.description: Nitra is an integrated financial and operational platform — an "operating system" — for independent medical practices, unifying business banking, spend management, payments, accounting, capital, and front-desk automation in one system. Its core products include the Nitra Card (a Visa business card with cashback and vendor pricing), NitraMart (a medical-supplies marketplace), BillPay payment processing, accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Nextech), Trina (an AI assistant for phone reception and invoice matching), and capital products such as lending, equipment financing, and insurance factoring. Nitra primarily serves eye care, aesthetics, dental specialty, and fertility practices as well as multi-site groups. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA-aware, holds funds at FDIC-insured banks, and is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital. Nitra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Revel Ai Health
providers.description: RevelAi Health is a healthcare technology company building a conversational AI platform for orthopedic and musculoskeletal care teams. Its AI agent, "kimi," automates patient outreach, triage, clinical documentation, and follow-up across the care episode, supporting value-based care models, quality reporting, and Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROM) collection. The platform offers multilingual population-health outreach across voice, text, and email, ambient clinical documentation, and AI-augmented staffing and task management for ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals and health systems, and physician practices. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance programs. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public API surface was found.

providers.name: ConnectRN
providers.description: connectRN is a Waltham, Massachusetts based per-diem (PRN) healthcare staffing marketplace that connects nurses, CNAs and allied clinicians with open shifts at hospitals, home health and hospice agencies, and skilled nursing facilities across the United States. Clinicians browse and claim shifts through the connectRN mobile app with no minimum commitment, no required weekends or holidays, and same-day pay; facilities post shifts, auto-backfill open coverage and approve timesheets through a web platform at app.connectrn.com. In April 2026 connectRN merged with SnapCare, combining connectRN's PRN clinician community with SnapCare's Booker workforce technology platform. connectRN operates a public status page but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its API host api.connectrn.com serves the first-party mobile and web applications only.

providers.name: Heard
providers.description: Heard (Heard Technologies, Inc.) is the financial management platform built specifically for therapists and wellness practitioners in private practice. Founded in 2019 and based in Seattle, Washington, Heard pairs easy-to-use software with a dedicated human team to handle bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and business banking in a single subscription, so licensed mental health and allied health clinicians can focus on their clients. Heard serves solo and single-owner group practices across the United States, from newer sole proprietors to established S corporations, and connects with tools practices already use such as SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Headway, Jane App, Stripe, and Square. Heard exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity, its public web properties, and the published llms.txt.

providers.name: Proximie
providers.description: Proximie is a health-tech company building a cloud platform it describes as the operating system for intelligent operating rooms, connecting surgical teams, medical devices, and data for remote telementoring, telesurgery, session recording, and AI-powered surgical insights across 500+ facilities in 50 countries. For developers, Proximie ships a pre-release C++ SDK (media streaming and session management, with an internal REST layer) and runs a Development Partners program that lets OEMs and medtech companies embed real-time connectivity, secure data routing, and white-label collaboration into their own devices. Proximie also open-sources WebRTC/Janus tooling (jarust, janus-mobile-sdk). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Vetcove
providers.description: Vetcove is a free purchasing and procurement platform for veterinary clinics and animal-health organizations that lets a practice shop every distributor and manufacturer at once. It consolidates accounts from suppliers such as Henry Schein, Patterson Vet, MWI, and Midwest Veterinary into one interface where staff compare live pricing and availability, place and track orders, and manage inventory across vendors without changing existing supplier relationships. The service is delivered as a web application and mobile app and is free to veterinary clinics and nonprofits. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Cadence Solutions
providers.description: Cadence Solutions, Inc. — operating as Cadence — is a New York-based clinical AI and remote patient monitoring company founded in 2020 by Chris Altchek. Cadence partners with large health systems and payers to deliver continuous chronic-care management between clinic visits: FDA-cleared connected devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, weight scales) stream daily vitals to a 24/7 clinical care team backed by supervised AI agents that flag out-of-range readings, close care gaps, and escalate to clinicians for medication titration. The platform covers hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure and COPD, is integrated two-way into partner EHRs (Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth), and supports Medicare RPM/CCM and the CMS ACCESS model. Cadence serves more than 100,000 patients across systems including Community Health Systems, LifePoint Health, Providence, Rush, MemorialCare, Corewell Health, Ardent Health and Duke Health. It raised a $100M Series C led by Spark Capital in June 2026 ($241M total, ~$1.23B valuation). Cadence publishes no public developer program or API: EHR interoperability is delivered as bilateral health system integrations, not a self-serve API surface.

providers.name: Docquity
providers.description: Docquity is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company operating Asia's largest verified professional network for licensed healthcare practitioners, with more than 500,000 verified doctors across nine markets including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore and Taiwan. Its flagship product, Dx, is an AI clinical thinking partner that bundles clinical search and decision support, accredited continuing medical education, peer community and case discussion, and patient-ready summary notes into an invite-only mobile and web platform gated behind medical-credential verification. For life-sciences and enterprise partners Docquity sells an Intelligence Suite comprising Pulse, which measures healthcare-professional conviction and engagement, and Dialog, which runs field engagement and activation programs against that audience. Docquity also operates Docquity Jobs, a medical recruitment board. The company publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its api.docquity.com backend and id.docquity.com identity service exist to serve its own first-party applications and are not offered to third-party developers.

providers.name: Smile Digital Health
providers.description: Smile Digital Health (formerly Smile CDR) is a Toronto-based health interoperability software company and the commercial steward of the open source HAPI FHIR project (the world's most widely deployed Java implementation of the HL7 FHIR standard). Its flagship product, Smile CDR — marketed under the broader Smile Omni portfolio as the OmniVera Health Data Platform — is a FHIR-native clinical data repository and integration platform that ingests HL7 v2.x, CDA, CSV, JSON, XML, and FHIR payloads, normalizes them into FHIR (R4, R5, STU3, DSTU2), and exposes them through a hardened FHIR REST API, SMART on FHIR / OAuth2 / OIDC security, Bulk Data export, Subscriptions, MDM, Terminology Services, CQL-based Quality Measures, and a JSON Admin API. The platform is deployed on-prem and across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with HITRUST v9.4, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ONC 2015 Edition certifications, and is used by 190+ global customers, including 30+ US payers running CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (CMS-0057-F) workloads on its CMS Suite. Adjacent Smile Omni product families include OmniCompli (regulatory compliance, including CMS Suite and CMS Concierge), OmniQ (digital quality measures / HEDIS, Intelligence Hub), and OmniConcierge (managed and professional services). The primary developer surface is the FHIR REST API, with per-endpoint auto-generated OpenAPI / Swagger UI at `{baseUrl}/swagger-ui/`, plus a separate JSON Admin API for cluster, module, user, audit, batch job, MDM, and OpenID Connect administration.

providers.name: Wheel
providers.description: Wheel is a healthcare technology company providing the infrastructure for modern telehealth. Its Wheel Horizon platform is a modular care-enablement system that combines a nationwide clinician network, evidence-based virtual care programs, and integrated clinical operations so digital health companies, health plans, retailers and pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations can launch and scale virtual care. Wheel also operates WheelX, an enterprise AI health exchange, and Connected Services for integration. Wheel exposes a partner API, governed by an API Terms of Use and gated behind an approval process; the platform is HIPAA compliant and maintains SOC 2 controls. Public API reference documentation, SDKs, and a developer portal are not published. Wheel was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV.

providers.name: Accurx
providers.description: Accurx is a United Kingdom clinical communication and workflow company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, whose software is used across NHS primary care, secondary care, and community and mental health services to message patients, run patient triage, batch-message cohorts, book and remind appointments, and (via its Scribe product) draft clinical notes with AI. Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

providers.name: Aiwyn
providers.description: Aiwyn is a practice-automation platform built for modern accounting and CPA firms, unifying payments, practice management, client experience, and tax into a single relationship-centered system. Aiwyn Payments automates invoicing, card and ACH collection, and reconciliation; Aiwyn Practice covers time, billing, project management and resource planning; Aiwyn Experience delivers a unified client portal for engagement letters and secure document exchange; and Aiwyn Tax adds AI-assisted tax preparation. The company serves 800+ firms and raised $113M from KKR and Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company; Aiwyn publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time, so enrichment is limited to identity, its published llms.txt, and probed domain security.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: NutriSense
providers.description: NutriSense is a metabolic health and wellness company that pairs continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with 1:1 registered-dietitian coaching and a mobile app. Members receive glucose biosensors, real-time and historical glucose analytics, AI-assisted pattern insights, stress-management sessions, and video consults with credentialed, glucose-certified nutritionists to build sustainable nutrition, weight-loss, and metabolic-health habits. Nutrisense runs a consumer product with a member web and mobile app experience; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It does publish a machine-readable llms.txt at nutrisense.io/llms.txt.

providers.name: Siemens Healthineers
providers.description: Siemens Healthineers AG is a German medical technology company (XETRA SHL) covering medical imaging, laboratory diagnostics, point-of-care testing, advanced therapies, and cancer care (following the April 2021 Varian Medical Systems acquisition for USD 16.4 billion). Its digital surface is anchored by the teamplay digital health platform, the Digital Marketplace, syngo.via OpenApps, and the Frontier Development Kit, with developer access offered through a gated teamplay developer portal that exposes APIs for single sign-on, licensing, user roles and permissions, the teamplay receiver plug-in, DICOM image access, customer-specific report submission, and status indicator notifications. No public OpenAPI specifications are published; the API catalog and reference documentation sit behind teamplay developer account authentication.

providers.name: Tomorrow Health
providers.description: Tomorrow Health is an AI-powered platform for home-based care that connects providers, payors, and durable medical equipment (DMEPOS) suppliers, using intelligent automation to simplify ordering, routing, and reviewing home healthcare services. Its Horizon Suite includes AI Ordering, AI Fax Intake, and THEA (Tomorrow Health Expert Assistant). Headquartered in New York and backed by a16z, Bond Capital, and Obvious Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is currently published; the customer application is a private authenticated web app.

providers.name: Unobravo
providers.description: Unobravo is Europe's largest online psychology service, founded in 2019 by psychologist Danila De Stefano. It matches people with one of 9,500+ individually vetted psychologists and psychotherapists for individual, couples, and group therapy delivered online, serving Italy, Spain, and France as well as Italians abroad, with 500,000+ people supported across more than 10 million online sessions, plus a B2B mental-wellbeing offering (Unobravo Business) and an ECM training academy. Backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Its backend API (api.unobravo.com) is private, with no public developer surface.

providers.name: BestDoc
providers.description: BestDoc is a healthcare patient-relationship-management (PRM) company that helps hospitals improve the patient experience across inpatient and outpatient care. Its platform includes BestDoc Concierge for inpatient experience management (non-clinical requests, room food ordering, discharge management), BestDoc Practice for outpatient patient-request management, BestDoc Survey for omni-channel patient feedback, an AI Reply Assistant for automated review responses, and continued-care engagement tools. BestDoc integrates with hospital information systems (HIS), EMRs, and payment gateways. BestDoc Technology Pvt. Ltd. is an ISO 27001:2013 certified company operating from Kochi, Bangalore, and Dubai. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Genalyte
providers.description: Genalyte, Inc. is a San Diego, California in-vitro diagnostics company building point-of-care blood testing systems based on silicon photonic microring resonator technology. Founded by Cary Gunn, the company developed the Maverick Diagnostic System and its successor Merlin, an automated benchtop analyzer that runs hematology, chemistry and immunoassay panels — including CBC, lipid panel and comprehensive metabolic panel — from small whole-blood or serum volumes and returns results in roughly twenty to thirty minutes while the patient is still in the clinic. A cloud verification layer the company markets as CloudLab quality-checks results and routes them into electronic medical record systems. Genalyte received FDA clearance for a thyroid stimulating hormone immunoassay performed on a silicon chip and previously held an FDA Emergency Use Authorization for a rapid COVID-19 antibody test. The company is investor-backed (Khosla Ventures, Verily Life Sciences and others) and is a HIPAA covered entity that publishes a Notice of Privacy Practices. As of this profile Genalyte publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Insightec
providers.description: Insightec Ltd. is an Israeli medical device company, founded in 1999 and headquartered in Tirat Carmel, Israel, that develops and sells MR-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) systems under the Exablate brand. Its Exablate Neuro platform focuses more than a thousand ultrasound beams through the intact skull to ablate a target deep in the brain without an incision, and is approved for essential tremor and Parkinson's disease, including staged bilateral treatment. The Exablate body platform is used for uterine fibroids, palliation of bone metastases, and prostate indications, and the company runs clinical programs in blood-brain-barrier opening and glioblastoma. Insightec publishes a public product documentation portal of operator manuals and handbooks for the Exablate systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs, or agent surface; its systems integrate with GE and Siemens MR scanners as clinical devices rather than through a public API.

providers.name: Medmonk
providers.description: Medmonk is a pharma market access platform that connects brand teams, healthcare providers, pharmacies, and patients on a single real-time infrastructure. It automates point-of-sale copay enrollment, benefit investigations, prior authorizations, financial assistance, hub workflows, and adherence tracking across specialty and rare-disease medications, reaching roughly 98% of U.S. pharmacy and buy/bill network connectivity. Medmonk states it exposes FHIR-compliant APIs to integrate with existing EHR, CRM, and pharmacy systems, and claims SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, though it publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Founded in the Y Combinator W12 batch.

providers.name: nference
providers.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Oscar
providers.description: Oscar Health (NYSE: OSCR) is a technology-driven health insurance company founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City. It offers individual and family health plans, small-business and ICHRA employer benefits, and Medicare Advantage in a growing set of U.S. states, pairing coverage with a consumer mobile app, 24/7 virtual urgent care, telemedicine, primary care, and concierge Care Teams. Oscar's +Oscar division licenses its full-stack technology platform (Campaign Builder and other tools) to other payers and providers. The company is NCQA-accredited across Health Plan, Utilization Management, Credentialing, Provider Network, and Health Equity programs. Oscar is a General Catalyst portfolio company. As a CMS-regulated payer it is subject to the Interoperability and Patient Access rule, though it does not currently publish an open, self-serve developer API portal.

providers.name: Pointone
providers.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

providers.name: Prenetics
providers.description: Prenetics Global Limited (NASDAQ: PRE) is a consumer healthcare and longevity company whose flagship brand is IM8, a science-backed daily-nutrition and longevity supplement line co-founded with David Beckham that reached roughly $120M in annual recurring revenue within its first year. The company's IM8 Health direct-to-consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-native commerce surface: it publishes an /llms.txt agent guide and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp that advertises a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) shopping endpoint, letting AI agents search the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout via Shop Pay, Google Pay, and Shopify card handlers. Prenetics itself publishes no separate developer/API program; the agent-commerce surface is the IM8 Health UCP/MCP storefront.

providers.name: RefleXion Medical
providers.description: RefleXion Medical is a privately held therapeutic oncology company headquartered in Hayward, California, founded in 2009 by Sam Mazin and Akshay Nanduri around the biology-guided radiotherapy (BgRT) concept conceived at Stanford University in 2007. The company designs, manufactures and commercializes the RefleXion X1 radiotherapy platform and SCINTIX biology-guided radiotherapy, which uses onboard PET detectors to sense emissions from an injected radiopharmaceutical and autonomously direct external-beam radiotherapy delivery with sub-second latency. The RefleXion X1 received FDA clearance for SRS, SBRT and IMRT in 2020, and SCINTIX therapy was FDA cleared in February 2023 for treating tumors in the lung or bone arising from primary and metastatic cancer. RefleXion has raised more than $500 million from investors including TPG's The Rise Fund, KCK Group, PSP Investments, Sofinnova, Pfizer Ventures and Johnson & Johnson Innovation. RefleXion is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Snap-on
providers.description: Snap-on Incorporated is a global manufacturer and marketer of tools, equipment, diagnostics, repair information, and systems solutions for professional users in vehicle repair, industrial, and other industries. The company provides diagnostic tools, electronic parts catalogs (EPC), repair information systems (ShopKey Pro, SureTrack), and shop management software. Snap-on integrates with dealer management systems (DMS) through its EPC integration program and strategic technology partnerships.

providers.name: Sonar Mental Health
providers.description: Sonar Mental Health provides 24/7 text-based wellbeing coaching and care navigation for youth. Trained Wellbeing Coaches lead the conversations, supported by AI tooling that surfaces context and flags risk without making independent decisions, delivering between-visit and after-hours support, escalation and care coordination to higher levels of care, and real-time insights dashboards for measurement-based care across schools, health systems, primary care, and EAP pathways. The company reports serving 20,000+ young people with higher engagement between visits, and is backed by 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture (SOC 2, HIPAA), and public web properties.

providers.name: Virta Health
providers.description: Virta Health is a virtual, nutrition-first healthcare company delivering sustainable weight loss and type 2 diabetes reversal. Its program combines personalized nutrition plans, continuous expert health coaching, physician-led medication management, and connected devices, delivered through a consumer mobile app and sold to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. Virta is HITRUST- and SOC 2 Type II-certified and operates as a HIPAA-covered clinical service. As of this enrichment pass Virta publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: voize
providers.description: voize is a German healthcare AI company (voize GmbH) building a voice-documentation platform for long-term care, skilled nursing, and disability-support facilities. Caregivers speak naturally on a smartphone during patient care and voize's on-device and cloud speech models convert the free speech into structured, categorized entries that sync bi-directionally in real time into the facility's electronic health record (EHR) system. The product reduces documentation burden for nursing staff, works offline, recognizes patient names and corrects grammar, and integrates directly with major EHRs used in skilled nursing. voize is backed by HV Capital and operates in Germany and the United States. It ships a mobile application rather than a public developer API, but exposes EHR integrations, a trust center, and a vulnerability disclosure / bug bounty program on its public surface.

providers.name: Defense Health Agency
providers.description: The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is a joint, integrated combat support agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to combatant commands. DHA operates the Military Health System (MHS), MHS Genesis electronic health record, the Military Health System Data Repository (MDR), and the Enterprise Intelligence and Data Solutions (EIDS) program. Data exchange inside MHS Genesis uses SMART on FHIR APIs, but DHA does not currently publish a general-purpose public developer API.

providers.name: Mars
providers.description: Mars, Incorporated is one of the world's largest privately held companies, producing confectionery, pet food, food, and providing veterinary care. The company owns iconic brands including M&M's, Snickers, Twix, Milky Way, Skittles, Wrigley, Orbit, Extra, Pedigree, Whiskas, Royal Canin, IAMS, and Sheba, and operates Mars Petcare clinical brands including Banfield Pet Hospital, VCA Animal Hospitals, BluePearl, and Antech Diagnostics. Mars operates in over 80 countries. Mars operates a public Azure-API-Management developer portal at developer.mars.com for partner and B2B integrations, alongside closed channels such as the Mars Supplier Gateway.

providers.name: 10x Genomics
providers.description: 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company building instruments, reagents, and software that resolve biology at single-cell and spatial resolution. Its Chromium platform delivers single-cell gene expression, immune profiling, and multiomic analysis; its Visium and Xenium platforms deliver spatial transcriptomics and in situ single-cell spatial biology. The company supports researchers with analysis software (Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, Xenium Onboard Analysis, Loupe Browser), a cloud analysis platform, and open datasets. 10x Genomics does not publish a general-purpose public REST developer API; its developer surface is command-line analysis pipelines, file-format tooling, and open-source repositories on GitHub.

providers.name: BrainCo
providers.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

providers.name: 7 Cups
providers.description: 7 Cups (7cups.com) is an on-demand emotional health and online therapy service founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator. It connects people seeking support with a network of trained volunteer listeners for free, anonymous one-on-one chat, and matches members with licensed therapists and social workers for paid online therapy delivered by messaging, audio, or video. The platform also runs peer community forums, group support chat rooms, and self-help "growth path" content. 7 Cups operates across 189 countries in 140 languages with hundreds of thousands of trained listeners. It is a consumer web and mobile product rather than an API-first developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and carries no public API at this time.

providers.name: Ambiq Micro
providers.description: Ambiq Micro is a semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for battery-powered and endpoint-AI devices. Its proprietary Subthreshold Power Optimized Technology (SPOT) platform lets its Apollo family of Arm Cortex-M microcontrollers and Artasie real-time clocks run at extremely low energy, powering wearables, hearables, healthcare, smart-home, industrial and gaming devices. Ambiq's developer surface is an embedded C/C++ toolchain - the AmbiqSuite SDK and the open-source neuralSPOT AI SDK/Toolkit - plus a set of first-party Python AI toolkits (heartKIT, sleepKIT, physioKIT, neuralspotx) published on PyPI and GitHub (AmbiqAI, AmbiqMicro). This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

providers.name: Floy
providers.description: Floy is a Munich-based healthcare AI company (founded 2021) that builds AI-powered radiology software for medical imaging. Its two products — opportunistic screening and diagnostic assistance — analyse CT and MRI examinations to surface additional findings beyond the initial radiologist assessment, enabling earlier diagnosis and better patient outcomes. The models are trained on 17 million medical examinations. Floy is an ISO 13485:2016 certified, EU MDR Class IIb medical-device manufacturer and is GDPR compliant, with research partnerships including DKFZ, LMU Klinikum Munich, Stanford, and the University of Oxford. It is backed by HV Capital, 10x Founders, xdeck, and Acurio Ventures. Floy is a clinical B2B product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Hello Patient
providers.description: Hello Patient builds AI agents (branded "Mia") for patient conversations across voice, text, and web chat, helping healthcare practices automate their front office, back office, and patient-growth workflows. Mia handles 24/7 appointment scheduling, insurance verification, and patient intake on the front office; revenue-cycle (RCM) follow-up and no-show recovery on the back office; and lead conversion, patient recall, and targeted outreach for growth. The platform serves dentistry, dermatology, ENT, mental health, optometry, primary care, urgent care, veterinary, and consumer-health practices, and integrates with EHR and practice systems including ModMed, AdvancedMD, NextGen, eClinicalWorks, Athena Health, Veradigm, Zenoti, and others. Hello Patient is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type 2 certified. It is backed by 8VC and Scale Venture Partners. No public developer API is documented at this time; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Oviva
providers.description: Oviva is a European digital health company, founded in 2014, delivering personalized, dietitian-led care for people managing type 2 diabetes, obesity, and other diet-related conditions. It combines a mobile app for logging food, activity, and progress with human coaching from a network of 420+ dietitians, psychologists, and doctors, operating across the UK, Germany, and Switzerland and serving 900K+ people. Oviva is delivered as a regulated digital therapeutic (CE-marked, ISO 27001, NHS DTAC and CQC assessed) rather than through a public developer API; this profile captures its security, compliance, and legal surface. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: Docura Health
providers.description: Docura Health builds purpose-built software for physicians who prepare medical-legal reports — independent medical examinations (IME), qualified medical examiner (QME), agreed medical examiner (AME), permanent-and-stationary, and supplemental evaluations. The platform organizes complete case files (medical records, audio, and video), generates intelligent chronological summaries that link back to source documents, guides AMA Guides-compliant impairment ratings (5th and 6th Edition), and produces structured reports from customizable templates matched to each evaluator's practice style. Docura is HIPAA compliant with enterprise-grade end-to-end encryption and audit trails, and is backed by Y Combinator. This profile was seeded from a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from Docura Health's public website and trust center; no public developer API or documentation was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Swift Medical
providers.description: Swift Medical develops AI-powered wound and skin care management software for healthcare organizations across acute, post-acute, home health, and hospice settings. Its flagship Skin & Wound app captures calibrated wound images on mobile devices, applies computer-vision tissue analytics and auto-tracing to measure and classify wounds, and coordinates care through longitudinal documentation backed by the company's database of more than 32 million wound images. The platform emphasizes secure, compliant handling of protected health information (SOC 2 Type 2, encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, MFA) and single sign-on via Okta and Microsoft. Swift Medical does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through direct engagement and enterprise SSO/EHR arrangements. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Brightline
providers.description: Brightline is an award-winning pediatric mental health practice delivering therapy, psychiatry (including medication management), and psychological testing for children and adolescents up to age 18, using an evidence-based, family-focused model that begins with a structured diagnostic evaluation. It treats anxiety, OCD, ADHD, disruptive behavioral disorders, depression, trauma, grief, and autism-spectrum symptoms via in-person clinics in New York and telehealth across NY, NJ, CT, MA, and WA, and operates BrightLife Kids, a free California state-funded behavioral health program for families with children up to age 12. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Threshold Ventures; Brightline is a consumer/clinical healthcare provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Capim
providers.description: Capim is a Sao Paulo-based vertical SaaS and fintech company for the dental sector in Brazil, founded in 2021 by Marcelo Lutz and Roberto Biselli. Its platform pairs dental-clinic management software - appointment scheduling (Agenda Capim), digital patient records, and AI-driven patient reactivation - with embedded financial products: buy-now-pay-later patient financing (Financiamento Capim, up to 36 installments), direct-credit collections (Carne Capim), and an integrated card/PIX payment terminal (Maquininha Capim). Capim serves more than 6,000 dental clinics, has issued over R$450 million in credit, and raised a US$26.7M Series A co-led by Valor Capital and QED Investors. No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Dandy
providers.description: Dandy is a digital dental lab platform for dentists, dental practices, and dental service organizations (DSOs). It combines intraoral scanner hardware, cloud-based case management software, and in-house dental lab manufacturing into a single scan-to-lab workflow. Dentists capture digital impressions with a Dandy intraoral scanner, submit cases through Dandy software, collaborate in real time with lab technicians via chat, video, and chairside scan review, and receive finished restorations manufactured by Dandy. Product lines include crowns, bridges, implants, clear aligners, retainers, dentures, night guards, splints, and sleep apnea devices. Dandy positions itself as an AI-powered digital dental lab modernizing restorative and orthodontic dentistry. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes an agent-facing llms.txt and ai-index.json but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Decorte Future Industries
providers.description: Decorte Future Industries (DFI) is a UK healthtech company building AI that extracts clinical health signals from sound. Its technology turns the microphone in an ordinary smartphone into a screening device, analyzing audio to detect signs of heart, breathing, brain, and gut conditions at a standard targeting in-clinic specialist examinations. DFI's first commercial product, Sonus Health, is a veterinary heart-screening platform: clinics and pet owners record 30 seconds of heart sound from dogs (cats and horses coming soon) with a phone, and AI returns heart rate, heart rate variability, murmur detection, and a composite Heart Health Score in seconds, with a full report reviewed by a board-certified veterinary cardiologist within 48 hours. Sonus Health ships as iOS and Android apps for pet owners and a web dashboard for veterinary clinics.

providers.name: Dutch
providers.description: Dutch (dutch.com) is a United States pet telemedicine service that gives dog and cat owners 24/7 access to licensed online veterinarians through a low-cost membership (from about $11/month), pairing virtual vet visits with free prescription delivery to most states. Founded to bring the direct-to-consumer telehealth model to pet care, Dutch is backed by Forerunner Ventures. The public presence is a consumer telehealth storefront hosted on Shopify; at the time of profiling no first-party public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface was found. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's real, published web surface (identity, policies, account, support) and the live platform-level discovery documents exposed on the domain.

providers.name: Evvy
providers.description: Evvy is a women's health company offering at-home vaginal microbiome testing and personalized care. Its CLIA-certified metagenomic (mNGS) Vaginal Health Test identifies over 700 bacteria and fungi from a self-collected sample, with results reviewed by licensed clinicians who deliver personalized insights and clinician-designed treatment programs for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis, aerobic vaginitis, yeast infections, recurrent UTIs, and fertility-related concerns. Evvy also sells a line of vaginal health products including probiotics and boric-acid, hyaluronic-acid, and probiotic suppositories, plus a provider program for clinicians and a large library of science-backed educational content. Backed by General Catalyst, Evvy was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Evvy is a direct-to-consumer health and e-commerce business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Petfolk
providers.description: Petfolk is a Charlotte, North Carolina based veterinary care company that operates a network of modern, company-owned pet care centers across the US Southeast and Texas, paired with a consumer mobile app. Founded and led by veterinarian Dr. Audrey Wystrach, Petfolk provides primary and wellness care, sick and urgent care, dentistry, surgery, spay and neuter, vaccinations and diagnostics for dogs and cats, delivered under a "gentle handling" clinical model with seven-day-a-week hours and published, transparent pricing. The Petfolk iOS and Android app lets pet parents book in-person or virtual appointments, message their care team around the clock, request medications and access their pet's medical records; a paid PetfolkCare membership layers on 24/7 veterinary support and per-visit savings. The company raised a $40M Series B in October 2023 led by Movendo Capital, with White Star Capital and Idea Farm Ventures participating. Petfolk is a consumer veterinary services operator, not an API provider: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, SDKs or MCP server. It does publish a hand-authored llms.txt at the site root, which is the company's only machine-readable, agent-facing surface.

providers.name: Tia Health
providers.description: Tia Health is a Canadian telehealth platform that connects patients with licensed Canadian providers - family doctors, nurse practitioners, specialists, and naturopaths - for on-demand virtual care by phone, video, and secure messaging. Its services span virtual walk-in and family-practice appointments, prescription renewals, sick notes, lab requisitions, and mental health therapy (via partner Focus Mental Wellness), with visits covered by provincial health plans in Ontario (OHIP), British Columbia (MSP), and Alberta (AHCIP) and paid options elsewhere. Tia Health is part of the WELL Health Technologies Corp. clinic network, one of the largest outpatient networks in Canada. As of this review Tia Health is a consumer-facing virtual-care product with no public developer portal, no documented REST/OpenAPI, and no exposed HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement or SMART-on-FHIR configuration; interoperability in the Canadian market is stewarded federally through Canada Health Infoway's pan-Canadian FHIR (CA Core / CA Baseline) specifications, which this platform does not publicly surface.

providers.name: 8fit
providers.description: 8fit is a consumer health and fitness application offering personalized home workout programs (HIIT, boxing, Pilates, yoga, and meditation), custom healthy meal and nutrition plans, and holistic wellness guidance built around sustainable habit-building rather than quick fixes. Founded in Berlin and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum, 8fit reached more than 40 million downloads before being acquired by Withings (a Gilde Healthcare portfolio company) in February 2022. Withings announced the discontinuation of the standalone 8fit app effective June 26, 2026, folding its nutrition and activity content into the Withings app and Withings+ service. 8fit is a mobile/web consumer app and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Aidence
providers.description: Aidence is a radiology AI company founded in Amsterdam in 2015 that builds clinical AI for the lung cancer pathway. Its flagship product, Veye Lung Nodules (now DeepHealth Lung), is a CE-marked AI solution that detects, classifies, quantifies, and measures growth of pulmonary nodules on chest CT scans, and is the AI of choice in NHS England's Targeted Lung Health Checks screening programme. Aidence was acquired by RadNet in 2022 and now operates under the DeepHealth brand; aidence.com redirects to deephealth.com/aidence. The product integrates with hospital systems over DICOM/PACS via the Veye Engine rather than a public developer REST API — no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published. This profile captures the company's identity plus its probed security and disclosure posture.

providers.name: Apricot
providers.description: Apricot is an AI-native clinical documentation platform for home health and post-acute care agencies, founded by home-health operator Trent Smith and headquartered in Oklahoma. Its software cuts start-of-care (SOC) and OASIS documentation time by up to 85% and QA time by up to 40%, automating medication reconciliation, wound documentation, ICD coding recommendations, and narrative generation while capturing vitals, photos, signatures, and voice notes in the home and syncing to each agency's EMR configuration. Apricot is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant and raised a Series A led by Insight Partners in 2025. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web presence; Apricot currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Cala Health
providers.description: Cala Health is a bioelectronic medicine company that develops wearable neuromodulation therapies for chronic disease. Its FDA-cleared Cala kIQ and Cala TRIO systems deliver TAPS (Transcutaneous Afferent Patterned Stimulation) therapy through a wrist-worn device that is physician-prescribed and clinically proven to reduce action hand tremors associated with essential tremor and Parkinson's disease. Patients manage therapy and view results through the MyCala portal, and clinicians access data through the Cala 360 provider portal. Cala Health is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company operating in the life-sciences / medical-device sector. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; enrichment has captured the company's public security, privacy, and support surface.

providers.name: Faks
providers.description: Faks is a French SaaS platform that digitizes and streamlines the commercial relationships across the pharmacy ecosystem. It gives pharmacies, pharmacy groups (groupements), and laboratories a single place to manage supplier relationships, commercial claims and disputes (litiges), expired and returnable product handling, promotions, and sell-in / sell-out performance. Faks connects to pharmacy management systems (LGO), purchasing platforms, and accounting tools through its Konnect integrations to automate what has traditionally been manual, paper, and email-driven work between the ~18,000 pharmacies, ~100 groups, and ~500 laboratories it targets in France. The company is backed by Seedcamp. Faks does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and the enrichment surfaces that could be probed.

providers.name: Gaia
providers.description: Gaia (Gaia Family) is a value-based family-building company that makes fertility treatment financially accessible. Founded by Nader AlSalim after his own multi-year IVF journey, Gaia replaces unpredictable cycle-by-cycle IVF billing with fixed-price, all-inclusive plans and monthly payments, backed by a protection model that offers more tries — or money back — if treatment does not succeed. It partners with 180+ fertility clinics across the US and UK, covering IVF, egg freezing, embryo transfer, hormone and lab testing, and fertility navigation, and also offers fertility benefits to employers. This profile is a company lead (no public API surface) maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Genome Medical
providers.description: Genome Medical is a telehealth-enabled genetic services provider offering expert genetic counseling, test selection and ordering support, results interpretation, and clinical trial matching for individuals with rare and hereditary conditions. It partners with health systems, life sciences organizations, and genetic testing labs to scale genetic care, reduce diagnostic backlogs, and accelerate diagnoses through a proprietary clinical platform and patient portal. Genome Medical does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lucis
providers.description: Lucis is a Paris-based, AI-powered preventative health platform (Y Combinator P25; backed by General Catalyst) that helps members understand their biology through comprehensive lab testing and personalised coaching. Members receive two annual lab assessments (blood, urine, and saliva) at 450+ partner labs across Europe, producing 110+ data points across 11 body systems — metabolic, cardiovascular, hormonal, nervous, and more — which an AI engine turns into personalised action plans spanning nutrition, supplementation, sleep, activity, and mental health. The platform ingests wearable data (Garmin, Withings, Oura, Strava; Apple Watch and Whoop coming soon) for ongoing monitoring. Lucis is a consumer health product; as of this profile it exposes a member web/mobile application and a compliance portal but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Opalite Health
providers.description: Opalite Health is building the language layer for healthcare. Its platform delivers real-time, AI-powered medical interpretation across 150+ languages, validated against certified human interpreters and engineered for HIPAA-aligned, clinical-grade use. Opalite connects providers and patients with limited English proficiency in seconds — through EHR workflows and rapid healthcare deployment — to close language gaps that drive health inequities and poor outcomes. The company publishes a marketing and validation-study presence but does not operate a public developer API program; api.opalitehealth.com is a private application backend. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with the company's real identity, compliance posture (HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, AES-256 encryption), and domain-security probes.

providers.name: SimplePractice
providers.description: SimplePractice is a cloud-based practice management platform and EHR for behavioral and mental health, therapy, and wellness practices, covering scheduling, client management, telehealth, intake and clinical documentation, insurance and superbill billing, and a secure client portal (Client Secure Messaging). As of this cataloging, SimplePractice does NOT publish a public, self-serve developer API - there is no developer portal, no documented REST endpoints, no OpenAPI, and no webhooks for third parties. The only programmatic surface is the partner-only SimplePractice Enterprise scheduling integration, which lets EAPs and Managed Care Organizations view in-network provider availability and request appointments; it is delivered through customized partnerships rather than as public developer documentation. Third-party pages that advertise a "stable SimplePractice REST API" for clients, appointments, notes, or billing are unofficial and not backed by any SimplePractice developer program.

providers.name: Sofia
providers.description: Sofía is a 100% Mexican digital health insurance company that modernizes traditional medical coverage for enterprises, individuals, and families. Its plans combine zero-deductible major and minor medical care, preventive care with an assigned primary-care physician, and unlimited no-cost video consultations, all managed through a mobile app and an HR administrative portal. Sofía operates its own integrated medical network (SofíaMed) of hospitals and specialists, offers add-ons such as maternity, mental health, dental, and international coverage, and reimburses claims in an average of five business days. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Sofía positions insurance as a digital-first, member-centric health experience rather than a paper policy.

providers.name: Solace
providers.description: Solace Health is a US healthcare navigation company that connects patients with human patient advocates and care coordinators whose services are covered by insurance, including Medicare. Through solace.health and the app.solace.health member portal, patients are matched with an advocate who helps them understand diagnoses, prepare for appointments, coordinate care, manage bills, and navigate the healthcare system. Solace is a consumer-facing healthcare service company; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer program, API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Transcarent
providers.description: Transcarent is a health and care experience company serving self-insured employers, health plans, and government and labor union clients. Its consumer-facing platform, WayFinding, combines generative AI agents with instant access to human health guides and clinicians to deliver benefits navigation, clinical guidance, virtual primary and specialty care, pharmacy care, surgery care, cancer care, weight-health programs, and 2nd.MD second opinions in a single experience. The platform is built on an API-first, cloud-native architecture with pre-built HL7 FHIR and EDI connectors that integrate with existing eligibility files and medical, pharmacy, and point-solution benefits. Transcarent exposes these integrations to enterprise partners rather than through a public self-serve developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Ultromics
providers.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Zentist
providers.description: Zentist is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform built specifically for dental support organizations (DSOs) and multi-location dental practices. Its flagship product, Remit AI, uses artificial intelligence to automate electronic remittance advice (ERA) and explanation of benefits (EOB) parsing, payment posting, denial and adjustment categorization, and claims status tracking, while Cavi AR drives intelligent accounts-receivable follow-up. Executive dashboards deliver practice-level and organization-wide analytics. Trusted by more than 400 DSOs, Zentist reports doubling RCM productivity and cutting the cash-to-claim cycle in half within the first 100 days. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Zentist operates as a login-gated SaaS application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Blooming Health
providers.description: Blooming Health is an AI-powered, omnichannel care-management and community-engagement platform for healthcare and social-services organizations. It lets teams design multilingual care workflows across voice, SMS, and email in minutes — automating screening and needs assessments, service recommendations, outreach, appointment reminders, wellness check-ins, emergency broadcasts, closed-loop referral tracking, and Medicaid/SNAP recertification. The platform integrates with existing EHR/CRM systems and databases via FHIR, HL7, API, and SFTP, and is HIPAA compliant with encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, audit trails, BAAs, and SOC 2 documentation available on request. Blooming Health is a healthcare portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes an enterprise integration surface but publishes no public developer portal or API reference.

providers.name: LUMICKS
providers.description: LUMICKS is a life-science instrumentation company that builds tools to directly measure molecular and cellular interactions. Its Dynamic Single-Molecule platform, the C-Trap, uses optical tweezers to resolve real-time biomolecular interactions at the single-molecule level, while its Cell Avidity platforms (Avidion and the compact z-Movi) quantify the binding strength between immune cells and their targets for immuno-oncology, CAR-T, and antibody-therapeutics research. The developer surface is client-side: the official Apache-2.0 Python library lumicks.pylake analyzes single-molecule optical-tweezer data exported from the Bluelake acquisition software (force calibration, force-distance curve fitting, kymo/scan imaging, kymotracking, population dynamics), and bluelake-scripting automates instrument control. LUMICKS publishes no hosted public web API.

providers.name: Peppy
providers.description: Peppy is a global employee healthcare benefits platform, delivered through a mobile app, that connects workers with specialist clinicians across key life stages. Offered by employers as a benefit, Peppy provides unlimited access to practitioners covering women's health, men's health, fertility, pregnancy and early parenthood, menopause, and neurodiversity, alongside lifestyle support for nutrition, fitness, and mental wellbeing. Peppy operates a consumer and employer facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its published web properties and security posture. Peppy is a Seedcamp portfolio company.

providers.name: All In
providers.description: All In Food makes organic, gluten-free nut & seed snack bars on a social-impact model — every bar purchased helps fund local nutritious-food-access initiatives such as food banks, community gardens, and meal programs across the U.S. The company is backed by Obvious Ventures (a reported $4M raise) and sells through Sprouts and Starbucks as well as its own online store. While All In is a consumer-packaged-goods brand rather than a developer platform, its Shopify storefront exposes a genuine agent-native commerce surface: a canonical agents.md document, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a live hosted MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp for agent-driven catalog search, cart, checkout and fulfillment, and Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect for buyer identity. Checkout always requires explicit human buyer approval on payment.

providers.name: Bamboo Health
providers.description: Bamboo Health (formerly Appriss Health + PatientPing) is a healthcare technology company delivering Real-Time Care Intelligence across the physical and behavioral health continuum. It operates one of the nation's largest care-collaboration networks, connecting health systems, health plans, pharmacies, and state agencies through prescription drug monitoring (PDMP), care coordination, and behavioral healthcare navigation. Flagship solutions include Bamboo Bridge, OpenBeds, Pings, NarxCare, and the PMP AWARxE state monitoring platform. Backed by Insight Partners, the company supports over a billion patient encounters annually. Bamboo Health does not publish a public developer API; integrations are delivered through EHR workflows and partner/state programs. Security posture is documented in a public Trust Center (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF, HIPAA, NIST 800-53).

providers.name: Cleardata
providers.description: ClearDATA is healthcare's dedicated cloud security, compliance, and operations partner, helping providers, payers, health-tech software companies, medical device makers, and life sciences organizations build and run on AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud in a HIPAA- and HITRUST-aligned way. Its offering spans Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) with 300+ healthcare-specific safeguards, Managed Detection & Response (MDR), automated Cloud Compliance, and Cloud Operations, delivered through the CyberHealth platform and managed/professional services. ClearDATA is an AWS Level 1 MSSP and Microsoft Gold Partner, and maps controls to HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST, ISO, PCI, and GDPR. ClearDATA is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; ClearDATA does not publish a public developer API or portal.

providers.name: Latent Health
providers.description: Latent Health (branded "Latent") is an enterprise pharmacy intelligence company that applies a clinical agentic engine to the medication-access workflow for hospital and health-system pharmacy teams. The platform spans four stages — Identify (care-gap detection, eligibility screening, site-of-care routing), Access (prior authorization, clinical review, appeal generation, benefit routing, payer outreach), Capture (340B eligibility auditing, leakage analytics, financial dashboards), and Engage (patient outreach, queue management, outcomes analytics). It ingests patient charts and EHR data, claims, payer policies, and drug labels, and is described as chart-native and EHR-agnostic across Epic and Cerner. The company reports deployment across 50+ health systems covering 2M+ patients annually, and raised an $80M Series A led by Spark Capital and Transformation Capital. Latent Health publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs as of this profile; it is an enterprise platform sold to health systems, and its public surface is limited to marketing, case studies, press, and a Vanta-hosted trust center.

providers.name: ABILITY Network (Inovalon)
providers.description: ABILITY Network is a healthcare SaaS business acquired by Inovalon in 2018 and now delivered as part of the cloud-based Inovalon ONE Platform. It provides US healthcare providers with software for medical billing and claims management, eligibility verification, revenue cycle management, clinical quality reporting, patient access, and workforce/staffing and care coordination. Inovalon pairs these provider-facing applications with large national datasets and analytics to support data-driven healthcare across payers, providers, pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations. Developer access to Inovalon ONE APIs is offered through the authenticated Inovalon developer portal at developer.inovalonone.com, which exposes sandbox, staging, and live environments.

providers.name: Framewise Health
providers.description: Framewise Health is an AI-native patient engagement platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts a patient's medical records into personalized, clinically-reviewed educational videos. The platform pulls patient data from electronic health records over any FHIR R4 endpoint, generates discharge and treatment-adherence education tailored to the individual using institutional protocols and drug-information databases, and delivers it by SMS in 75+ languages with no app and no login. It then tracks patient comprehension in real time, giving care teams engagement data to flag which patients need follow-up. Framewise integrates with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), Athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks, and NextGen, and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant with an AWS BAA and end-to-end encryption. It targets hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and private clinics seeking to improve patient outcomes and medication adherence.

providers.name: Allara
providers.description: Allara Health is a virtual women's healthcare platform focused on complex hormonal, metabolic, and gynecological conditions such as PCOS, insulin resistance, endometriosis, thyroid disorders, menopause, and PMDD. Serving more than 85,000 patients across 45 states and D.C., Allara connects members with board-certified OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, women's health nurse practitioners, and registered dietitians for virtual consultations, advanced hormonal and metabolic lab testing, personalized treatment plans, and ongoing care coordination. The company operates consumer-facing web and patient portal applications; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as an index-ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Allara Health
providers.description: Allara Health is a telehealth platform specializing in women's hormonal, metabolic, and gynecological health. Founded by Rachel Blank following her own PCOS diagnosis, Allara connects patients with dedicated multidisciplinary care teams of board-certified physicians, OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, nurse practitioners, and registered dietitians who deliver personalized treatment through virtual visits. The platform treats complex conditions including PCOS, insulin resistance, endometriosis, thyroid disorders, fertility concerns, and other metabolic and endocrine issues, combining medical care, nutrition counseling, advanced testing, lifestyle support, and medication when appropriate. Allara accepts most insurance plans and offers self-pay options.
