Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; Allara is a consumer telehealth service with no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Aumet
providers.description: Aumet is a MENA-based healthtech company building an AI-first procurement and pharmacy operating system for healthcare. Its platform connects pharmaceutical manufacturers, distributors, and pharmacies through a B2B marketplace and a suite of pharmacy software: Pulse (point-of-sale, inventory, and smart reordering for individual pharmacies), Chain (multi-branch pharmacy management), and Enterprise (solutions for government health systems and hospitals). The platform adds AI-powered demand forecasting, procurement automation, price transparency, and analytics, and reports serving 12,000+ pharmacies and 1,000+ suppliers across Jordan, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia with over $1B in gross merchandise value and millions of transactions annually. Aumet is backed by 500 Global and Techstars.

providers.name: Backpack Healthcare
providers.description: Backpack Healthcare is a virtual (telehealth) pediatric and family mental health provider delivering therapy, psychiatry, and medication management for children, tweens, teens, young adults, and adults. It offers age-based care (Littles 4-10, Tweens & Teens 11-17, Young Adults 18+, and Adults) across concerns including ADHD, anxiety, autism spectrum disorder, depression, OCD, maternal mental health, and substance use, alongside a consumer Self Care / Care Companion mobile app. Backpack partners with health plans, schools, health systems, and community and government agencies to expand access to youth behavioral health, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Big Sky Health
providers.description: Big Sky Health (now operating as Zero Longevity Science, Inc.) is a Bozeman, Montana consumer digital-health company best known for Zero, one of the most popular intermittent-fasting and nutrition-tracking mobile apps. Zero combines a fasting timer, photo-based meal and protein logging, a personalized Protein Score, and water-intake tracking to help users manage body composition and adopt science-backed longevity practices. The company runs as a direct-to-consumer mobile subscription business (Zero Plus) on iOS and Android. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer program. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Trinity Ventures portfolio company awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Caliber Fitness
providers.description: Caliber Fitness, Inc. is a consumer strength-training and fitness-coaching company behind the Caliber: Strength Training app (iOS and Android). Caliber combines data-driven resistance-training and nutrition programming, a library of 600+ exercises, workout tracking, and one-on-one video coaching from certified personal trainers across free, Caliber Plus, and Premium Coaching tiers. Founded by Justin Fauci and Chris Muir, the company is backed by Trinity Ventures. Caliber operates as a consumer mobile app and coaching service; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. This profile tracks its public web, legal, and membership surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Calibrate
providers.description: Calibrate is a telehealth metabolic-health and weight-loss company that pairs clinician-prescribed GLP-1 medications with 1:1 video coaching and a science-backed educational curriculum to help members improve metabolic health and achieve sustainable weight loss. Programs are sold directly to individuals (from $199/month) and through employer benefits. Calibrate delivers its service through consumer web and iOS mobile apps rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks the company's public web and account surface. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Ezra
providers.description: Ezra (Ezra AI, Inc.) is a preventive-health company offering full-body MRI and CT cancer-screening scans directly to consumers. Its screening service scans up to 13 organs in as little as 22 minutes to detect early signs of cancer and hundreds of other conditions without harmful radiation, with plans spanning a full-body MRI, MRI with spine, a comprehensive skeletal/neurological MRI, and heart and lung CT scans, plus couples pricing and locations across the United States. Ezra was surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp; this profile is a consumer healthcare company with no public developer API, and was enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline against its public web surface.

providers.name: Fightcamp
providers.description: FightCamp is a consumer connected-fitness company that sells an at-home boxing and kickboxing training system combining physical equipment (a free-standing bag, quick-wrap gloves, and Bluetooth motion-tracking punch trackers) with a subscription app of on-demand classes led by professional fighters. The trackers use motion sensors and AI to measure punch output, speed, and workout stats, syncing to a member app and customer dashboard for progress tracking. FightCamp is a direct-to-consumer hardware-plus-membership business (backed by IVP) and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, commerce, support, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Headlight
providers.description: Headlight is a US mental health services company delivering teletherapy, in-person therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through a clinician-centered care model. Founded by Drs. Manish Sheth and Shashita Inamdar, it helps patients move from initial interest to a well-matched therapist or prescriber with less friction, treating conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, trauma, OCD, panic disorder, postpartum depression, and insomnia. Headlight is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Cross, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Kaiser, Moda) and operates across Alaska, California, Colorado, Oregon, Texas, and Washington. The company raised $18M led by Matrix and EPIC Ventures. This is a consumer clinical services provider with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Headspace
providers.description: Headspace is a global mental health platform offering consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep content alongside Headspace Care (formerly Ginger) — on-demand coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — and Headspace EAP. The B2B business (Headspace for Organizations) serves 4,000+ employers, health plans, and consultants in 190+ countries with a stratified care model (AI companion Ebb, coaches, therapists, psychiatrists). Integration surfaces for enterprise customers — eligibility file feeds, SSO, SCIM, benefit-platform connectors — are delivered under enterprise contracts and are not exposed via a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve partner onboarding.

providers.name: Homage
providers.description: Homage is a Singapore-headquartered holistic health and caregiving platform that connects families with screened, professional caregivers, nurses, and therapists to deliver personal care, home nursing procedures, rehabilitation, and health services where people live. Founded in 2016, Homage operates across Singapore, Malaysia, and Australia through consumer mobile apps and a care-management operations platform, offering flexible on-demand and recurring visits, care assessments, custom care plans, and teleconsultations for conditions such as dementia, stroke recovery, and post-surgical care. Homage does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web properties and probed domain security.

providers.name: Hormona
providers.description: Hormona is a women's hormonal-health company founded in 2020 by Karolina Lofqvist and Jasmine Tagesson, with offices in London, UK and Stockholm, Sweden. It builds a hormone-tracking mobile app together with an at-home hormone monitor and urine-test kits that users scan with a phone camera to get real-time, quantitative hormone results without a lab visit. The app uses AI to learn each user's patterns and predict when PMS or period symptoms are likely, offering 30+ tools to manage hormonal symptoms and supporting women from their first period through perimenopause and menopause. Hormona is distributed on the App Store and Google Play and is used by women in 185+ countries. It is a direct-to-consumer product with no public developer API program.

providers.name: Joinmidi
providers.description: Joinmidi (Midi Health) is a virtual care company for women in midlife, providing insurance-covered telehealth from women's health specialists across all 50 states. Its clinicians deliver personalized, evidence-based care for perimenopause and menopause plus weight management, sexual wellness, mood, sleep, hair and skin health, and cancer survivorship, backed by custom prescription medications (Midi Custom Rx) and a targeted supplement line. Midi is NCQA accredited, works with major insurance plans, and partners with health systems and Fortune 100 employers as a covered benefit. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: kelaHealth
providers.description: kelaHealth is a healthcare AI company that improves surgical outcomes through its Surgical Intelligence Service, an AI-enabled API delivering patient-specific predictive insights at critical decision points across the perioperative process. Models trained on millions of surgical procedures predict individual patient risk across nine major complication categories, identify modifiable factors, and recommend stratified interventions tailored to hospital standards. The service integrates into existing medtech and healthcare software applications using EHR, robotic, and social-determinants-of-health data to help providers improve growth, efficiency, quality, and safety. kelaHealth is HIPAA compliant and backed by Techstars. It does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; its API is delivered through partner integrations.

providers.name: Meditopia
providers.description: Meditopia is a holistic mental-wellbeing platform founded in 2017 that blends psychology, technology, and wellness to support the mental, emotional, and physical health of individuals and organizations. For consumers it ships a meditation and mindfulness mobile app (sleep programs, guided meditations, personalized assessments, self-guided content) available in nine-plus languages and used by 40+ million people across 60 countries. For organizations it offers Meditopia for Work: a modern Employee Assistance Program (EAP), 1-on-1 expert sessions, a WellnessPass benefits platform, online trainings, and Soul, an AI wellbeing coach. Meditopia is backed by Creandum. The company operates a consumer mobile app and a B2B web platform; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: MTN OPS
providers.description: MTN OPS is an American-owned outdoor performance nutrition and lifestyle brand founded in 2014 and headquartered in Fruit Heights, Utah. The company develops, manufactures, and sells energy and nutrition supplements (pre-workout, protein, hydration, creatine, and energy bars) alongside apparel and gear for hunters, tactical professionals, military, and outdoor athletes, running a "Conquer Hunger" program that donates one meal for every order placed. MTN OPS is a direct-to-consumer, internet-first retailer operating on the Shopify platform and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes no bespoke developer API; the only machine-readable surfaces on its domain are the Shopify New Customer Accounts OIDC discovery documents and a Shopify-generated agent-commerce llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Norwest portfolio lead and enriched from the provider's live public surface.

providers.name: Ophelia Health
providers.description: Ophelia is a telehealth company providing private, evidence-based medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder from home. Founded in 2019 by Zack Gray and Mattan Griffel and headquartered in New York City, Ophelia connects patients with licensed clinicians for video visits, prescribes Suboxone (buprenorphine + naloxone) sent to a local pharmacy, and provides ongoing care-team support seven days a week. The subscription service accepts most major insurance plans, including Medicaid, and is licensed to provide care across 49 states and Washington, D.C. Ophelia is a direct-to-consumer clinical service and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner API program; this profile captures its public web presence and domain security posture.

providers.name: Pear Suite
providers.description: Pear Suite is a care management platform built for community health workers, care navigators, doulas, and community-based organizations, describing itself as an operating system for community-based work. The platform provides custom assessments and care pathways, goal and outcome tracking, patient communication over phone, SMS, and encrypted email, client and population-level analytics, and billing and claims integration, connecting community health initiatives with health plans and health systems. Pear Suite reports serving 2,500+ community workers across 300+ organizations nationwide.

providers.name: Physiohome
providers.description: Physiohome, operating as Ameen (رعاية أمين), is a Saudi Arabia-based, tech-enabled provider of home rehabilitation and physical therapy services. Founded in 2021 out of a Ministry of Health sector accelerator, the company delivers physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, nutritional therapy, and personal training for adults and seniors in patients' homes and rehabilitation centers. Its platform manages the full care journey from assessment and treatment planning through session tracking, provider equipping, and reporting, with 100+ active service providers operating across nine cities and a wider network of 700+ providers. Ameen offers iOS and Android apps, an online booking flow, and a patient portal, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. It is a portfolio company of Sanabil 500 (500 Global) and Saudi Venture Capital.

providers.name: Prenuvo
providers.description: Prenuvo operates a preventive healthcare screening service built around whole-body MRI imaging paired with blood biomarker panels and personalized results reviews. A single scan captures on the order of a billion data points while screening for hundreds of conditions across major organ systems, without radiation or contrast agents, and completes in under an hour. Blood panels measure 80+ biomarkers tied to inflammation, hormone levels, and metabolic health, with optional advanced imaging for brain, heart, and body composition. Prenuvo runs clinics across the US, Canada, Australia, and the UK, and works with research institutions including Mount Sinai, UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Penn. Prenuvo does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Roger
providers.description: Roger (operated by Sanos Services GmbH, Berlin, Germany) is a B2B SaaS practice-management platform for dental clinics. It layers automation and AI onto existing German dental practice-management systems (PVS) such as CGM Z1, Charly, Dampsoft, Evident and Dento Office, adding patient recall, digital intake forms, WhatsApp/SMS communication, AI-assisted documentation with billing-position capture, digital treatment-plan signing, factoring with default protection and instant payout, and outsourced ZMV/reception staffing. The product is DSGVO/GDPR-compliant and hosted in Germany. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network via VC-portfolio discovery, Roger publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Rupa Health
providers.description: Rupa Health (now a Fullscript company) is a healthcare platform that lets functional and root-cause medicine practitioners order, track, and receive results from specialty and functional lab tests across hundreds of lab companies through a single unified dashboard. It provides a lab test catalog, patient result portals, practitioner ordering and billing, phlebotomy coordination, and educational resources (Rupa University, the Root Cause Medicine podcast, and a lab reference guide). Rupa integrates with a range of EHR/EMR systems used by independent practitioners but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Seer
providers.description: Seer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SEER) is a Redwood City, California life-sciences company pioneering proteomics, the large-scale study of proteins. Its Proteograph Product Suite pairs engineered nanoparticles with automated sample preparation and mass spectrometry to profile tens of thousands of proteins across biological samples at scale, and its cloud-based Proteograph Analysis System (PAS) software processes and interprets the resulting proteomic data for pharmaceutical, biopharma, and academic research. Seer exposes no public developer API; its software surface is the login-gated PAS platform delivered to customers of the Proteograph suite.

providers.name: Spill
providers.description: Spill is a UK-based employee assistance programme (EAP) that delivers mental health support to employees directly inside the tools teams already use, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. The platform offers same-day, message-based counselling, structured multi-session therapy courses for specific mental health conditions, drop-in group sessions, manager mental-health training, and self-guided wellbeing content, all through a single subscription. Spill serves over 600 companies on month-to-month terms and is backed by Seedcamp. It is a B2B software-as-a-service wellbeing product rather than an API provider; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been published.

providers.name: Summer Health
providers.description: Summer Health is a pediatric health company offering families fast, board-certified pediatric care. Its flagship consumer service provides comprehensive at-home blood work for children ages 8-18 (one blood draw covering 74 biomarkers) reviewed by board-certified pediatricians over video, alongside text-based urgent-care messaging with pediatric clinicians. The service is HSA/FSA eligible and LegitScript-approved. Summer Health is a consumer-facing telehealth offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API documentation, or third-party integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Teal Health
providers.description: Teal Health, Inc. is a women's health company behind the Teal Wand, the first and only FDA-approved at-home self-collection device for cervical cancer screening in the United States. Its end-to-end telehealth service pairs the self-collection kit with virtual Teal medical providers who prescribe the kit, review Roche cobas HPV lab results, and support patients aged 25-65 throughout the screening experience. Now available in all 50 states, Teal Health runs a HIPAA-compliant direct-to-consumer telehealth platform and is a consumer of third-party healthcare APIs (Healthie for scheduling/telehealth, Candid for billing) rather than a publisher of a public developer API.

providers.name: Terapify
providers.description: Terapify is an online therapy platform for the Spanish-speaking market, connecting individuals in Mexico and Latin America with certified psychologists for private, secure video-call sessions. Founded in 2019 and backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator, the platform matches patients to therapists via a therapeutic-affinity test, offers individual and couples therapy, parent orientation, and workplace mental-health programs for companies, plus mindfulness, yoga, and breathing resources. It operates as a consumer web and mobile (iOS/Android) product and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Vitrue Health
providers.description: Vitrue Health is a London-based, Techstars-backed digital health company providing an AI-powered musculoskeletal (MSK) and workplace ergonomics platform. Its VIDA product uses camera-based AI assessments to automate Display Screen Equipment (DSE) compliance, deliver personalized pain-management pathways, and give employers analytics through a VIDA Co-Pilot dashboard, reporting an average 34% reduction in MSK pain. The platform integrates with HR systems, learning management systems, and SSO/provisioning identity providers, but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Clivi
providers.description: Clivi is Mexico's largest digital clinic for diabetes and obesity care, delivering fully online telehealth treatment that combines endocrinologists, internists, nutritionists, and psychologists with continuous glucose monitoring and GLP-1 medications (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Saxenda, Rybelsus). Founded in 2020 and based in Mexico City, Clivi serves patients nationwide through WhatsApp-based virtual care, home medication delivery via its Farmacia Clivi digital pharmacy, and tiered treatment plans (Clivi Pro, Plus, Total, and Zero). Backed by 500 Global and other investors, Clivi operates as a consumer healthtech service; it publishes no public developer API, but does expose an llms.txt content index for AI agents.

providers.name: Ferrum Health
providers.description: Ferrum Health is a healthcare AI governance company whose AI Governance Suite lets health systems deploy, validate, orchestrate, and monitor clinical AI models securely behind their own firewall, without protected health information leaving the health system. The vendor-neutral, privately deployed platform integrates once with existing EMR, PACS, and worklist infrastructure, then routes every clinical AI model — FDA-cleared, CE-marked, open-source, or homegrown — through a single secure path via its Deployment Fabric, curates 60+ applications in its Model Hub across radiology, cardiology, oncology, neurology, and musculoskeletal specialties, and continuously links predictions, ground truth, and outcomes for bias and drift detection through its Observability Lens. It is SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR aligned, and is used by Sutter Health, Carle Health, and 250+ sites.

providers.name: Grow Therapy
providers.description: Grow Therapy is a mental-health platform that connects individuals with licensed therapists and prescribers, offering virtual and in-person talk therapy plus medication management in one insurance-integrated experience. The company operates a two-sided marketplace: a client-facing product for finding, booking, and paying for care (with insurance verification and an average session cost around $21 for covered clients) and a provider portal that gives clinicians scheduling, billing, telehealth, and practice-management tooling. Grow also partners with employers, physicians, and payors on B2B mental-health access. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; Grow Therapy publishes a public Statuspage but does not expose a public developer API, so this profile captures its company identity, operational transparency, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: HealthEngine
providers.description: HealthEngine is Australia's largest consumer healthcare marketplace and patient-engagement platform, founded in 2006 and headquartered in Perth, Western Australia. Its consumer app and website let millions of Australians search a national directory of primary-care providers and book, manage, and attend appointments (including telehealth) across GP, dental, allied-health, and specialist practices. For practices, HealthEngine sells a SaaS suite - GP Complete, Patient Connect, Online Booking, Appointment Reminders and Recalls, Featured Listings, online payments, patient reviews, and Scripts - that plugs into the practice's existing software. It maintains private, real-time integrations into 25+ Australian practice management systems (Best Practice / Bp Premier, MedicalDirector Pracsoft, Zedmed, Cliniko, Genie, Gentu, Medtech, Nookal, PracSuite, Dental4Windows, and others) so appointment availability and bookings sync directly with the front desk. Home market is Australia. HealthEngine does NOT publish a public developer portal, REST OpenAPI, or HL7 FHIR endpoint - its API surface is a set of gated, partner-only PMS integrations rather than a self-serve developer program, so this profile is an honest identity stub with no public machine-readable contract to harvest.

providers.name: Almanac Health
providers.description: Almanac Health is a clinical AI company building a research-validated clinical decision support platform, delivered as Almanac Chat, that brings specialist-grade, evidence-based answers to clinicians at the point of care. Founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, MD, the platform is designed to work within existing electronic health record (EHR) workflows, is governed by institutional controls, and is grounded in peer-reviewed research rather than pharmaceutical promotion. In April 2026 the company raised a $10 million seed round led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web, trust, and security surface; Almanac Health does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Blackrock Neurotech
providers.description: Blackrock Neurotech is a Salt Lake City, Utah based neurotechnology company that designs and manufactures implantable brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and the research instrumentation around them. Its platform pairs Utah Array microelectrode arrays and the next-generation Neuralace interface with the NeuroPort, Cerebus and CerePlex Direct neural signal processors, the CereStim stimulation system, and the Central software suite for acquisition, visualization and offline spike sorting. The company reports more than 19 years of human clinical study, 1,000+ research institutions served and 2,000+ published studies using its hardware. Blackrock does not publish a public web API: its programmatic surface is a set of device and file-format libraries distributed as downloads and GitHub source (cbSDK C++ API, cbMEX MATLAB API, CereStim API, brPY/brpylib Python data loader, and the NPMK MATLAB toolkit). Enrichment probing on 2026-08-02 found no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP, agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known/ discovery surface on any Blackrock host.

providers.name: DeepScribe
providers.description: DeepScribe is a San Francisco, California ambient AI medical scribe company that automates clinical documentation and coding for specialty healthcare providers. Founded in 2017 (incorporated 2019) by Matthew Ko, Kairui Zeng, and Akilesh Bapu, DeepScribe captures the natural conversation between clinician and patient and produces structured clinical notes inside the provider's existing EHR workflow. The platform is HIPAA-compliant and is deployed across more than 1,500 healthcare organizations, with reported traction of 8 million+ visits captured and a 99.92% note-satisfaction rating. Core products include the AI Medical Scribe (ambient documentation), SmartPrep (pre-visit intelligence), AI Coding (E/M, ICD-10, and HCC automation), Customization Studio (provider-specific note personalization), and DeepScribe Assist (point-of-care insights). DeepScribe ships bi-directional EHR integrations with Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, AdvancedMD, drchrono, ModMed, Flatiron (OncoEMR), Ontada (iKnowMed Generation 2), and Objective Medical Systems, with a focused practice in oncology, cardiology, gastroenterology, neurology, orthopedics, urology, and value-based care. The company partners with AWS, Anthropic, Deloitte, and Panda Health for infrastructure, model, and go-to-market support. DeepScribe is sold as enterprise SaaS through a contact-sales motion; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and authentication into the clinician workspace happens through canvas.deepscribe.ai.

providers.name: Octave Bioscience
providers.description: Octave Bioscience is a precision neurology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, that develops blood-based multi-protein biomarker tests for chronic neurological disease. Its commercially available Octave Multiple Sclerosis Disease Activity (MSDA) Test measures a panel of serum proteins to produce a quantitative disease activity score used alongside clinical and imaging assessment, and is available across the United States through a strategic collaboration with Quest Diagnostics. The company is also developing a Multiple Sclerosis Disease Progression (MSDP) test and a Parkinson's disease biomarker assay supported by a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant. Octave publishes a public trust center documenting HITRUST, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA and GDPR posture, but operates no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Somethings
providers.description: Somethings is a teen mental health support platform that connects adolescents with Certified Peer Specialist Mentors through a mobile app for iOS and Android. Rather than traditional therapy or AI chatbots, teens can call or chat anytime with trained mentors who have personal lived experience overcoming challenges like anxiety, depression, self-harm, eating disorders, and ADHD, backed by clinical supervision. The service is HIPAA-compliant and sold to health plans, insurers, employers, and directly to parents. Somethings is a venture-backed company in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer/clinical mobile product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Virgin Pulse
providers.description: Virgin Pulse is a corporate health and employee wellbeing platform that in 2024 merged with HealthComp and rebranded as Personify Health, operating today at personifyhealth.com. The company delivers a personalized health platform that unites wellbeing, healthcare navigation and advocacy, benefits administration, third-party administration (TPA), and rewards into a single employee experience for enterprises, health plans, and health systems. Integration with Personify Health is handled through an authentication-gated developer portal (developer.personifyhealth.com) and a partner marketplace (marketplace.personifyhealth.com); there is no publicly documented, open API specification. This profile was seeded as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched from the company's live public surface (llms.txt, status page, developer portal, and DNS/TLS probes).

providers.name: Camber
providers.description: Camber is a healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) and medical billing software platform purpose-built for specialty care providers, including ABA (applied behavior analysis) therapy, physical therapy, and ENT and allergy clinics. The platform automates the full claims lifecycle — creation and submission, pre-submission scrubbing and eligibility verification, payment posting and reconciliation, and denial management and prevention — using a rules engine and AI trained on billions of dollars in real claims data, combined with human review where judgment matters. Founded in 2021 (Y Combinator W21, rebranded from Juniper Behavioral Health to Camber), the New York-based company is backed by Craft Ventures, a16z, and Y Combinator, and processes over a million claims annually for hundreds of specialty care providers across all 50 states.

providers.name: Collective Medical
providers.description: Collective Medical is a full-continuum, real-time care collaboration network for healthcare, connecting hospitals, health systems, post-acute providers, health plans, and payers so care teams can coordinate around complex, high-risk, and vulnerable patients across the entire patient journey. Founded in Utah and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Kleiner Perkins, the platform is known for its real-time event notifications, ADT-based care-coordination alerts, and shared clinical insights used by emergency departments and care-management teams. Collective Medical was acquired by PointClickCare in 2020 and is now fully integrated into PointClickCare; its former developer, login, support, and legal surfaces are served through PointClickCare properties (developer.pointclickcare.com and pointclickcare.com). This profile tracks the Collective Medical brand within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Juniper Behavioral Health
providers.description: Juniper Behavioral Health (now operating as Camber, camber.health) is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) software company for specialty and behavioral health providers. Founded in 2021 and backed by a16z, Y Combinator, and Craft Ventures, the company automates medical billing, claims processing, denial management, and payment analytics so behavioral and specialty clinicians (ABA, PT, ENT, allergy) can collect more from insurance and spend less time on administrative overhead. Their platform is built on AI systems trained on more than $2.5B in claims data. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from the public Camber website; the company exposes a customer web application (app.camber.health) and a published responsible-disclosure policy but no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Prax Health
providers.description: Prax Health is a healthcare platform that helps nurse practitioners launch and grow their own independent practices. It provides an all-in-one back office that handles business formation, regulatory and clinical compliance, medical billing, insurance credentialing, an integrated EHR, and ongoing practice consulting. The company's stated mission is to put healthcare back in the hands of providers by removing the administrative and operational burden that keeps clinicians from practicing independently. Prax Health is a venture-backed company (Canaan Partners) and operates a consumer/clinician web application rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it exposes no public API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: 28 labs
providers.description: 28labs Inc. operates She's Well (sheswell.co), a consumer fertility-care platform that bundles egg freezing, fertility testing, IVF coordination, clinic visits, labs, medications, and concierge nurse support into a single transparent subscription plan starting at $249/month over up to 60 months. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a business-to-consumer digital-health service with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Aledade
providers.description: Aledade is a physician-led public benefit corporation and national leader in value-based care, partnering with independent primary care practices, community health centers, and health systems. It pairs data analytics, guided clinical workflows, integrated care solutions, and payer contracts to help primary care organizations succeed in accountable care organizations (ACOs) and value-based payment models, improving patient outcomes while supporting the business sustainability of independent practices. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of gv, ivp, and lightspeed-venture-partners.

providers.name: Aluna
providers.description: Aluna is a digital respiratory health company behind an FDA-cleared, portable Bluetooth spirometer and companion mobile app that let people with asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis measure lung function (FEV1) at home and share the results with their care teams. The platform pairs a hospital-grade sensor with a gamified app and machine-learning analytics to encourage proper technique, track symptoms, triggers, and medications, and surface trends that help clinicians intervene before an exacerbation. Founded by Charvi Shetty and Inderjit Jutla out of UC Berkeley's bioengineering program, Aluna raised a $15.3M Series B and is a Matrix Partners portfolio company; the product is now operated under Huma Therapeutics. Aluna publishes consumer, clinical-provider, and clinical-trial surfaces but no public developer API.

providers.name: Becton Dickinson
providers.description: Becton Dickinson (BD) is a global medical technology company that develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices, instrument systems, and reagents. In October 2025, BD launched the BD Incada Connected Care Platform, an AI-enabled, cloud-based platform built on AWS that unifies data from nearly 3 million connected BD devices including infusion pumps, patient monitors, and pharmacy robotics. BD also produces the Pyxis medication management system and integrates with EMRs via HL7 FHIR standards for clinical data exchange.

providers.name: BillionToOne
providers.description: BillionToOne is a molecular diagnostics company using proprietary single-molecule Quantitative Counting Template (QCT) technology to detect disease at the DNA level from cell-free DNA. Its Unity prenatal screening suite (Unity Complete, Unity Confirm, and Unity fetal antigen tests) delivers non-invasive prenatal testing from maternal blood at nine weeks, and its Northstar oncology line (Northstar Select and Northstar Response) provides liquid-biopsy therapy selection and real-time treatment-response monitoring. BillionToOne integrates with electronic medical records through a collaboration with Epic and delivers results through its provider and patient portals. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Birches Health
providers.description: Birches Health is a fully virtual behavioral addiction treatment provider specializing in gambling disorder and related compulsive behaviors such as sports betting, day trading, video gaming, and pornography. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, the company delivers confidential online care from licensed gambling counselors, peer mentors, financial coaches, and group therapy across all 50 states. Birches Health partners with 18+ state governments that have legalized sports betting and 100+ national insurance plans (including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna, and Blue Cross Blue Shield) so most clients pay $0-25 per session, with a core program completed in about 12 weeks. The company has raised approximately $20M from AlleyCorp, General Catalyst, and Will Ventures. Birches Health does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Caer
providers.description: Caer, Inc. is the company behind YUMI (helloyumi.com), a direct-to-consumer children's nutrition brand that makes nutritionally-engineered organic snacks for babies, toddlers, and kids. The product line includes toddler bars, squeezable smoothies-to-go, freeze-dried smoothie melts, super/breakfast bars, and soft-baked cookies, all formulated as function-first, nutrient-dense, organic, dairy-free, gluten-free, and clean-label. YUMI sells through its own WooCommerce storefront, Amazon, and select retail, offering one-time purchases and recurring subscription memberships. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was seeded as a venture-portfolio stub; it is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no first-party public developer API, so most API-artifact scoring dimensions are not applicable.

providers.name: Fort
providers.description: Fort is a Y Combinator (W26) hardware startup building a screenless wearable that automatically tracks strength training for people who care about longevity. Founded by three former Tesla engineers, the device uses heart rate and motion sensing to detect gym sessions, workout classes, sleep, and recovery without requiring the wearer to manually log reps, sets, or exercises, then delivers actionable feedback on how lifestyle factors affect strength progress. Fort is styled as jewelry rather than performance gear, ships in three finishes with 7+ day battery life, and pairs with Fort Foundations, an expert-led training program built around core movement patterns. The product is currently available for pre-order and has no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public web and commercial presence.

providers.name: Hykso
providers.description: Hykso, Inc. is the company behind FightCamp, an at-home boxing and kickboxing training system that pairs a free-standing bag, quick-wrap gloves, and wireless motion-tracking punch trackers with an on-demand library of trainer-led workouts. The Hykso punch trackers began as standalone wearable sensors that measure punch count, speed, and output for boxers and gyms, and now power FightCamp's real-time performance stats and workout scoring. This profile is a company stub in the API Evangelist network; Hykso/FightCamp is a direct-to-consumer connected-fitness brand and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Irhythmtech
providers.description: iRhythm Technologies is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: IRTC) digital healthcare company specializing in ambulatory cardiac monitoring for the detection and management of heart arrhythmias. Its Zio service pairs a wearable single-lead ECG biosensor patch (Zio monitor and Zio AT) with FDA-cleared AI/deep-learning algorithms, qualified cardiac technician verification, and cloud-based data analytics to produce end-of-wear diagnostic reports for clinicians. The platform includes the ZioSuite clinician portal for report interpretation and patient management, the MyZio patient app for symptom logging and education, EHR integration, and telehealth workflows. iRhythm was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal; enrichment is limited to public identity, trust, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Naluri
providers.description: Naluri is a digital health and corporate wellness platform operating across Southeast Asia. It delivers Employee Assistance Programmes, chronic disease management (mental health, obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and cholesterol), health coaching and consultations, performance workshops, and Mental Health First Aid training for employers, insurers, and individuals. The company reports serving over one million members and 200-plus companies, and states it is certified for HIPAA, GDPR, and ISO/IEC 27001. No public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Pluto
providers.description: Pluto (Pluto Health, trypluto.com now pluto.health) is an AI-powered clinical intelligence and care-delivery platform that unifies fragmented health data from roughly 90% of US health systems. It aggregates medical records, insurance data, and social determinants of health, then applies AI-driven clinical intelligence to surface care gaps, coordinate preventive care, screenings, vaccines and at-home lab testing, and match patients to clinical trials. Pluto offers turnkey, white-label, or API-based deployment of its clinical operations. It is backed by Sierra Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: SAVA
providers.description: SAVA (sava.health) is a health-monitoring company developing a minimally invasive, continuous multi-molecule biosensor worn just beneath the skin. The platform is designed to capture real-time molecular data - glucose, lactate, ketones, sodium, histamine, urea, alcohol, and cortisol - and surface it through a connected mobile app, aiming to shift healthcare toward preventative monitoring and personal wellness. The company is early stage and pre-launch, operating a waiting-list model for early access to its device rather than a public product. It publishes no first-party developer API or health-data API; its marketing site is built on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint and a published llms.txt for agentic access to public site content only. Backed by Balderton Capital.

providers.name: Tendo Systems
providers.description: Tendo (Tendo Systems) is a healthcare technology company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith, building software, analytics, and healthcare marketplaces on a next-generation platform that connects patients, clinicians, and providers across the fragmented care experience. Its application suite spans Tendo Insights (clinical quality and financial analytics), Tendo QDI (clinical documentation integrity and workflow optimization), Tendo Outreach (targeted patient engagement), and Care Connect, a shoppable bundled-procedure marketplace built on its 2023 acquisition of MDsave. Tendo does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or open developer portal; its documentation and support portals are gated behind authentication. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity and security posture.

providers.name: TMRW Life Sciences *
providers.description: TMRW Life Sciences is a medical technology company that builds the world's first and only FDA-cleared automated platform for the safe management and storage of frozen eggs and embryos used in IVF and fertility treatment. Its cryo-storage hardware combines robotic specimen handling with digital tracking, chain-of-custody monitoring, and real-time visibility for fertility clinics and their patients, replacing manual, paper-based handling of irreplaceable reproductive tissue. Deployed at clinic networks including CCRM Fertility, Pinnacle Fertility, RFC, and IVIRMA North America. TMRW is a private company backed by GV (Google Ventures). It publishes a Security & Trust program (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018) but does not expose a public developer portal, API, or specification surface.

providers.name: Lunabill
providers.description: LunaBill is an AI revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for hospitals, health systems, and RCM/BPO firms, built by LunaHealth Technologies, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator. A coordinated team of AI agents works the entire accounts receivable queue end to end — placing real calls to payers and waiting on hold, navigating IVR phone trees, checking payer portals (Availity, Waystar), working denials, filing appeals, and resubmitting claims — while running inside the EHR and clearinghouses a provider already uses (Epic, Cerner, GoRev, Waystar, Availity) and leaving a full audit trail on every claim. Pricing is performance based (1.5% of net collections recovered, nothing upfront). LunaBill is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type I (Type II in progress). It does not currently publish a public developer API; integration is delivered through EHR and clearinghouse connectors rather than a documented API surface.

providers.name: Nines
providers.description: Nines was a teleradiology and medical-imaging AI startup founded in 2017 and backed by Accel and 8VC (a $16.5M Series A in 2019), co-founded by CEO David Stavens. It built FDA-cleared AI algorithms — NinesAI Emergent Triage (for intracranial hemorrhage and mass effect) and NinesMeasure (a lung-nodule algorithm) — alongside a live teleradiology practice. On 2022-02-18, Sirona Medical acquired Nines' AI technology, clinical data pipeline, machine-learning engines, and key personnel, folding the FDA-cleared devices into RadOS, Sirona's cloud-native Radiology Operating System (reporter, viewer, PACS, worklist, and platform AI). The nines.com domain now redirects to sironamedical.com. There is no public developer API today; a RadOS "Amplify" SDK (TypeScript/Python, REST + streaming APIs, event subscriptions) is on Sirona's roadmap as an early-access program for design partners.

providers.name: ScreenPoint Medical
providers.description: ScreenPoint Medical is a Netherlands-based healthcare AI company, founded in 2014 by Professor Nico Karssemeijer and Professor Sir Michael Brady, that develops Transpara Breast AI for earlier detection of breast cancer in 2D (FFDM) and 3D (DBT) mammography. Transpara is vendor-agnostic, integrates into PACS and reading workflows via medical-imaging (DICOM) pipelines rather than a public developer API, and is FDA cleared (K241831, K232096) and CE marked (0344). The product is used in over 200 clinics across 25+ countries and is backed by three randomized controlled trials (including MASAI in The Lancet). The company is backed by Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: no public developer/API surface exists, but real security-disclosure and compliance posture were captured.

providers.name: Bold
providers.description: Bold (Age Bold, Inc.) is an AI-enabled healthy-aging company founded in 2019 by Amanda Rees and Hari Arul that combines age-friendly virtual care with senior-focused exercise and nutrition programs for Medicare members. The platform delivers personalized at-home programs — live and on-demand classes, balance and fall-prevention regimens, pain and mobility programs, nutrition coaching, and telehealth visits with clinicians — to adults 65 and older, distributed through Medicare Advantage plans, provider groups, and the CMS ACCESS program rather than sold as a developer platform. Bold reports its balance programs lower fall risk and its pain programs reduce joint pain among participating members, and states its platform is HIPAA compliant and requires no lengthy IT integration for plan partners. The company has raised roughly $27M, with a $17M Series A led by Rethink Impact alongside Andreessen Horowitz Bio + Health, Khosla Ventures, Samsung Next, GingerBread Capital, and Primetime Partners. As of this enrichment pass Bold publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or partner API surface — integrations are handled through its partnerships team.

providers.name: Hippocratic AI
providers.description: Hippocratic AI builds safety-focused generative AI agents for non-diagnostic healthcare tasks, powered by its Polaris constellation architecture. Polaris 5.0 is a multi-trillion-parameter constellation of specialized models clinically validated by U.S.-licensed clinicians. Hippocratic AI sells agents such as Nurse Co-Pilot and AI Front Door to health systems, payors, and life-sciences organizations through enterprise sales rather than a self-service public API.

providers.name: Lantum
providers.description: Lantum (formerly Network Locum, founded 2012 in Shoreditch, London) is a United Kingdom healthcare workforce-management company whose Connected Scheduling platform helps NHS primary- and secondary-care organisations build digital staff banks, manage rotas and e-rostering, run automated timesheets and payments, and fill clinical shifts from a verified network of 30,000+ locum clinicians. It serves over 2,000 primary-care organisations, GP practices, PCNs, GP federations, and integrated care systems across the UK. Lantum is a practice-management and workforce platform rather than a clinical-data interoperability vendor, and it does NOT publish a public developer portal, a documented REST API, or an HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement. Its product is delivered through a gated web and mobile application (lantum.com), onboarded via sales and demo request, with any system integrations (for example to GP clinical systems) handled through private partner arrangements rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Lenus eHealth
providers.description: Lenus eHealth is a Copenhagen-headquartered health and fitness technology company that builds a coaching platform for online health and fitness coaches, positioning itself as a growth partner rather than a consumer fitness app. Coaching partners run their businesses through the Lenus web dashboard and branded consumer mobile apps: client onboarding and screening, training and nutrition programming, habit and progress tracking, in-app messaging, content delivery, subscription billing and business analytics. The company also operates Lenus Academy, a certified education program for online coaches, and in the United States offers a GLP-1 weight management program delivered with independent medical partner Beluga Health. Lenus operates from 20+ offices including Copenhagen, Berlin, London, Amsterdam, Stockholm, Madrid, New York and Toronto, and is backed by EQT Ventures. The platform is closed and invitation-based: as of July 2026 Lenus publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications, and access is available only to coaching partners under a partnership agreement.

providers.name: NOCD
providers.description: NOCD is a virtual mental-health provider specializing in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Through its web and mobile applications the company matches members with licensed therapists trained in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy, delivers live video sessions, and provides between-session messaging, a peer community, and in-app therapeutic tools. NOCD is in-network with a large number of US health plans and serves children, adolescents, and adults. The product is delivered as an end-user clinical service — the company operates a private mobile/web application backend at api.treatmyocd.com but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Petsapp
providers.description: PetsApp is a veterinary client engagement and practice communication platform used by more than 1,000 veterinary practices worldwide, with millions of pets registered and millions of dollars in payments processed. It gives clinics two-way SMS and in-app messaging, appointment booking, video consultations, digital payments, wellness and health-care plan management, automated reminders, and a lightweight CRM for building client relationships. PetsApp does not publish a public developer portal or open API; API access and documentation are offered privately to technology and PIMS integration partners through its partner program, and its public docs subdomain is a Jira Service Management customer help center rather than API reference documentation.

providers.name: Stellar Sleep
providers.description: Stellar Sleep (Y Combinator S23, backed by Initialized Capital) is a mobile app that helps people with chronic insomnia sleep better using psychology rather than medication. Its personalized program is based on CBT-I (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia), the first-line treatment recommended by sleep experts, delivered through iOS and Android apps published by Merlin Collective, LLC. Started at Harvard Innovation Labs in 2021, Stellar Sleep also offers clinician and employer programs, with clinical-system integrations arranged by its team. It is a consumer digital-health product with no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface.

providers.name: Vida Health
providers.description: Vida Health is a San Francisco-based virtual care company founded in 2014 that combines an AI-powered mobile app with a national network of licensed clinicians, coaches and therapists to prevent, manage and reverse chronic cardiometabolic and behavioral health conditions including obesity, diabetes, hypertension, depression and anxiety. Vida sells a turnkey enterprise programme to employers and health plans, layering GLP-1 prescribing and clinical oversight on top of behavioral coaching, and its platform ingests real-time readings from more than 100 connected devices and consumer health apps to feed outcome reporting back to its enterprise buyers. Vida publishes no public developer portal or API documentation: the API host api.vida.com is live but returns 401 on every path, and data/EHR integration for health plans and employers is arranged through enterprise sales rather than self-service onboarding.

providers.name: WellTheory
providers.description: WellTheory is a virtual autoimmune care platform that provides whole-person support for people living with autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, pairing members with a dedicated care team for nutrition, lifestyle, and clinical guidance across more than 100 conditions. The company sells to employers and health plans as a covered benefit as well as direct to consumers, and is backed by Accel and General Catalyst. WellTheory publishes no public developer API surface today; its api.welltheory.com backend and docs are private/internal.

providers.name: Allswell
providers.description: Allswell is an online mental health platform providing virtual, trauma-informed therapy for the LGBTQ+ community. Licensed therapists with master's degrees in social work, counseling, or marriage and family therapy deliver individual telehealth sessions alongside peer support groups and skills-building resources, covering trauma, anxiety, depression, identity exploration, and relationship dynamics. Allswell serves clients in Maryland, DC, and Virginia, accepting Medicaid and major insurance plans as well as cash-pay. Backed by Techstars, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: BrightInsight
providers.description: BrightInsight is a regulated digital health platform for biopharma and medtech. Its cloud-based, microservices platform captures, transmits and analyzes data from CE-marked and FDA-regulated medical devices, combination products, apps and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in compliance with global security, privacy and regulatory requirements. The platform integrates with 400+ medical devices across 50+ manufacturers, connects to EHRs in 500+ U.S. provider networks, and is available in 48 countries. Founded in 2017 (formerly Flex Digital Health) and based in Alviso, California, BrightInsight is used by top biopharma and medtech companies to build and launch commercial regulated digital health solutions. It is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or public API; integration is delivered under managed engagements.

providers.name: Curative
providers.description: Curative is a health insurance and healthcare services company founded in 2020 that reengineered the employer-based health plan around simplicity, engagement, and cost transparency. Its fully insured and level-funded plans give members a competitive monthly premium with zero copays, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs, starting each member with a baseline visit that tailors a preventative care plan. Curative serves more than 1,200 employer clients and over 165,000 members, reached profitability, and achieved unicorn status ($1.275B valuation) following a $150M Series B round backed by DCVC. Curative operates as a HIPAA-regulated health plan; it has no public developer/API program, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity, its member/provider web surface, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Medzoomer
providers.description: Medzoomer is an on-demand prescription delivery platform that connects pharmacies, healthcare providers, and patients through a secure, HIPAA-compliant network of verified couriers. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, the company handles last-mile medication logistics, including controlled substances (Schedule II-V), with tamper-evident packaging, FDA/TSA-approved envelopes, and real-time order tracking. Pharmacies and couriers operate through dedicated web and mobile applications, and the platform is backed by Techstars, UnitedHealthcare Accelerator, and other investors. Medzoomer operates a private pharmacy integration API but publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Calo
providers.description: Calo is a food-tech company founded in Bahrain in 2019 that operates a personalized meal-subscription and delivery service. Nutritionist-designed, chef-prepared meals are portioned to each customer's health goals and lifestyle, with 80+ new meal options rotated weekly and flexible pause/cancel anytime. Built by chefs, nutritionists, and software engineers around proprietary nutritional algorithms, Calo has expanded to seven markets across the GCC and beyond (Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman), ordered through its consumer apps. Calo is backed by 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documented client SDKs.

providers.name: CareFusion (BD)
providers.description: CareFusion is a medical technology brand, acquired by BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) in 2015, best known for the Alaris infusion system and the Pyxis automated dispensing product line. CareFusion does not expose a public developer API; instead, its devices and dispensing systems interoperate with hospital EMRs and pharmacy systems over HL7 v2 messaging, smart-pump interoperability middleware, and vendor-managed integration services. The Alaris Infusion Interoperability program wirelessly transmits orders from EMRs (such as Epic and Cerner) into Alaris large-volume and syringe modules and returns infusion status back to the EMR in near real time, using the Alaris Guardrails drug library as a safety layer.

providers.name: Modern Fertility
providers.description: Modern Fertility is a women's health company offering at-home fertility and hormone testing along with pregnancy, ovulation and prenatal products. Its flagship Modern Fertility Hormone Test lets people measure reproductive hormones from home and review results with providers. The company was acquired by telehealth provider Ro and is now operated as part of Ro: modernfertility.com redirects to ro.co/fertility and the brand's products, accounts, legal terms and security program are served under the parent Ro platform. Modern Fertility exposes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a consumer health brand within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cortico
providers.description: Cortico (Cortico Health Technologies) is a Vancouver, British Columbia based healthcare connection platform, founded in 2019, that links patients, medical clinics, and health records across Canada and the United States. Its patient-engagement suite layers online booking, automated appointment reminders, secure two-way patient messaging, digital intake forms, telemedicine, specialist e-referrals, payments, and AI-driven administrative automation on top of the electronic medical records (EMRs) clinics already run — most notably a supported two-way integration with OSCAR EMR through that system's REST/SOAP web services, plus SMART on FHIR contextual launch and robotic process automation (RPA). Cortico is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and compliant with HIPAA, PIPEDA, and PHIPA. Cortico consumes EMR and FHIR interfaces rather than publishing its own public developer API: as of this review there is no public developer portal, API reference, or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and integration is delivered through a partnership and onboarding model rather than self-serve API access.

providers.name: CVS Health
providers.description: CVS Health is a Fortune 50 healthcare services and retail pharmacy company. Its core operating units include CVS Pharmacy (retail pharmacy and mail-order), CVS Caremark (pharmacy benefit management / PBM), Aetna (health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, dental and vision), MinuteClinic (walk-in clinics), Oak Street Health (primary care for Medicare patients), and Signify Health (in-home health evaluations). CVS Health does not currently operate a public developer portal or generally available REST API. Programmatic integrations with CVS Pharmacy, Caremark, and Aetna are typically established through business partnership agreements, EDI / NCPDP pharmacy networks, and HIPAA-aligned interoperability channels (e.g., FHIR endpoints exposed to qualifying healthcare partners under regulatory mandates such as the CMS Interoperability Rule). Developer-facing artifacts in this index are limited to public marketing, corporate, and digital health references.

providers.name: Field Medical
providers.description: Field Medical, Inc. is a Carlsbad, California clinical-stage cardiac electrophysiology company founded in 2022 by Dr. Steven Mickelsen to build a second-generation pulsed field ablation (PFA) platform. Its FieldForce Ablation System pairs a focal catheter design with proprietary FieldBending energy and is positioned as the first PFA system purpose-built for ventricular arrhythmia ablation, with atrial fibrillation applications in development. The company holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and a place in the FDA TAP Pilot Program for its VT indication, has published first-in-human VCAS data in Circulation, and has raised roughly $75M across Series A and Series B. Field Medical is a medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public REST/GraphQL API and no SDKs. Its only machine-readable public surface is the llms.txt and anonymous site MCP endpoint that its Wix-hosted corporate website serves.

providers.name: Gireve
providers.description: Gireve is a B2B digital platform for electric-vehicle charging and new-mobility services, connecting charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs), and EV drivers across Europe. Its interoperability hub powers EV charging roaming, clearing and transaction settlement, Plug & Charge, smart charging, and mobility data services, spanning 680,000+ connected charging points and roughly one million monthly roaming transactions across 13,000+ signed agreements. Technical integration is delivered to connected operators over an OCPI-based hub through the Connect Place B2B platform; Gireve does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: LabDoor
providers.description: Labdoor is an independent San Francisco-based supplement testing company that buys top-selling vitamins, supplements, protein powders and energy drinks off retail shelves and online stores and sends samples to FDA-registered analytical laboratories for chemical analysis of active ingredients and potential contaminants. It grades every product on Label Accuracy, Product Purity, Nutritional Value, Ingredient Safety and Projected Efficacy, then publishes the resulting rankings, scores and expert reports for free so consumers can compare products, and it funds that testing through retail sales and through Labdoor Enterprise certification and custom-testing services sold to manufacturers. Labdoor publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: Standard Practice
providers.description: Standard Practice builds voice AI for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) teams. Its AI agents place and handle outbound phone calls to insurance payers to automate administrative work — claim status follow-up, benefits verification, prior authorization, and EDI enrollment — so billing teams can scale collections and get paid more, faster. The platform is delivered as a private, login-gated web application. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Wing Venture Capital and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Tennr
providers.description: Tennr is a New York City-based healthcare technology company (founded 2021) building agentic patient-orchestration software that automates referral-based care operations for providers and health systems. Its proprietary vision-language model, RaeLM, is trained on over 100 million anonymized medical documents to read faxes, referrals, and unstructured records, then automates document classification, data extraction, patient qualification, insurance eligibility verification, and prior-authorization submission by integrating directly with existing EHR systems. Tennr processes over 10 million documents monthly and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant. It raised a $101M Series C at a $605M valuation led by IVP, with a16z, Lightspeed, GV, ICONIQ, and Foundation Capital participating. Tennr does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or specification; integrations are delivered through EHR connections and professional services.

providers.name: TherapyNotes
providers.description: TherapyNotes is a HIPAA-compliant practice management and electronic health record (EHR) platform built specifically for behavioral health - therapists, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, and group practices. It provides interactive note templates and clinical documentation, scheduling with appointment reminders, a client portal, telehealth, electronic insurance claims and ERA, credit card processing, and TherapyFuel AI tooling. As of this writing TherapyNotes does NOT expose a public or partner developer API, webhooks, or documented programmatic interface; access to client, appointment, clinical-note, and billing data is through the browser application and manual exports only. This entry documents TherapyNotes as an API-relevant provider and honestly models the capability areas a behavioral-health EHR API would cover; the API surfaces below are modeled, not published, and no endpoints are fabricated.

providers.name: Tia
providers.description: Tia is a women's healthcare company that operates in-person clinics and a virtual care platform, bringing primary care, gynecology, mental health, and wellness services into one connected care experience. Founded in 2017 and backed by Canaan Partners, Tia runs clinics in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix, offers virtual visits across multiple states, and partners with health systems. Tia is a consumer healthcare provider and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Carrot Fertility
providers.description: Carrot Fertility is a global fertility and family-building benefits platform for employers and health plans, providing members with comprehensive reproductive and family-forming support across more than 195 countries. Carrot covers fertility care and preservation (egg, sperm, and embryo freezing), IVF and other assisted reproduction, surrogacy, adoption, pregnancy and postpartum support, low- and no-cost fertility options, gender-affirming care, and menopause and midlife care. Delivered as a B2B employee benefit with member and provider portals, Carrot pairs concierge care navigation with a network of clinics and experts. The company is HIPAA-compliant and maintains SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, PCI DSS, and HITRUST attestations. This API Evangelist profile tracks Carrot as a healthcare provider surfaced from the Uncork Capital portfolio; Carrot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cedar
providers.description: Cedar is a healthcare financial technology company whose patient financial experience platform unifies billing, payments, insurance coverage, and support for health systems, hospitals, and clinician-services groups. Its products include Cedar Pay (pre-visit, post-visit, and financing patient payments), Cedar Cover (benefits and financial assistance, including Medicaid enrollment), Cedar Support (AI-powered patient support and call-center automation via Kora AI), and Cedar Intelligence (a proprietary AI system for personalized patient engagement). Cedar reports having served over 50 million patients and processed billions of dollars in patient payments. The company is backed by a16z, Founders Fund, QED Investors, and SV Angel. Cedar publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or GitHub organization; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security-posture surface.

providers.name: Ixlayer
providers.description: Ixlayer is a direct-to-patient healthcare technology company that helps biopharmaceutical companies transform the patient experience through an integrated, AI-enabled platform. Its unified platform spans virtual patient onboarding and intake, telehealth for primary and specialty care, at-home and in-center lab testing with mobile phlebotomy, prescription fulfillment (retail, specialty, and home delivery), benefits verification and claims, connected care with provider directories and scheduling, and the ixAI patient concierge for AI-powered support and care coordination. Ixlayer says it has powered more than 1,100 nationwide programs and enabled over 4 million patient care journeys, and states its services are SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliant. The company is backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Paradigm Health
providers.description: Paradigm Health is an AI-native clinical trial platform connecting biopharma sponsors with a research-ready provider network spanning roughly 2,100 care locations across the United States. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, the company operates infrastructure implemented at healthcare provider organizations to make clinical research part of routine care. Its Study Conduct platform captures data directly from electronic health records and other structured and unstructured sources, algorithmically evaluates FDA-defined data points in real time, and transmits the critical safety and efficacy signals needed for regulatory determinations to trial sponsors and the FDA. Paradigm serves both trial sponsors (protocol optimization, feasibility and site selection, patient identification and enrollment, data collection and delivery, post-approval evidence) and research sites. The company acquired Flatiron Health's Clinical Research business, announced a research collaboration with the U.S. FDA, and is backed by ARCH Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and GV. Paradigm currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity, legal, and published security/compliance surface.

providers.name: Aspect Health
providers.description: Aspect Health is a digital health company offering a science-backed program for women managing PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome). Its PCOS program combines continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), personalized coaching from board-certified health coaches, at-home lab testing for inflammation, hormonal, cardiovascular, and metabolic markers, and the Aida AI dietitian, all delivered through a mobile app. Additional programs cover weight loss, general women's health, and a 21-day check up, with HSA/FSA-eligible plans. Aspect Health is a Techstars-backed company and operates as a consumer (B2C) health platform; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or MCP server.

providers.name: Caremessage
providers.description: CareMessage is a healthcare technology non-profit that operates one of the largest patient engagement platforms serving low-income and underserved populations across the United States. Since 2013 the platform has reached more than 20 million patients and is used by roughly 1 in 7 federally qualified health centers plus 200+ free clinics. Its products include 1:1 direct messaging, appointment lifecycle messaging, population outreach, health coaching, closed-loop referrals, Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) workflows, and Wellness Copilot, an AI-backed diabetes-management automation. CareMessage does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; access to the platform is through its web application and a login-gated help center. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from CareMessage's public web surface.

providers.name: Circle Medical
providers.description: Circle Medical is a San Francisco-based online and in-person primary care clinic offering telemedicine and clinic-based visits with same and next-day availability. Founded through Y Combinator, the company operates 20+ physical locations and provides virtual appointments across multiple US states through Circle Medical Care of California, an independent medical practice. Its 400+ board-certified physicians, physician assistants, and nurse practitioners treat primary care, mental health (ADHD, anxiety, depression), hormone and sexual health, urgent care, weight loss (GLP-1s), sleep, and dermatology. Circle Medical is a HIPAA-covered, patient-facing digital health provider; it publishes no public developer API or SDK program, and this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cooler Heads
providers.description: Cooler Heads Care, Inc. is a San Diego medical device company founded in 2018 by Kate Dilligan that makes Amma, an FDA-cleared Portable Scalp Cooling System (PSCS) used to reduce chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Amma circulates chilled fluid through a fitted cap to constrict scalp blood vessels and limit chemotherapy delivery to hair follicles, and is designed to be portable enough that patients can keep cooling outside the infusion chair. The company sells to infusion centers and oncology practices and publishes patient, provider, reimbursement and training material on its own site. It ships no developer API, SDK or public API documentation; its only machine-readable public surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served from its own host.

providers.name: Digbi Health
providers.description: Digbi Health is a digital therapeutics company delivering a precision-biology virtual clinic for food-related and inflammatory illnesses — obesity, cardiometabolic disease, type 2 diabetes, digestive disorders (IBS, GERD), MSK chronic pain, PCOS, sleep and mental health.
