providers.description: Cityblock Health is a value-based healthcare provider delivering integrated primary care, behavioral health, and social-services support to Medicaid and lower-income (dual-eligible) Medicare populations across multiple U.S. markets. Cityblock pairs community-based care teams with a proprietary care-delivery technology platform to coordinate wraparound care for historically underserved communities. The company is backed by 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio profile; it operates as a care provider and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Geneoscopy
providers.description: Geneoscopy is a commercial-stage molecular diagnostics company headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, focused on gastrointestinal health. Its platform analyzes stool-derived eukaryotic RNA (seRNA) biomarkers, a proprietary approach the company applies to colorectal cancer screening, inflammatory bowel disease and other gastrointestinal conditions. Its lead product, ColoSense, is a noninvasive multi-target stool RNA (mt-sRNA) colorectal cancer screening test approved by the FDA in May 2024 for adults aged 45 and older at average risk; it evaluates eight colorectal neoplasia-associated RNA markers together with occult hemoglobin, and has since been added to the American Cancer Society and NCCN colorectal cancer screening guidelines. Geneoscopy operates a CLIA-certified (26D2253457) and CAP-accredited clinical laboratory with permits in New York, California, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island and the District of Columbia, and partners with biopharma and research organizations on stool-biomarker diagnostics and prognostics. Geneoscopy is a diagnostics and clinical-laboratory company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Pendulum
providers.description: Pendulum (Pendulum Therapeutics, pendulumlife.com) is a microbiome-management and metabolic-health company that develops clinically validated probiotic supplements built on novel, patented anaerobic microbial strains such as Akkermansia muciniphila. Its consumer products - including Glucose Control, Metabolic Daily, Akkermansia, and a GLP-1 probiotic - are formulated to fuel and maintain the gut lining, support immunity, relieve gas and bloating, and help keep blood glucose in a healthy range, differentiated by double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials rather than off-the-shelf probiotic blends. Pendulum is a direct-to-consumer health and supplement brand and is a portfolio company of DCVC; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Spring Health
providers.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

providers.name: SteadyMD
providers.description: SteadyMD is a telehealth infrastructure and clinical-workforce company (a DocGo company) backed by Lux Capital. It supplies board-certified physicians and nurse practitioners, clinical operations, and 50-state licensing and credentialing, plus technology and telehealth APIs that let healthcare and digital-health partners launch branded, fully managed virtual care. Its APIs cover patient data submission, synchronous and asynchronous consult requests, two-way patient-clinician messaging, intake forms, clinician availability, real-time status updates, document attachments, scheduling, and reporting/SLA retrieval, offered as either a Limited (partner-EMR) or Complete (SteadyMD-EMR) integration. API documentation is provided under a business agreement via a request form; there is no public developer portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Talkspace
providers.description: Talkspace is a New York City-based online behavioral healthcare company founded in 2012 by Oren Frank and Roni Frank that delivers virtual therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through video, voice, messaging, and live chat. The platform connects users with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers across all 50 U.S. states, covering more than 150 mental health conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, bipolar disorder, OCD, PTSD, insomnia, postpartum depression, and substance use. Service lines include individual therapy for adults, teen therapy (ages 13-17), couples therapy, psychiatry with prescription management, and specialized programs for LGBTQIA+, military/veteran, and senior populations, plus the women's mental health program Chapters. Talkspace is in-network with major payers such as Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Optum, Blue Cross Blue Shield, TRICARE, and Medicare, and sells B2B solutions (Talkspace for Business) to employers, payers, benefit consultants, educational institutions, and government agencies. The company markets Precision Therapy, an internal machine-learning and NLP system used to match members to providers and surface clinical signal. Talkspace went public on NASDAQ under ticker TALK on June 23, 2021 via a SPAC merger with Hudson Executive Investment Corp, and was acquired by Universal Health Services on March 9, 2026. Talkspace does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; integrations with payers, EAPs, and benefits platforms are delivered through private partnership channels, and the platform is HIPAA, HITECH, and GDPR compliant.

providers.name: TheraNest
providers.description: TheraNest (now marketed as Ensora Mental Health) is a behavioral and mental health practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, and social workers. It covers client intake, scheduling, telehealth, clinical documentation and notes, treatment plans, client portals, insurance billing and claims, and reporting. TheraNest is the flagship mental health product of Ensora Health (formerly Therapy Brands). As of this review, Ensora does not publish a documented, self-serve public developer API for TheraNest - integration is via partnerships, HIPAA-gated interoperability, and contact-sales arrangements rather than an open developer portal. The API entries below are logical resource groupings modeled from the product surface; their endpoints are NOT documented public endpoints (endpointsModeled true).

providers.name: Bodyport
providers.description: Bodyport is a San Francisco healthcare technology company delivering remote heart-failure monitoring. Its FDA-cleared Cardiac Scale captures hemodynamic biomarkers through a patient's feet in under 30 seconds and transmits the readings over cellular to care teams within minutes. The company's Congestion Index algorithm combines multiple hemodynamic biomarkers to detect worsening heart failure earlier than standard weight-based rules, and its connected Care Platform surfaces monitoring, alerts, and care coordination through a clinical dashboard and a patient portal. Bodyport works with health systems and pharma partners including Geisinger, Boehringer Ingelheim, Stanford, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Duke, and Yale. The company publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its product, portal, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Datavant
providers.description: Datavant is a United States health-data logistics company, formed from the 2021 merger of Datavant and Ciox Health, that connects and de-identifies healthcare data across a "network of networks" spanning 350+ real-world data partners, 80,000+ hospitals and clinics, and a majority of the largest US health systems. Its core capabilities are privacy-preserving record linkage using Datavant tokens, HIPAA Expert Determination and de-identification, medical record retrieval / release of information, and real-world evidence generation for life sciences, payers, providers, and government. Datavant publishes a real machine-readable contract for the retrieval side of that business: an OpenAPI 3.1.0 document for the Datavant REST API (36 paths, 54 operations, OAuth 2.0 client credentials, base https://api.datavant.io/v2) is served anonymously at https://developer.datavant.com/openapi.json, even though that host's root returns HTTP 404. Access is still enterprise and contract-gated - there is no self-serve sign-up, no published pricing beyond a single AWS Marketplace listing, no published scopes or rate limits, and no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Home market is the United States.

providers.name: Invitae
providers.description: Invitae — operated as Labcorp Invitae / Labcorp Genetics since Labcorp acquired select Invitae assets out of the company's 2024 Chapter 11 — is a United States medical genetics and healthcare-technology company providing clinical-grade hereditary and somatic genetic testing across oncology, women's health, cardiology, neurology, pediatrics, and rare disease. Its laboratory is CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited, and it publishes a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices and state laboratory licensure. Clinicians order tests and receive results through a web portal with licensed genetic counseling and the Gia digital assistant. Invitae publishes no API: contract discovery across every Invitae host found no developer portal, no OpenAPI, no GraphQL endpoint, no MCP server, no A2A agent card, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, no SMART-on-FHIR configuration, no webhooks, no client SDK and no /.well-known document. api.invitae.com resolves but returns a blanket nginx 403 for every path, and the developer, docs and fhir subdomains do not resolve at all. The company's public GitHub organization is genuine but consists of forks of upstream bioinformatics projects, not first-party specifications or libraries.

providers.name: Kheiron Medical Technologies
providers.description: Kheiron Medical Technologies is a London-founded medical-imaging AI company best known for Mia (Mammography Intelligent Assessment), a deep-learning solution that supports radiologists in breast-cancer screening as an independent, concurrent, or triage reader. Founded in 2016 and backed by investors including Atomico, Kheiron now operates as part of RadNet's DeepHealth, whose portfolio spans breast, prostate, lung, brain, and thyroid imaging plus the Diagnostic, Operations, and TechLive suites. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kheiron/DeepHealth as a health-AI provider; the company exposes clinical products and enterprise integrations rather than a public self-serve developer API, so most machine-readable API artifacts are not applicable and this record captures its identity, security, and legal surface.

providers.name: Lumeon
providers.description: Lumeon is a clinical automation and care orchestration platform that uses intelligent automation and real-time data integration to remove inefficiencies from care-coordination processes. It lets health systems scale best-practice care pathways across the enterprise so clinicians can focus on patients while operational cost falls and outcomes improve. Lumeon serves 70+ health systems globally — including Optum, NYC Health+Hospitals, and the NHS — and is now part of Health Catalyst. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published; this profile captures the company identity and its security and compliance posture.

providers.name: MicroTech Medical
providers.description: MicroTech Medical (Hangzhou) develops user-friendly diabetes glucose monitoring devices — blood glucose monitoring systems (BGMS), the AiDEX continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system, the Equil patch insulin pump, a closed-loop artificial pancreas, point-of-care testing (POCT), and LinX. Its AiDEX API Platform (aidexapi.microtechmd.com) is a self-service developer portal that registers developers and issues API credentials for accessing blood glucose data resources from AiDEX CGM devices, with separate global and China regional endpoints. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: PocketHealth
providers.description: PocketHealth is a patient-centric medical imaging platform that lets patients access, view, store, and share their diagnostic imaging (DICOM) and reports online, and lets healthcare providers exchange imaging across institutions and networks. PocketHealth also publishes an open, RESTful developer API aimed at RIS/PACS/VNA vendors, letting them embed PocketHealth's patient enrollment, electronic consent, and background record-delivery workflows natively into their own clinical software. The developer API is partner-gated - it is free forever for RIS/PACS vendors, healthcare providers, and physicians, but the full technical reference (base URL, endpoint paths, authentication) is not published on the open web; engaged vendors are assigned a dedicated integration rep who provides testing resources and detailed documentation. As a result the APIs below are modeled from PocketHealth's public developer-program descriptions rather than a public API reference or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Ro
providers.description: Ro (ro.co) is a direct-to-consumer telehealth company that connects patients with US-licensed healthcare providers entirely online, offering prescription treatment, provider visits, and pharmacy fulfillment across categories including men's and women's health, weight management (Ro Body), dermatology (Ro Derm), hair loss, fertility (Ro Fertility), and sexual health. Ro deliberately operates a "Zero-API" vertically integrated online-visit experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its only public machine-readable surface is a security posture (RFC 9116 security.txt and a HackerOne vulnerability disclosure program). Ro is backed by Canaan Partners, General Catalyst, and Initialized Capital.

providers.name: SuppCo
providers.description: SuppCo is a consumer supplement tracking and optimization platform, describing itself as the world's first real supplement tracker and optimizer. Its iOS and Android app lets people log their supplement stack and get a personalized StackScore across quality, dosing, goal coverage, and nutrient levels, plus a TrustScore that rates products on 29 attributes. It is backed by a database of 160,000+ products, 20,000+ research studies, and 80+ expert protocols from functional-medicine practitioners. SuppCo is in open beta (free, with an optional Pro tier) and was acquired by Function Health. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: tab32
providers.description: tab32 is a cloud-based dental practice management, imaging, and analytics platform for dental practices and dental service organizations (DSOs). tab32 offers a real, commercial API - powered by Google Apigee and HIPAA / SOC 2 Type II compliant - that exposes tab32's patient, provider, schedule, charts, notes, ledger, and payments data objects to DSOs and third-party developers. Access is partner-gated, not open self-service - developers reach the API through tab32's developer API portal after establishing a partnership or enterprise relationship, and full endpoint reference, authentication, and base URL details live behind that portal rather than on the public website. The API entries below are modeled from tab32's publicly documented data objects and API messaging; their endpoint paths are not published publicly and are therefore illustrative, not confirmed.

providers.name: ThinkSono
providers.description: ThinkSono is a medical technology company that develops AI-powered ultrasound software enabling non-specialist clinicians to detect deep vein thrombosis (DVT) blood clots at the point of care. Its real-time AI guidance walks a clinician through capturing and interpreting a compression ultrasound scan, compressing what is typically a full-day specialist referral pathway into an approximately 30-minute point-of-care assessment. The product is positioned for hospital and primary-care settings (including NHS deployments) to reduce DVT diagnostic waiting times. ThinkSono is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. It is a B2B medical-device software business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Tryadonis
providers.description: Adonis (Adonis Technology, Inc., tryadonis.com redirects to adonis.io) is a healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) software company that applies AI to medical billing. Its platform connects in real time with a practice's existing EHR, practice-management, billing, and patient-portal systems to surface revenue-related insights, automate claims and billing workflows, and reduce manual work for revenue teams. The company is backed by Homebrew. This is a B2B SaaS product with a private, authenticated product API (api.adonis.io) and a customer app (app.adonis.io); it does not currently operate a public developer program, OpenAPI documentation, or API portal.

providers.name: Accolade
providers.description: Accolade is a personalized healthcare and benefits navigation platform for employers and health plans. It pairs members with a care team of advocates, registered nurses, physicians, and mental-health specialists to help them understand their benefits, find in-network care, book appointments, and manage chronic and complex conditions. Accolade combines this human advocacy with virtual primary care, expert medical opinion, and mental-health services delivered through its member web and mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Accolade is a member-facing benefits platform and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Baba
providers.description: Baba Care, Inc. is a healthcare company that provides patient advocacy and care-navigation services for Medicare beneficiaries in the United States. Operating under the tagline "Healthcare simplified," Baba pairs each member with a dedicated advocate who handles their healthcare headaches — coordinating care, benefits, and administrative tasks — with the service covered by Medicare. The member experience is delivered through a login-gated web application at baba.care; the company publishes no public developer or API surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: CapsoVision
providers.description: CapsoVision, Inc. (Nasdaq: CV) is a commercial-stage medical technology company headquartered in Saratoga, California that develops advanced imaging and artificial-intelligence technologies for gastrointestinal disease detection and screening. Its CapsoCam Plus single-use capsule endoscope captures a 360-degree panoramic view of the small-bowel mucosa without external receiver equipment, and is paired with CapsoCloud, an account-gated cloud application, and CapsoView review software for physician image review and reporting. A next-generation CapsoCam Colon system is in development. CapsoVision publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification; CapsoCloud is an end-user clinical web and mobile application whose JSON backend is private to the product.

providers.name: Carta Healthcare
providers.description: Carta Healthcare, Inc. is a San Francisco based clinical data management company that applies a "Hybrid Intelligence" model — proprietary AI paired with certified human clinical abstractors — to extract, validate and submit structured clinical data on behalf of hospitals and health systems. Its product family covers Voyager (the underlying AI data platform trained on electronic medical record content), Lighthouse and Atlas (AI-assisted clinical registry abstraction and submission, including the ACC NCDR, STS/ACC TVT and Vascular Quality Initiative registries), Navigator (clinical data intelligence and analytics), Harbor (cohort selection and clinical trial matching) and outsourced expert abstraction services. Carta Healthcare is an NCDR certified software vendor and has completed a Type 2 SOC 2 examination with an unqualified opinion covering security, availability and confidentiality. The company sells and integrates directly with hospital EMR environments under enterprise agreements; it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract on its public web surface.

providers.name: Cerebral
providers.description: Cerebral is an American telehealth company providing online mental health and wellness care, including therapy, counseling, psychiatric evaluations, and medication management delivered through its website and mobile app on a subscription basis. Founded in 2020 by Kyle Robertson and Ho Anh, the company treats conditions such as depression, anxiety, insomnia, ADHD, and substance use disorder. Cerebral is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, which led a $300M Series C in December 2021 valuing the company at roughly $4.8B. Cerebral is a direct-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API or programmatic surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public company and website properties.

providers.name: Citruslabs
providers.description: Citruslabs is a clinical research organization (CRO) that designs and runs clinical trials, consumer perception studies, and randomized controlled trials for consumer health brands across supplements, skincare, pet health, food and beverage, longevity, and women's health. It handles IRB approval, protocol design, participant recruitment, decentralized data collection, and statistical analysis, then turns results into regulator-reviewed, marketing-ready product claims for retailers, advertising, and packaging. Studies range from DIY consumer perception studies to full randomized controlled trials, typically completing in four to sixteen weeks.

providers.name: Claritypediatrics
providers.description: Clarity Pediatrics is a virtual pediatric telehealth clinic that diagnoses and treats ADHD, anxiety, and childhood obesity in children ages 5-17, currently serving families in California and Texas. It combines clinical evaluations, medication management, and evidence-based behavioral programs — Behavioral Parent Training (BPT) and RUBI for ADHD, the SPACE program and a Teen Anxiety Program for anxiety, and lifestyle medicine for obesity — delivered by licensed multispecialty clinicians through video visits and weekly group sessions. It is a direct-to-consumer healthcare platform (parent app + provider referral) with no public developer or API surface at this time. Backed by Homebrew; added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched from its public web presence.

providers.name: Conceive
providers.description: Conceive is a telehealth platform for fertility and pregnancy support. It offers 24/7 text access to fertility and pregnancy nurses, coaches, and dietitians, personalized fertility coaching, fertility test interpretation, virtual video visits with providers, expert-led community events, and an educational library. Membership is delivered through Conceive Plus and Conceive Premium tiers. The company is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. As a consumer telehealth app it publishes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its published identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Dawaai
providers.description: Dawaai is Pakistan's leading digital healthcare platform, operating a licensed online pharmacy alongside telehealth and diagnostic services. Founded on a licensed retail pharmacy (License #1265, 2014) and headquartered in Karachi, Dawaai lets patients order authentic prescription and OTC medicines for temperature-controlled doorstep delivery, book doctor and mental-health consultations, order home-based lab tests and checkups, arrange home nursing and medical services, and subscribe to chronic-care programs for diabetes and obesity. It is a LegitScript-certified healthcare merchant that sources directly from manufacturers and distributors, with qualified pharmacists handling procurement, storage, and dispensing. Dawaai is backed by 500 Global and operates across Pakistan, including Karachi and Rawalpindi. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network via the venture portfolio pipeline; Dawaai publishes no public developer/API program at this time.

providers.name: Dawn
providers.description: Dawn (Sleepedy, Inc. dba Dawn) is a digital-health company offering a clinician-guided Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) program delivered through a mobile app. The service pairs users with licensed sleep coaches and therapists for weekly video sessions and between-session chat, daily 5-7 minute sleep lessons, live sleep-performance insights, and weekly progress reports, with the goal of treating primary and chronic insomnia and reducing reliance on sleep medication. Dawn is in-network with major U.S. insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, United Healthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and offers an employer/enterprise workplace-wellness program. Backed by Kindred Ventures. Dawn publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Denticon
providers.description: Denticon is a cloud-based dental practice management platform built for dental service organizations (DSOs) and multi-location group practices, owned and operated by Planet DDS (which also owns Cloud 9 Ortho and Apteryx imaging). The Denticon API program - relaunched in July 2024 on a new developer portal powered by Azure API Management - exposes RESTful APIs, webhooks, and batch data extracts covering patient, appointment, financial/ledger, insurance and claims (Revenue Cycle Management), clinical, and practice/office data, with OAuth 2.0 auth, an event-driven architecture for synchronized updates, and writebacks into Denticon. API access is partner-gated - Planet DDS must approve vendors and each client practice authorizes vendor access to specific office locations (OIDs). Public documentation exists, but keys and interactive access require program enrollment, so the endpoint surface below is modeled from the published API categories rather than a downloadable OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Finni Health
providers.description: Finni Health is a telehealth company that connects families of children on the autism spectrum with Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapists and mental health providers. Operating across more than 30 states, Finni offers both in-home and in-clinic ABA therapy with flexible scheduling, handles insurance coordination and billing for its provider network, and gives parents a portal for progress tracking and family-led goal setting. The company positions itself as an operating platform for ABA practices as well as a care provider for families, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Five Lives
providers.description: Five Lives is a health-technology company building evidence-based digital tools for dementia prevention and brain health for adults aged 50 and over. Founded by former Peak brain-training leaders Xavier Louis (CEO) and Sylvain Piquet (COO), the fully remote company operates two consumer mobile apps: Five Lives Brain Health, a prevention app available since 2021 with cognitive tests, brain games, and lifestyle tracking across five pillars (nutrition, sleep, physical activity, mood and social connection, and mental stimulation); and Five Lives Care, an evidence-based memory and autonomy programme for people aged 60+ launched in January 2026 and developed with leading memory centres in the UK and France. Its work draws on the FINGER study and the Lancet Commission's modifiable dementia risk factors, with research partners including the University of Oxford, Trinity College Dublin, the FINGER Brain Health Institute, Dementias Platform UK, and the Gerontopole d'Ile de France. Backed by Speedinvest. Five Lives does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Frontera
providers.description: Frontera (Frontera Health) is an AI-assisted clinical documentation company for behavioral health. Its software automates assessment and diagnosis report writing for Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) and clinical psychologists working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and autism care, cutting report time from 6-10 hours to 2-3 hours. The platform pairs a BCBA-trained AI Assessment Builder and Diagnosis Builder with digital phenotyping, and is delivered as a HIPAA-compliant web application (customer login at portal.fronterahealth.com) rather than a public API. Frontera is a venture-backed portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and security surface; as of this pass Frontera publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP server.

providers.name: Grouper
providers.description: Grouper, operated by Element3 Health, Inc. (d/b/a Grouper) and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, is a healthy-aging benefit company that connects older adults to social clubs, group activities, and virtual community programming through health plans. Its consumer product, "Hello by Grouper," is a membership platform offering live and on-demand instructor-led virtual classes, research-based monthly brain-health challenges, and members-only online events, with the goal of keeping members active, socially connected, and healthier as they age. Grouper distributes primarily through Medicare Advantage and other health-plan partners rather than a direct developer channel; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface as of this profile, which was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture (a16z-associated) portfolio lead.

providers.name: Kindara
providers.description: Kindara is a fertility-awareness and reproductive-health company offering a digital fertility charting system across web (app.kindara.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps. It lets users track basal body temperature, cervical fluid, and menstrual cycle data to understand their fertility, time conception, or practice fertility-awareness-based birth control. Kindara pairs its charting app with the Wink basal thermometer and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer-facing femtech product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Lucid Lane
providers.description: Lucid Lane (now operating as Skyler Health) is a telehealth mental health platform delivering virtual talk therapy and counseling for mental health conditions, an AI-powered coaching companion, and guided meditation and mindfulness content through its Listen Therapy service. Originally founded to help patients taper off opioids and manage medication dependence during and after surgery, the company has since broadened into remote behavioral and mental health care delivered to members, employers, clinics, and providers. It is a consumer- and employer-facing care service with no public developer or API surface; member access is via the Skyler Health member portal. Backed by Accel and Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Milu Health
providers.description: Milu Health is a health technology company that pairs a virtual care team with an AI engine to help employees and their families get higher-quality healthcare at a lower cost. Founded in 2023 by Sasha Gribov and Gautam Kumar, Milu integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) data from tens of thousands of provider groups and health systems to proactively flag medication issues, care gaps, fairly priced and high-quality doctors, incorrect medical bills, and more affordable medications. The platform also ingests an employer's health plan and benefits so it can notify members when an existing benefit could help. Milu is offered through employers and benefits advisors as well as directly to individuals. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by a16z Bio + Health in March 2024. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; Milu does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Mindbloom
providers.description: Mindbloom is a direct-to-consumer telehealth company offering at-home ketamine-assisted therapy for anxiety, depression, and PTSD, combining psychiatric clinician oversight, guided therapeutic sessions, and peer support. Clients complete a psychiatric evaluation, receive either sublingual tablets or subcutaneous injectable treatments, and are supported through a structured program with monitoring and integration guidance. The company reports having facilitated over 200,000 ketamine therapy sessions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public API, developer platform, or developer documentation — Mindbloom is a consumer healthcare service, not an API provider.

providers.name: Musely
providers.description: Musely is a telehealth platform, founded in 2012 by Jack Jia and Carrie Jiao and based in San Jose, California, that connects patients with U.S. board-certified dermatologists for personalized, prescription-strength skincare and related care. Patients share skin concerns online, physicians craft personalized treatment plans, and freshly compounded formulas are shipped to the patient. Since pivoting from a wellness community to prescription skincare in 2019, Musely has expanded into hair loss, hormonal/menopause health, and longevity, serving more than 1.2 million patients. Musely is a consumer/health company in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a direct-to-consumer web and mobile telehealth experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Optimal
providers.description: Optimal is a preventive-health and longevity company based in Mexico City, backed by 500 Global, operating across Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, and Peru). Optimal offers a consumer blood test that analyzes more than 300 biomarkers and uses AI to surface problems before symptoms appear, positioning itself as a predictive health platform (branded "health OS") that integrates biological data, wearable metrics, behavioral patterns, and medical history into longitudinal health models to identify risk before it becomes disease. The company sells directly to consumers via a web app and subscriptions and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Poppins
providers.description: Poppins is a French digital health company that develops a clinically validated digital therapeutic (DTx) for children aged 7-11 with dyslexia. Classified as a Class I medical device under EU Regulation 2017/745, the mobile application delivers home-based, game-based training sessions of about 20 minutes per day, 3-5 times per week, targeting phonological awareness, reading speed, and visual attention span. Poppins complements in-person speech therapy, supports speech-language pathologists through professional accounts, and partners with insurers. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Poppins publishes a consumer and healthcare-professional web/mobile product but no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Q Bio
providers.description: Q Bio is a Redwood City, California health-technology company offering the Q Exam and the Q Bio Health Dashboard, sold directly at its clinic and through enterprise partners. The Q Exam is a comprehensive preventive-health assessment that combines whole-body non-contrast MRI, 120+ blood biomarkers, analysis of 163 risk-relevant genes, wearable data, medical history, and board-certified physician review into a single longitudinal health baseline. Imaging is quantified by Constellation, the company's FDA-cleared AI image-analysis software that segments organs and measures anatomy, and results are stored in the Q Bio Health Dashboard for year-over-year comparison. Q Bio is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Signos
providers.description: Signos is a metabolic health technology company founded by Sharam Fouladgar-Mercer and Bill Tancer that pairs a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) sensor with an AI-powered mobile app to help people understand their individual metabolic responses to food and make data-driven lifestyle changes for weight management. In August 2025 Signos received FDA clearance as the first over-the-counter glucose monitoring system for weight loss, making it available without a prescription to adults not on insulin. The platform integrates with the Dexcom Stelo sensor, Apple Health, Google Health Connect, smartwatches and smart scales, delivers real-time glucose insights, personalized meal and movement recommendations, registered-dietitian support, and daily and weekly metabolism scores, with optional GLP-1 medication access through partner healthcare providers. Signos was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). It is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Somnee
providers.description: Somnee is a consumer sleep-technology company behind a smart sleep headband that uses personalized neurostimulation to improve sleep. Developed over roughly eight years by a team of UC Berkeley neuroscientists (co-founders include sleep scientist Dr. Matthew Walker, Dr. Robert T. Knight, Dr. Rich Ivry, and CSTO Dr. Ram Gurumoorthy, with CEO Tim Rosa, former Fitbit CMO), the wearable pairs clinical-grade EEG+ sensors with a companion app and proprietary AI to deliver a 15-minute pre-bedtime session that the company says helps users fall asleep about 50% faster and cut nighttime wake-ups by roughly a third, without medication. Somnee sells the headband, accessories, and a sleep-service membership direct to consumers, and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Somnee publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: The Helper Bees
providers.description: The Helper Bees is an Austin-based aging-in-place technology company that operates one connected platform linking benefits, in-home service providers, and support so older adults can safely age at home. Its products include Care Concierge human guidance, an Aging-in-Place Marketplace for OTC products and nonmedical services (home care, safety modifications, meals, transportation), the Helpful benefits card, digital invoicing and claims processing for home and facility care, and digital nurse eligibility assessments for long-term care insurance. The company runs one of the nation's largest networks of vetted in-home care agencies and sells to Long-Term Care Insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid plan administrators. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The Helper Bees publishes member and provider applications (the api.thehelperbees.com app host, the myhomealign.com provider portal, and mobile apps) but does not currently expose a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Tuli
providers.description: Tuli Health operates a UK-wide network of over 300 high-street pharmacies as local diagnostic hubs, making clinical services - primarily blood testing and phlebotomy - accessible in every neighbourhood so people can get care close to home. It offers healthcare providers three models - One Network (white-label phlebotomy), One Solution (end-to-end test kits, draws and lab analysis), and an Enterprise tier with custom integration. Tuli exposes an API and web portal for booking and managing tests, though public developer documentation is not yet published.

providers.name: Visby Medical
providers.description: Visby Medical is a molecular diagnostics company that has miniaturized the gold-standard PCR laboratory onto a single-use, palm-sized point-of-care device, delivering lab-quality results in about 30 minutes without any instrument, sample transport, or lab infrastructure. Its consumer offering (sold direct at visby.com) is an FDA-authorized at-home women's sexual health test that detects Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, and Trichomoniasis, paired with same-day telehealth consultation on a positive result. Visby also builds point-of-care PCR platforms for clinical and respiratory pathogen testing. The company is backed by venture investors including Amplify Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks Visby Medical as a company; the business is a hardware diagnostics and direct-to-consumer commerce operation and does not publish a first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Weekend Health (Found)
providers.description: Weekend Health, Inc. (operating as Found / Found Health) is a consumer telehealth company offering personalized, science-based weight-loss care, including GLP-1 and other obesity medications, clinician oversight, coaching, and habit-change support delivered direct-to-consumer and through employer and health-plan channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile carries the company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Galileo
providers.description: Galileo (galileo.io, formerly reached at galileohealth.com) is a value-based, digitally enabled healthcare delivery company founded by Tom X. Lee (previously Epocrates and One Medical). It delivers 24/7 primary and multi-specialty care through a mobile app, in-home visits, mobile clinics, and virtual care, combining a proprietary clinical technology platform, a recruited network of primary-care and specialist clinicians, and hospitality-style member support. Galileo operates a fully bilingual (English/Spanish) platform and serves individuals and families, employers, small businesses, and health plans through membership and population- health partnerships. It is a care-delivery business, not an API platform: as of this profile Galileo publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Hidrate
providers.description: HidrateSpark is the world's smartest water bottle brand, tracking daily water intake with a Bluetooth-connected sensor puck that glows to remind you to drink and syncs to the HidrateSpark hydration app, Fitbit, and Apple Watch. The company (originally Hidrate, Inc., a Techstars-backed startup) sells its smart bottles and accessories through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at hidratespark.com. It does not publish a first-party developer or product API; the only machine-facing surface is the Shopify platform layer — OIDC/OAuth customer accounts and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce endpoints that let buyer-approved AI shopping agents browse and check out.

providers.name: Min Doktor
providers.description: Min Doktor is a Swedish digital healthcare provider (operated by MD International AB) offering online primary care through its mobile app and web service. Founded in 2013 as one of Sweden's first digital-first care providers, it connects patients with doctors, psychologists and nurses for consultations, prescriptions, referrals and vaccinations, and also runs white-label care services for partners such as Skandia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures. Min Doktor operates as a consumer/patient-facing service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable public security, identity and compliance footprint.

providers.name: Pathai
providers.description: PathAI is a healthcare artificial-intelligence company transforming pathology through machine learning. Its AISight Image Management System (IMS) and the AISight Link open API deliver AI-assisted disease detection, biomarker quantification, fields-of-interest and AI Impressions, and laboratory workflow integration for pathologists, hospital and reference labs, and biopharma research partners. AISight Link is an enterprise interoperability surface that connects AISight with third-party AI algorithms and Laboratory Information Systems (LIS/LIMS) over REST and HL7; PathAI does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. The company is ISO 27001 certified and operates a vulnerability disclosure program. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc.

providers.name: Womaness
providers.description: Womaness is a women-founded midlife wellness brand created to modernize aging for women and to help them navigate the phases their bodies move through around menopause. The direct-to-consumer company sells clean, estrogen-free, doctor-approved and clinically tested skincare, supplements, sexual-health and menopause-support products (including Let's Neck serum, Melt for You inserts and Daily V Soothe) through a Shopify-hosted online store and select retail partners. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer e-commerce brand with no first-party public developer API surface.

providers.name: Zoetis
providers.description: Zoetis is the world's leading animal health company, dedicated to discovering, developing, manufacturing, and commercializing medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, and technologies for animals. The company operates in over 100 countries and provides digital connectivity solutions that integrate veterinary diagnostics, reference laboratory services, and practice management systems through the Vetscan platform, enabling bidirectional communication between point-of-care analyzers and veterinary practice information management systems (PIMS).

providers.name: Biostate AI
providers.description: Biostate AI is a Houston-based precision-health biotechnology company combining proprietary wet-lab chemistry with generative AI to make RNA and DNA sequencing dramatically cheaper and more accessible. Its BIRT (Barcode-Integrated Reverse Transcription) plus PERD (Probes for Excess RNA Depletion) platform delivers Total RNA sequencing from around $60 per sample, and its N-Act and RNAstate AI models turn omics data into clinical insights for autoimmune, cardiovascular, and cancer diagnostics. The company operates a cloud data lake for AI-ready omics data and runs research partnerships across the U.S., India, and China. As of this profile Biostate publishes a marketing and publications site plus open research model repositories on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK client library, or developer portal.

providers.name: Labcorp
providers.description: Labcorp helps patients, providers, organizations, and biopharma companies guide vital healthcare decisions every day. Labcorp supports HL7 / FHIR-based integration for laboratory orders and results exchange with electronic health record (EHR) systems, but does not publish a fully open public developer portal; access is granted through health-system and biopharma integration agreements.

providers.name: Amperos
providers.description: Amperos provides AI-powered insurance claims management and revenue recovery for healthcare providers, using agentic AI to recover insurance revenue end-to-end and drive more collections, faster. The platform automates denial management, claims processing, and collections workflows while keeping human experts in the loop for complex cases, and integrates with major EHR / practice-management systems including eClinicalWorks, Athenahealth, NextGen, Epic, ModMed, and Dentrix. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Amperos exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time; the product is delivered as a managed service and web application.

providers.name: AnswersNow
providers.description: AnswersNow is a virtual Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy provider for individuals with autism, delivering personalized, evidence-based care from board-certified behavior analysts (BCBAs) through its proprietary telehealth platform. Families access one-on-one therapy sessions, caregiver and parent training, and individualized treatment plans remotely, expanding access to ABA care in areas with limited in-person availability. AnswersNow accepts major insurance carriers including Medicaid, is BHCOE accredited and a CASP member organization, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. This profile has been enriched with company identity and domain-security posture; AnswersNow publishes a consumer web application (web.getanswersnow.com) but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: August AI
providers.description: August AI is a consumer health-AI companion that helps people understand their symptoms, lab reports, prescriptions, and medications, and connects them to licensed physicians through asynchronous, chat-based telehealth visits. Founded in 2022 by Anuruddh Mishra after a four-month misdiagnosis, August operates as a 24/7 health assistant available on iOS, Android, and WhatsApp, storing lab reports and conversation history in long-term memory to deliver personalized guidance. The service pairs a free AI symptom-assessment experience with paid online doctor consultations from board-certified MDs licensed across all 50 US states. August reports serving millions of users across 160+ countries in 30+ languages, and publishes medical benchmarks including 100% accuracy on the USMLE, 97.4% on MedQA, 99.4% on lab-report document processing, and 100% precision/recall on emergency escalation. It is backed by Accel and Claypond Capital. August is a consumer application and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Chamber Cardio
providers.description: Chamber Cardio is a Washington, D.C.-based healthcare technology company building a cardiology-focused platform for value-based care. Chamber partners with cardiology practices and health plans to align clinical signals, workflows, and patient data so cardiologists can identify high-risk patients earlier, close gaps against treatment guidelines, and reduce administrative burden. Its workflow-integrated AI surfaces clearer signal from the large volumes of cardiovascular data generated in care, supporting better patient outcomes and financial predictability for payers as cardiology moves beyond fee-for-service. The company supports more than 500 cardiologists across seven states and raised a $60M Series A led by Frist Cressey Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, AlleyCorp, American Family Ventures, Company Ventures, Optum Ventures, Healthworx Ventures, and Black Opal Ventures. Chamber does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; its platform is built on a FHIR-based data stack (Medplum) with internal REST and GraphQL services.

providers.name: Eden
providers.description: Eden is a Latin American healthcare technology company providing cloud-based medical imaging and radiology software for hospitals, clinics, and diagnostic centers. Its platform includes Eden PACS (a cloud picture archiving and communication system and DICOM viewer), Eden Management (scheduling, referral, and operational workflow tools), Eden Intelligence (data-driven analytics for medical institutions), and Eden Creator (an AI assistant for drafting diagnostic impressions). Eden is backed by Sierra Ventures and serves medical institutions across Latin America. No public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Gyant
providers.description: Gyant was a San Francisco-based digital health company that built an AI-powered conversational virtual assistant for health systems, guiding patients through symptom checking, care navigation, and triage across web and messaging channels. In 2022 Gyant was acquired by Fabric (fabrichealth.com), and gyant.com now redirects to Fabric's healthcare care-access platform, which combines conversational AI with physician-built clinical protocols for virtual care, patient engagement, and clinical automation. Gyant does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, published legal/compliance surface, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Harbor Health
providers.description: Harbor Health is a Central Texas healthcare company building a vertically integrated "pay-vider" model that combines primary care, specialty care, and health coaching clinics with its own commercial and individual health insurance plans, so the same organization both delivers and covers care. Founded in 2022 by Dr. Clay Johnston (founding dean of UT Dell Medical School), Tony Miller, and Eric Scott, the company operates clinics and Express Care walk-in locations across the Austin, Dallas, El Paso, and San Antonio metros, and is pursuing a value-based care model for the commercial market. It is backed by General Catalyst, 8VC, and Alta Partners. Harbor Health publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (member portal, plans, blog, privacy and terms) for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Instride Health
providers.description: InStride Health is a virtual mental health provider delivering specialized, insurance-based treatment for children, teens, and young adults ages 7 to 24 who struggle with anxiety, OCD, panic, phobias, school avoidance, and related disorders. Its structured four-to-eight month program pairs each patient with a coordinated care team of a therapist, a psychiatric prescriber, and an exposure coach, combining evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy and exposure-and-response prevention delivered over telehealth. The company is backed by General Catalyst and tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a clinical care provider and publishes no public API, developer program, or SDK.

providers.name: Juno Chat
providers.description: Juno (junocompanion.com), operated by SharedGenes, Inc., is a Y Combinator-backed (P26) consumer digital-health startup building an AI personal health assistant for the 1B+ people living with chronic illness. The Juno mobile app (iOS and Android) builds a longitudinal health profile through conversation, biometrics, and medical history to deliver personalized symptom guidance, automated symptom tracking by text or voice, trigger-pattern identification, and appointment-ready reports for clinicians. It supports conditions including fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, lupus, and MS, and is informed by research from Oxford and UCL plus 1,000+ patient interviews. Founded in 2025 by Marshall Gould (CEO) and Isaac Tolley (CTO); HIPAA-aligned infrastructure with no health data sold. Juno is a consumer app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Myndlift
providers.description: Myndlift is a digital neurofeedback and mental-health company that pairs a consumer/clinical mobile app with a wearable EEG brain-sensing headband (Muse) to deliver therapist-guided, personalized brain-training programs. The platform provides brain mapping and assessments, gamified real-time neurofeedback sessions, progress tracking, and remote-monitoring dashboards used by both individuals and mental-health practitioners for attention, anxiety, stress, sleep, and peak-performance goals. Backed by 500 Global, the company reports 26,000+ members and more than one million neurofeedback sessions delivered. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record with verified identity links.

providers.name: Plenful
providers.description: Plenful is an AI-powered workflow automation platform for pharmacy and healthcare operations, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco with an office in New York City. The platform automates complex, high-ROI administrative pharmacy workflows — 340B audit and optimization, 340B referral capture, rebate and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) reconciliation, benefits verification and prior authorization, and infusion order intake — using large language models and machine learning tuned to each organization's data. It ingests PDFs, flat files, APIs, HL7 feeds, and databases, supports unlimited organizational logic rules, and serves 100+ healthcare organizations including Prisma Health, Renown Health, Temple Health, Cencora, and Samaritan Health Services. Plenful is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital), SUSA Ventures, TQ Ventures, and Waterline Ventures. Plenful ships an enterprise SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pomelo Care
providers.description: Pomelo Care is a value-based virtual healthcare company delivering 24/7 clinician-led care for women and children across fertility and preconception, prenatal and postpartum, pediatric and NICU, and midlife and menopause health. Operating as a telehealth platform contracted with employers and health plans, Pomelo pairs licensed clinicians, doulas, and care teams with remote monitoring to close the gaps between doctor visits, reduce NICU admissions, and improve maternal and infant outcomes. The company reports covering 25 million lives across all 50 states and raised a $92M Series C at a $1.7B valuation. Pomelo Care is a patient-, employer-, and payer-facing platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and First Round Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network for company-level discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Rula
providers.description: Rula is a telehealth mental health platform that connects patients with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their insurance. Operating as an in-network behavioral health marketplace across all 50 states, Rula matches individuals with more than 23,000 licensed clinicians for individual, couples, family, child, and teen therapy as well as psychiatric medication management, covering 90+ conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, PTSD, OCD, and addiction. Rula is in-network with 120+ insurance plans nationwide (Aetna, Cigna, Optum, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross, Kaiser), with patients paying an average of about $15 per session with insurance. Rula publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface as of this profile; care is delivered through its patient and provider web applications.

providers.name: Telepatia AI
providers.description: Telepatia is an AI-native clinical platform built for Latin American healthcare. It listens to doctor-patient consultations and generates clinical documentation in real time (AI Writer), surfaces evidence-based clinical recommendations during the visit (AI Advisor), integrates with 50+ electronic health record and hospital systems such as Epic, TASY, iClinic and MV (AI Integrator), and produces analytics on protocol adherence and clinical performance (AI Business Intelligence). Founded by Nicolas Abad and backed by a16z with a $33M Series A, the platform has deployed across 25+ hospital systems in Brazil, Colombia and Mexico. As of this enrichment pass Telepatia exposes a product and web application but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Thyrocare
providers.description: Thyrocare Technologies Limited is an Indian chain of diagnostic and preventive-care laboratories headquartered in Navi Mumbai, founded in 1996. Built around a centralized, highly automated laboratory model, it focuses on affordable preventive health checkups, thyroid and pathology testing, and sells through a nationwide network of DSA (Direct Selling Agent) franchise partners. Norwest Venture Partners invested pre-IPO, and PharmEasy (API Holdings) acquired a majority stake in 2021. Its partner order-booking API (TechSo/BTS) is gated behind the DSA program and publishes no public OpenAPI.

providers.name: Candid Co.
providers.description: Candid Co. (candidco.com), operating today as CandidPro, is a New York-based dental-technology company that delivers custom clear aligners for teeth straightening. Founded in 2017 as a direct-to-consumer brand backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Greycroft, and e.ventures, Candid pioneered at-home impression kits and remote monitoring, and has since pivoted to a dentist-directed model: aligners are prescribed and overseen by a licensed dentist with orthodontist support and convenient virtual visits (CandidMonitoring). Candid handles the clinical treatment plan, 3D-printed aligner manufacturing, and patient communication for crowding and common bite misalignments. This is a consumer/health brand with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain security posture, and commercial link properties.

providers.name: Curve Health
providers.description: Curve Health is a New York City-based digital health technology company, founded in 2020, that delivers a virtual care and telemedicine platform purpose-built for skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) and senior care. The platform unifies telemedicine, a health information exchange, predictive analytics, and smart billing into a single system so nurses, physicians, behavioral health providers, and facility operators can deliver care in place and reduce avoidable hospital transfers. Curve Health reports enabling 150,000+ remote care visits and an 80% reduction in hospitalizations for partner facilities, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Morningside. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web and product-documentation surface; Curve Health does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: mPower Social
providers.description: mPower Social Enterprises Ltd. is a Dhaka, Bangladesh technology-for-development company founded in 2008 by Harvard and MIT graduate students as ClickDiagnostics — winner of the MIT $100K competition — and renamed after moving its center of gravity to Bangladesh in 2010. mPower designs, builds and operates information systems for governments, UN agencies, donor organizations and international NGOs across health and nutrition, water and sanitation, agriculture and livestock, education, governance and rights, livelihood and poverty alleviation, climate and environment, and humanitarian response, and states it has deployed more than 300 ICT solutions across 17 countries in the Global South. Its engineering practice is built on open-source digital public goods — DHIS2, OpenMRS, OpenSRP / FHIR Core, Bahmni and Moodle — which it customizes, integrates and supports for national health management information systems, electronic medical records and shared health records, rather than shipping a hosted product of its own. The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified. mPower publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; its public software surface is a GitHub organization made up largely of downstream forks of the open-source health platforms it implements, plus a set of first-party Android apps on Google Play.

providers.name: OneHealthCompany
providers.description: The One Health Company is a Palo Alto veterinary precision-oncology company, best known for its FidoCure platform, that brings human-grade precision cancer medicine to dogs. FidoCure sequences a dog's tumor with next-generation DNA sequencing, matches the cancer-driving mutations to targeted therapies, and gives veterinarians an individualized treatment plan grounded in the world's largest proprietary canine cancer dataset (billions of data points across a network of more than 1,300 veterinary clinics). The company was founded in 2015 by Christina Lopes and Ben Lewis on the "One Health" thesis that treating cancer in companion dogs also advances real-world evidence for human oncology. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z bio), Y Combinator, Polaris Partners, Borealis Ventures, Lerer Hippeau and Tau Ventures. As of this profile the company exposes a consumer and veterinarian web experience (including a veterinarian login portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Quant Network
providers.description: Quant Network is a blockchain interoperability company whose Overledger platform provides APIs to issue, connect, and monitor digital assets, smart contracts, transactions, and accounts across multiple distributed ledger technologies without requiring blockchain expertise.

providers.name: Rex Inc
providers.description: Rex Inc, operating as Rex.fit (BabylonAI Inc.), is a Y Combinator (W23) health and fitness company building AI-powered, fully automated nutrition tracking. Its consumer products include Rex Nutribot, a WhatsApp AI nutrition coach; the Drop, a wearable AI camera pendant that detects meals and automatically logs calories, protein, carbs, and fats via computer vision; an AI body scanner; and personalized coaching with daily health reports. Rex also offers a white-label B2B nutrition-and-fitness AI that fitness chains and app builders integrate to add meal logging (photo, barcode, or text), recipe and meal-plan generation, workout logging, 3D body scans, and nutrition analytics under their own brand.

providers.name: Science
providers.description: Science Corporation is a clinical-stage medical technology company founded in 2021 by Max Hodak and headquartered in Alameda, California, with offices in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina and Paris, France. Science develops brain-computer interface (BCI) and neural-engineering technologies to restore vision, cognition, and mobility, including the PRIMA retinal implant for patients with macular degeneration, the Biohybrid neural interface, and the Vessel perfusion platform. Through its Foundry division Science also offers MEMS production and neural-engineering services to external partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Science publishes no public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Solv Health
providers.description: Solv Health operates a consumer marketplace (solvhealth.com and the Solv app) for booking same-day urgent care, primary care, and lab appointments, plus a provider-facing platform (scheduling, intake, patient acquisition, reputation management, messaging, payments) sold to clinics and health systems. There is no self-serve public developer API or published API reference on solvhealth.com; API access is gated behind a sales-led partnership. Solv states it exposes "interoperable APIs" that power custom booking experiences on partner websites and apps, a "Final Mile" API/network that lets digital-first and virtual-care partners (e.g. Included Health) hand patients off to real-time same-day appointment availability at Solv's national network of urgent care clinics, and bidirectional EHR interoperability (APIs, HL7, FHIR, and RPA) that syncs patient demographics, appointment status, and documents with systems like Epic, Athena, Cerner, Allscripts, DrChrono, eClinicalWorks, Experity, and NextGen. None of these capabilities have a published base URL, endpoint reference, or self-serve API key signup; access is provisioned per partner/clinic inside a commercial contract.

providers.name: str8bat
providers.description: str8bat is a Bangalore, India based sports-technology company that builds a pocket-sized IoT sensor which attaches to a cricket bat and captures batting metrics in real time — bat speed, impact speed, back-lift angle, timing, sweet-spot placement and a 360-degree view of every shot. The sensor pairs with the str8bat mobile app (iOS and Android) to deliver instant, visual and actionable insights plus an AI cricket coach. The company reports 30,000+ active users, 6+ million shots recorded and operations across 350+ Indian cities and 14+ countries. str8bat is a consumer hardware and mobile-app company and publishes no first-party developer API; its str8bat.com storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes standard commerce discovery surfaces (customer-account OIDC and a Universal Commerce Protocol agent-commerce MCP endpoint).

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: VillageMD
providers.description: VillageMD is a Chicago-based, value-based primary care organization that operates and supports physician practices across the United States through its Village Medical, Village Medical at Home, Summit Health, CityMD and Starling Physicians operating companies, serving millions of patients across primary care, multispecialty and urgent care. It runs clinics — free-standing practices, in-Walgreens practices, home-based care and virtual visits — rather than selling software, and its clinical record and patient-facing digital surface run on athenahealth: patient portals are hosted at practice-specific athenahealth portal subdomains and the Village Medical mobile app is the athenaPatient experience. VillageMD publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no machine-readable specification and no SDK; the only public machine-readable interfaces touching its patients are athenahealth's certified FHIR R4 APIs, which are operated and documented by athenahealth, not by VillageMD. Since Sycamore Partners took Walgreens Boots Alliance private in August 2025, VillageMD has operated as a standalone company in that portfolio.

providers.name: WOO Sports
providers.description: WOO Sports makes a sensor-based performance-tracking system for kitesurfing, wingfoiling, and windsurfing. The WOO 4.0 device mounts to a board and measures jump height, airtime, G-force, and landing impact, syncing sessions through the WOO Sports mobile apps (iOS, Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS, and Garmin) to a global community platform with leaderboards, spots, activity feeds, and events. More than 100,000 riders use WOO to track sessions and compete, including on the GKA Kite World Tour. WOO Sports is a Techstars-backed brand operated under Boards & More. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web surface; no public developer API was found (docs.woosports.com is a consumer user guide, not an API reference).

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Augmedix
providers.description: Augmedix is a San Francisco-based health technology company providing ambient AI medical documentation (AI scribe) services that capture patient-clinician conversations and generate clinical notes so that physicians can focus on patient care instead of EHR data entry. Founded in 2012, the company went public on Nasdaq in 2021 (AUGX) and was acquired by Commure in October 2024, becoming part of Commure's clinician-workflow platform alongside HCA Healthcare-aligned tooling. Augmedix's product line spans three service tiers — Augmedix Go (self-service AI scribe), Augmedix Assist (AI drafting with human editing, coding, and referral-letter support, notes ready within an hour), and Augmedix Live (full-service dedicated medical documentation specialist before, during, and after the visit) — plus specialty variants for Emergency Medicine, oncology, and other specialties. The platform integrates with major EHRs including Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth, Meditech, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, and iKnowMed, and is HIPAA-compliant and HITRUST-certified. Augmedix's GitHub presence consists of internal QA, scribe-app base, and ambient API automation repositories; there is no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification — integration with Augmedix is handled through enterprise EHR partnerships and the Commure clinician platform rather than a self-service developer surface.

providers.name: Delve Bio
providers.description: Delve Bio is a genomic diagnostics company commercializing clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnosis. Its flagship test, Delve Detect, analyzes all nucleic acids in a single cerebrospinal fluid sample to simultaneously detect bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, screening against a curated database of more than 68,000 pathogen species to diagnose meningitis and encephalitis with results in roughly 48 hours. The company is the exclusive licensee of the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) mNGS technology developed at the Center for Next-Gen Precision Diagnostics, founded by Charles Chiu, Joe DeRisi, Michael Wilson, Pardis Sabeti, and Matthew Meyerson, and backed by investors including GV. Delve Bio operates as a CAP/CLIA-certified clinical laboratory serving labs and clinicians; it exposes no public developer API surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a gv portfolio lead.

providers.name: LEAP
providers.description: LEAP is cloud-based legal practice management software for law firms, covering matter and contact management, document automation and court forms, time recording, billing, and trust accounting, tightly integrated with Microsoft 365. LEAP operates a LEAP Developer Console and LEAP Marketplace (developer.leap.build / console.leap.build) through which approved third-party developers build REST-based integrations (an "API Reference" is versioned there, e.g. v1.0.4, v1.0.5), but the technical reference - endpoint paths, base URL, and authentication schema - sits behind developer registration and an app review process rather than a public, self-serve API reference. There is no publicly published OpenAPI document, public base URL, or anonymous API key signup. Existing Marketplace integrations (Xero, Zoom, InfoTrack, LawTap, and others) confirm the API surface is real and in production use, but its concrete shape is not publicly disclosed.

providers.name: Zwift
providers.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

providers.name: Alto Pharmacy
providers.description: Alto Pharmacy is a San Francisco-based digital pharmacy and pharmacy-technology company (founded 2015 as ScriptDash) that combines a full-service licensed pharmacy with a proprietary pharmacy operating system, Alto OS.
