Alto fills retail, specialty and fertility prescriptions with same-day courier delivery, pharmacist care and automated benefits investigation, and it sells that stack to industry partners as Alto Hub+, Alto Dispensing and Alto Complete — hub services, dispensing and end-to-end pharmacy-as-a-service for pharmaceutical manufacturers, health plans, health systems and digital health companies. Alto markets intake, transfer and Surescripts-based integrations to those partners, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification; technical access runs through its partnerships team.

providers.name: Capstan Medical
providers.description: Capstan Medical is a Santa Cruz, California medical device company founded in 2020 out of the Occam Labs incubator by Dan Wallace, with Maggie Nixon as CEO. The company is developing a surgical robotics platform for structural heart disease, merging robotic catheter navigation with next-generation transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve implants so heart valves can be repaired or replaced without open heart surgery. In 2025 Capstan completed what it describes as the world's first robotic catheter mitral valve replacements in humans, and it raised a $110M Series C led by Eclipse with participation from Intuitive Ventures and Yu Galaxy, bringing total funding past $150M ahead of a second-generation system planned for 2026. Capstan is pre-commercial and regulated medical device focused: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Clear Labs
providers.description: Clear Labs builds automated next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms that combine laboratory robotics, cloud software, and bioinformatics to deliver genomic data and actionable insights. Its product lines span oncology research (Clear Dx), infectious-disease and microbial genomics (Clear Ix), and food-safety pathogen testing (Clear Safety) for organisms such as Listeria and Salmonella. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Clear Labs publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile; the record captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Click Therapeutics
providers.description: Click Therapeutics, Inc. is a New York-headquartered digital medicine company founded in 2012 by David Benshoof Klein that develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments — the category it named Digital Therapeutics. Its AI-enabled platform targets diseases with an underlying neurological or behavioral component through cognitive and neurobehavioral mechanisms, delivered as smartphone software used independently or alongside biomedical therapy (Software-Enhanced Drugs). Authorized and commercial programs include CT-152 (Rejoyn, major depressive disorder, developed with Otsuka), CT-132 (episodic migraine) and AspyreRx (type 2 diabetes), with a pipeline spanning schizophrenia (CT-155 with Boehringer Ingelheim, CT-156), opioid use disorder, multiple sclerosis, atopic dermatitis, obesity, oncology, insomnia and acute coronary syndrome. Click publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK — its software is distributed as regulated prescription therapeutics, not as a platform.

providers.name: EarLens
providers.description: Earlens Corporation is a privately held medical technology company in Menlo Park, California that makes the Earlens Contact Hearing Solution, a non-surgical, custom-fit direct-drive hearing device. Instead of amplifying sound through a speaker, a custom lens rests on the eardrum and is driven by light from an ear-tip, vibrating the eardrum directly to reproduce a broader frequency range than conventional hearing aids. Founded by Dr. Rodney Perkins, the company holds more than 180 patents, received FDA clearance for its second-generation system in 2019, and was named to TIME's Best Inventions of 2020. Earlens is sold through audiology and ENT providers and publishes a consumer and provider marketing site, patient support documents, and a news section. As of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Endotronix
providers.description: Endotronix, Inc. is a Naperville, Illinois medical device and digital health company founded in 2007 and acquired by Edwards Lifesciences in July 2024, where it now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary. Endotronix builds the Cordella Heart Failure System, an integrated remote heart-failure management platform combining an implantable wireless pulmonary artery (PA) pressure sensor — granted FDA premarket approval in June 2024 — with a patient-facing myCordella tablet application, connected home vitals peripherals (blood pressure cuff, weight scale, pulse oximeter), and the myCordella Patient Management Portal, a cloud-based web application clinicians use to review transmitted PA pressure, vitals and symptom data and to titrate guideline-directed medical therapy. The company publishes clinical evidence (PROACTIVE-HF), instructions for use and device manuals, but operates no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification on any Endotronix host.

providers.name: Healthera
providers.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Lifesum
providers.description: Lifesum is a Stockholm-based digital health company whose consumer mobile application helps people improve their well-being through food logging, calorie and macronutrient tracking, personalized meal plans, recipes, and habit building. Backed by Balderton Capital, the company operates a subscription business-to-consumer product across iOS and Android in a dozen languages. As of this profile Lifesum publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or partner API portal, so this entry is an identity-only company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API profile.

providers.name: MedThread
providers.description: MedThread is an AI-powered Health Information Management (HIM) platform built specifically for long-term and post-acute care facilities — skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), nursing homes, assisted living facilities (ALFs), and rehabilitation centers. The platform digitizes paper records with AI-powered scanning, runs continuous automated audits for documentation completeness and regulatory compliance, monitors CMS quality metrics (rehospitalization, pressure ulcers, antipsychotic use), and provides a compliance dashboard, provider portal, and patient-facing Personal Health Record (PHR). MedThread advertises FHIR compatibility and pre-built EHR integrations (Epic, Cerner, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Meditech, athenahealth, Greenway, Practice Fusion) via a secure API. Techstars-backed and based in Miami, FL. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Paradromics
providers.description: Paradromics is a clinical-stage neurotechnology company headquartered in Austin, Texas, with a machine-learning and data-science office in Oakland, California, developing high-data-rate implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCI). Founded in 2019 by Matt Angle, the company builds the Connexus BCI, an investigational fully implantable system that records high-resolution intracortical neural activity and transmits it through the skin to an external system that decodes intended speech, text and digital device control for people with severe motor impairment. Connexus holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designations for speech decoding (2023) and digital device control (2024), was accepted into the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program, and received an Investigational Device Exemption in November 2025 for the Connect-One Early Feasibility Study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07357428). Tempo BCI is a pre-clinical-trial pipeline product. Paradromics publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its only machine-readable public surface is an llms.txt AI-context file at paradromics.com/llms.txt.

providers.name: 01health
providers.description: 01Health is a UK-based health technology company building clinical infrastructure that lets specialist healthcare be delivered safely inside community and dental clinics rather than only in hospitals. Founded in 2022 by Dr Sonia Szamocki, its platform centralizes patient acquisition, clinical protocols, remote specialist oversight, treatment workflows, procurement, and financial management into a single system, currently spanning orthodontics (32Co) and sleep medicine (Aerox). 01Health is backed by Balderton Capital, Gresham House Ventures, Eka Ventures, and Wavemaker360. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been published to date; this profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web surface.

providers.name: Briya
providers.description: Briya builds AIRE (AI Research Environment), a privacy-first AI platform for healthcare and clinical research that lets researchers analyze real-world medical data without writing code. AIRE trains AI models on real-world data and provides domain-specific agents for literature review, hypothesis testing, population and cohort analysis, study design, and manuscript-ready output with built-in validation. Data is accessed across multiple sources without centralizing it into a warehouse, with a compliance posture aimed at HIPAA, GDPR, and FDA/EMA regulatory standards. Briya serves emerging biotech, life sciences organizations, academic institutions, and healthcare systems, with offices in New York, Nashville, and Tel Aviv. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass on a portfolio lead; Briya publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Forus (fka Tandem Health)
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem Health) is a US healthcare technology company building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to bring new therapies to patients. Its platform automates the medication-access workflow end to end: prior authorization submissions, appeal-letter generation, insurance enrollment forms, benefit verification, pharmacy routing, patient status communication, PA renewal tracking, and affordability-program enrollment. It integrates with major EHRs so prescribers can submit directly, covers any drug/plan/pharmacy across all 50 states, and is HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. The company publishes an engineering blog at build.forus.com but does not currently expose a public developer API. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Generation Lab
providers.description: Generation Lab is a longevity science company founded in 2023 by Alina Su, UC Berkeley bioengineer Dr. Irina Conboy, and Michael Suswal, and backed by an $11M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first longevity bet). Its flagship SystemAge test measures biological age across roughly 460 biomarkers spanning 19 to 21 physiological systems and organs from an at-home, needle-free blood collection, returning a personalized aging report and science-backed action plan that ranges from lifestyle and supplement guidance to clinical interventions. The test is distributed through 300+ clinic partners across 18 countries and via a patient/provider portal. Generation Lab publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public web, product, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: MedAll
providers.description: MedAll is a UK-founded healthcare education platform on a mission to make medical education radically accessible. It hosts live and on-demand courses, conferences, workshops, webinars and training sessions for healthcare professionals, students and organisations, and provides event management tooling for registrations, feedback forms, certificates, abstracts, schedules and digital poster halls, alongside CME (continuing medical education), question banks and mobile apps for iOS and Android. The platform is used by clinicians and institutions worldwide. As of this enrichment pass MedAll publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture. Backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Pivotal Health
providers.description: Pivotal Health (formerly Radix Health) is a healthcare technology company and self-described "IDR Authority" that helps medical providers secure fair out-of-network reimbursement through the federal Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process created by the No Surprises Act. Its platform combines automated eligibility screening, dispute submission software integrated with major revenue cycle management (RCM) systems, payer data, and white-glove managed services across emergency medicine, anesthesiology, radiology, surgery, pathology, air ambulance, and hospitals and health systems. Pivotal Health is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Rescripted
providers.description: Rescripted is a digital women's health platform dedicated to empowering women across the entire lifecycle, from first period to last. It combines an editorial content hub of expert-reviewed articles, videos, and clinical research with Clara, an AI-powered health companion built on thousands of real questions and reviewed by medical experts. The platform spans menstrual health, fertility, pregnancy, sexual health, general wellness, and condition management for PCOS, endometriosis, and related concerns, and works with 200+ health and wellness partners. Founded by Kristyn Hodgdon and Abby Mercado and backed by Techstars, Rescripted is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: River Health
providers.description: River Health is an employer-sponsored virtual-first health plan operated by Mountain (joinmountain.com) that gives employees comprehensive primary and behavioral care at no cost to them. Members get unlimited virtual primary care and in-person doctor visits, behavioral health and therapy, thousands of free medications with home delivery or pharmacy pickup, free preventive care and screenings, after-hours urgent care, no-cost specialty and chronic- condition care, and free lab testing through Quest Diagnostics. Employers from small businesses to the Fortune 500 sponsor the plan; members enroll and manage care through the River Health member app at app.helloriver.com. River Health is a portfolio company of Techstars. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal has been published.

providers.name: Rovi Health
providers.description: Rovi Health is a clinical navigation platform for employer health plans that puts "a clinician in every member's pocket." Members get text-based access to registered nurse care advisors who help them find high-quality, in-network doctors and specialists, navigate their insurance benefits and coverage, and coordinate care across every stage of treatment. The company also uses AI agents to search millions of pricing and quality data points to surface the best in-network providers for complex care and to handle appointment scheduling, aiming to help employers cut 10-20% of healthcare spend while improving employee outcomes. Rovi Health was a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) company operating in the digital health, health insurance navigation, and consumer health services space. As of this enrichment pass Rovi Health publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Ruma Care
providers.description: Ruma Care is a healthcare software company that streamlines the prior authorization process for biologic and infusion medications in infusion clinics. Its AI-powered platform pulls patient and insurance data from electronic health records (EHRs) to identify payer requirements, auto-populates payer-specific prior authorization forms with clinical data, flags missing documentation, and then manages insurer communication and follow-up until an authorization is approved. Built by former infusion clinic staff, Ruma Care consolidates the manual portal, fax, and paper workflows behind buy-and-bill and infusion services into a single platform to reduce denials and accelerate patient access to biologics. Ruma Care is a Y Combinator-backed company. As of this profile the company exposes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Simplifeye
providers.description: Simplifeye is a dental practice management platform that helps practices grow and streamline front-office operations through integrated payments, online scheduling, live webchat, and patient-engagement campaigns. Its HIPAA-compliant payments product supports in-office transactions, invoicing, and customizable payment plans; its 24/7 real-time online scheduler lets patients self-book appointments; and its live webchat is staffed by real people who answer patient questions and qualify leads outside business hours. Simplifeye was acquired by Vyne Dental and integrates with the Vyne Trellis billing platform for claims, eligibility, and revenue acceleration. Simplifeye operates a private, authenticated backend (api.simplifeye.co) that powers its dashboard and patient-facing widgets, but publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Sprinter Health
providers.description: Sprinter Health is an in-home preventive and diagnostic healthcare company that pairs trained community health workers ("Sprinters") who visit patients at home with a virtual team of physicians, nurses, and care navigators. Its hybrid Sprinter Care+ model delivers vitals, blood draws, ECGs, cancer and diabetic screenings, wellness visits, medication reconciliation, care-gap closure, health risk assessments, and social-needs screening, and partners with health plans such as Humana, Molina Healthcare, and Anthem. Backed by a16z, Accel, General Catalyst, and GV. No public developer or API surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture, and legal/trust properties.

providers.name: Cytovale
providers.description: Cytovale is a San Francisco-based medical diagnostics company that develops early-detection technology for sepsis. Its flagship product, IntelliSep, is the first and only FDA-cleared in vitro diagnostic test for sepsis: it uses microfluidics, high-speed video, and computer-vision algorithms to measure the biophysical rigidity of tens of thousands of white blood cells, detecting the immune activation that signals sepsis risk and returning a risk stratification in roughly eight minutes. The test runs on the Cytovale System medical device in emergency-department settings. Cytovale is venture-backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sands Capital, and the Global Health Investment Corporation. The company operates as a clinical/diagnostics device maker and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Modern Animal
providers.description: Modern Animal is a membership-based veterinary healthcare company operating physical primary and urgent care clinics across major U.S. metropolitan regions, combining in-clinic visits with 24/7 virtual veterinary consultations, pharmacy and prescription management, dental care, surgery, and preventive care. It runs a subscription membership model (All Access, Essential, and Pay As You Go tiers) with transparent, upfront pricing and a companion mobile app for booking and virtual care. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and susa-ventures. Modern Animal is a consumer veterinary brand and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Oshi Health
providers.description: Oshi Health is a virtual, whole-person gastrointestinal (GI) care clinic delivering insurance-covered telehealth to patients with digestive conditions such as IBS, GERD, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. Care is provided by a coordinated team of GI providers, registered dietitians, and gut-brain behavioral health specialists, and is offered to members through major health plans and employers. Oshi Health is a patient-facing healthcare services company rather than an API producer; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with the artifacts the company genuinely publishes.

providers.name: Sol
providers.description: Sol Reader is a wearable e-reader — marketed as the world's first wearable e-reader — built by Sol and backed by Initialized Capital. The device is a lightweight (104g) headset with dual 1.3" 271ppi side-lit E Ink displays, adjustable diopter optics and IPD, a handheld remote, and 25+ hours of battery for a distraction-free reading experience. It reads a connected Kindle library and DRM-free EPUB uploads, offers the Sol Store with over one million titles, plus AI question-answering and an AutoPilot speed-reading mode. Sol is a consumer hardware company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Stel
providers.description: Stel Life provides cellular-connected remote patient monitoring (RPM) infrastructure for healthcare. Its cellular-enabled vitals hubs and connected medical devices — blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters, glucometers, thermometers, and scales — let patients transmit vital-sign readings to electronic health record (EHR) systems without WiFi, broadband, a smartphone, or app setup, targeting elderly, low-income, rural, and low-tech-literacy populations. Health systems and digital health organizations use Stel across the care continuum, from wellness and chronic-care management to hospital-at-home. Stel is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

providers.name: Teladoc Health
providers.description: Teladoc Health is a global leader in whole-person virtual care, providing on-demand healthcare, expert medical opinions, mental health services, chronic condition management, and integrated virtual care solutions to consumers, employers, health plans, hospitals, and clinicians. The company connects patients with clinicians via mobile, web, phone, and video to deliver 24/7 access to care across a wide range of conditions. Teladoc Health offers integration capabilities for partners and health systems, but does not publish a publicly accessible developer API portal with open documentation.

providers.name: Viz.ai
providers.description: Viz.ai is a healthcare AI company that builds an intelligent care coordination platform. Its FDA-cleared, AI-powered software analyzes medical imaging (CT, CTA, MRI, echocardiography) to detect suspected disease — stroke (large vessel occlusion, ICH), aneurysm, pulmonary embolism, and cardiovascular conditions — and automatically alerts and connects the multidisciplinary care team in real time to accelerate diagnosis and treatment. Backed by CRV, GV, Insight Partners, Scale Venture Partners, Seedcamp, Susa Ventures, and Threshold Ventures. Viz.ai exposes no public developer API; integration is delivered through clinical/enterprise deployment, and its governance-relevant public surface is a Drata-hosted Trust Center documenting a broad security and compliance program (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and an extensive ISO family including ISO 42001 for AI management).

providers.name: Biobeat
providers.description: Biobeat Technologies is an Israeli med-tech company whose remote patient monitoring (RPM) health-AI platform pairs a disposable short-term chest-monitor and a reusable long-term wrist-monitor - both using a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor - to continuously track up to 13 vital signs, including FDA-cleared cuffless blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, temperature, stroke volume, cardiac output, and one-lead ECG (chest-monitor). Readings stream to Biobeat's HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant, cloud-based patient management platform, where clinicians view real-time data, trends, and configurable alerts. Biobeat offers programmatic data access and EMR/EHR integration as a paid add-on for hospitals, health systems, and research partners; there is no publicly documented self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Mend
providers.description: Mend is a HIPAA-compliant telehealth and patient engagement platform for mental and behavioral healthcare organizations, powering appointment scheduling, automated reminders, secure video visits, digital intake forms and consents, patient messaging, payments, and AI no-show prediction. Mend integrates with EHR and practice-management systems through a combination of HL7, SFTP, and an API served from api.mendfamily.com. That API exists and is used by Mend's own portal for session initialization and signaling, but its reference documentation is delivered through a login-gated customer knowledge base rather than a public developer portal, so Mend's programmatic surface is best characterized as partner- and customer-gated rather than openly self-serve.

providers.name: Cornerstone Robotics
providers.description: Cornerstone Robotics (CSR) is a Hong Kong-headquartered surgical robotics manufacturer founded in 2019 at Hong Kong Science Park, building the Sentire Endoscopic Surgical System (C1000) — a multi-specialty, minimally invasive robot-assisted surgery platform developed entirely in-house and indicated for general surgery, gynecology, thoracic and urology. The Sentire system has received regulatory clearance in China (NMPA), the European Union and Singapore, and has completed multicenter clinical trials in China and the United Kingdom. The company operates three global R&D hubs, six business centers and a 30,000 square meter manufacturing facility, and sells a regulated physical medical device rather than software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Elephant Healthcare
providers.description: Elephant Healthcare is a global health-technology company, headquartered in the UK, that partners with governments to digitise and strengthen public health systems across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Its flagship product, ElephantOS, is a mobile- and offline-first electronic health record (EHR) that streamlines clinical workflows for primary and secondary care facilities, serving over 19 million contracted patients across Nigeria, Kenya and Pakistan. The company also builds Elephant Nudge, a clinical co-pilot that guides and rewards quality of care, and Elephant Platform, an emerging AI-driven marketplace that connects clinicians to third-party healthcare software, medical devices and supply-chain partners. Elephant is backed by General Catalyst and Seedcamp. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Iantrek
providers.description: Iantrek, Inc. is a venture-backed ophthalmic medical technology company headquartered in White Plains, New York, pioneering the field it calls bio-interventional ophthalmic surgery (BIOS) for the treatment of glaucoma. Founded in 2019 by ophthalmic innovator Sean Ianchulev, MD, MPH, the company develops micro-interventional surgical devices that reinforce and restore the eye's natural aqueous outflow pathways with biologic allograft tissue rather than bypassing or removing tissue. Its commercial and pipeline portfolio includes AlloFlo Uveo, AlloSert Uveo, C-Rex and AlloSpan Canal. Iantrek has raised approximately $103M across its rounds, including a $42M Series C used to launch AlloFlo Uveo in the United States in October 2025. Iantrek publishes a corporate and surgeon-facing marketing website at iantrekmed.com; it operates no public developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Sully AI
providers.description: Sully AI is a US-based healthcare AI company that ships a portfolio of "AI employees" for clinical and administrative work — including an AI Scribe that turns patient conversations into structured, HIPAA-compliant notes, an AI Receptionist for scheduling and front desk, an AI Triage Nurse for patient engagement, an AI Medical Coder for autonomous ICD-10 coding, an AI Pharmacist, and an AI Consultant for chart prep. The platform integrates with Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, Athenahealth, Allscripts, Veradigm, and 50+ other EHRs. Beyond the end-user products, Sully exposes a public REST API covering audio transcription (file upload and real-time WebSocket streaming), clinical note generation (SOAP and custom templates), medical coding extraction (ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED), note templates, and a medical consensus alpha feature, with asynchronous results delivered over webhooks. Official Apache-2.0 licensed TypeScript/Node and Python SDKs are published under the sullyai GitHub org, and an Odiggo-maintained sully-api-demo repo showcases end-to-end usage. Sully's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions to healthcare providers, hospitals, and digital health platforms.

providers.name: Trupanion
providers.description: Trupanion is a pet medical insurance provider for cats and dogs, best known for its patented software that pays participating veterinary hospitals directly at checkout (VetDirectPay) rather than reimbursing pet owners after the fact. Trupanion operates a partner developer portal (Azure API Management) that exposes Partner APIs for Quotes, Enrollments, and Offers, plus a Vet Portal / VetDirectPay integration used by veterinary practice management systems such as ezyVet, IDEXX, and DaySmart Vet. API access is gated - partners must be approved through Trupanion's Partner Program and are issued OAuth client credentials (client ID and client secret) plus a subscription key; the endpoint reference is not publicly published. The APIs listed here are modeled from Trupanion's public partner and portal materials, not from an openly documented API reference.

providers.name: Acme Markets
providers.description: Acme Markets is a regional supermarket chain founded in 1891 and headquartered in the U.S. Northeast, operating approximately 164 stores across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, New York, Connecticut, and Maryland. Acme is a banner of Albertsons Companies, Inc., one of the largest food and drug retailers in the United States. The brand has no publicly documented developer program or public API: digital surfaces (store locator, loyalty program "ACME for U", FreshPass subscription, DriveUp & Go, delivery, pharmacy) are delivered through Albertsons-shared web and mobile platforms. The Android package ID (`com.safeway.client.android.acme`) confirms that the Acme app is built on the shared Safeway/Albertsons banner application, suggesting a shared backend API surface across Albertsons banners that is not externally published.

providers.name: Laboratory Corporation of America (Labcorp)
providers.description: Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings, doing business as Labcorp, is a leading global life sciences company providing diagnostic, drug development, and technology-enabled solutions to improve health and lives. This repository is an alias of the labcorp index and tracks the same FHIR / HL7 integration surface.

providers.name: Massive Bio
providers.description: Massive Bio is an AI-powered healthcare company that matches cancer patients with clinical trials. Its platform analyzes 500+ medical data elements — diagnosis, genomic profile, and clinical history — to deliver personalized trial-match reports within 24 hours, connecting patients, physicians, pharmaceutical sponsors, and research institutions. Products include a patient-facing matching service, the Trial Relay physician screening and referral tool, and iOS/Android mobile apps. The company reports 200,000+ registered patients and coverage of 19,000+ active oncology and hematology trials across multiple international markets. Massive Bio does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Numan
providers.description: Numan (trading as Vir Health Limited) is a UK-based digital healthcare and telemedicine company offering convenient, clinician-led care direct to consumers. Its services span weight-loss programmes (including GLP-1 medications such as Mounjaro and Wegovy), men's health (erectile dysfunction, hair loss, testosterone), women's health (menopause support), at-home blood tests and diagnostics, supplements, and one-off doctor consultations, delivered through its website and iOS/Android app. Numan is regulated by the Care Quality Commission and operates a GPhC-licensed pharmacy. It is a portfolio company of Anthemis. As of this enrichment pass Numan publishes no public developer API, SDKs, MCP server, or partner integration surface.

providers.name: actnano
providers.description: actnano, Inc. is a Massachusetts-based advanced materials company that develops and manufactures PFAS-free protective nanocoatings for electronics. Its flagship Advanced nanoGUARD technology is a gel-state, 100% fluorine-free conformal coating applied to printed circuit board assemblies, connectors, antennas, LEDs and high-heat-generating components, delivering up to IPx8 moisture and condensation protection without trapping heat or degrading signal integrity. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with a Munich center of excellence and operations in Mexico and Japan, actnano serves mobility and automotive electronics, consumer electronics, AI and data-center infrastructure, solar, industrial electronics, medical devices and optical anti-fog applications. The company states REACH and RoHS compliance and ISO 9001:2015 certification, and is backed by BMW i Ventures, Porsche Ventures and Emerald Technology Ventures. actnano is a materials manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Athos
providers.description: Athos is a sports performance technology company founded in 2012 and based in Redwood City, California, that builds athletic apparel with embedded surface electromyography (EMG) sensors. Its garments and snap-on Athos Core module capture muscle activity, effort, and motion data, streaming it over Bluetooth to a mobile app and coaching dashboard so athletes, trainers, and sports scientists can measure muscular exertion, fatigue, and return-to-play readiness in real time. Athos is a consumer and team hardware brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AZmed
providers.description: AZmed is a Paris-based medical-imaging AI company whose Rayvolve AI Suite assists radiologists by automatically analyzing X-rays and other studies. Its applications include AZtrauma (fracture detection), AZchest (chest imaging), AZmeasure (anatomical measurements), AZboneage (bone-age assessment) and AZnod (CT nodule detection). The software integrates into existing radiology workflows rather than being exposed as a public developer API, and is deployed across 2,500+ healthcare centers in 55+ countries, analyzing over 15 million X-rays annually, backed by 10+ peer-reviewed publications. As of this profile AZmed does not publish a public REST API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Binx Health
providers.description: binx health, inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts point-of-care diagnostics company whose binx io platform is the first FDA-cleared, CLIA-waived molecular point-of-care test for chlamydia (Chlamydia trachomatis) and gonorrhea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae), returning central-lab-equivalent results in roughly thirty minutes from female vaginal swabs or male urine so a patient can be tested, diagnosed and treated in a single visit. The instrument pairs ultra-rapid PCR amplification with the company's proprietary electrochemical detection and needs no calibration, preventative maintenance or result interpretation, so it can be run by staff with no laboratory training. binx sells into urgent care, OB/GYN, pediatrics, student health, government health and other specialty settings through distributors including Cardinal Health, McKesson, Medline and Fisher Healthcare. The company divested its at-home consumer testing business to imaware in December 2023 and retained the point-of-care molecular diagnostics business. binx health publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Biofourmis
providers.description: Biofourmis is a health technology company founded in 2015, with offices in Boston, Singapore and India, that partners with health systems, hospitals, payers and life science companies to deliver care in the home. Its platform combines medical-grade device connectivity, FDA-cleared algorithms and digital biomarkers, a patient mobile app and clinician dashboard, and 70+ dynamic care pathways to support Hospital at Home, Timely Discharge, SNF at Home and Remote Patient Monitoring programs. Biofourmis merged with CopilotIQ in October 2024 to form an end-to-end platform for AI-driven in-home care; ActiGraph acquired the Biofourmis life science business in January 2025. The company markets EMR integration and device-agnostic connectivity to enterprise healthcare customers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Cagent Vascular
providers.description: Cagent Vascular is a privately held endovascular medical device company based in Wayne, Pennsylvania, that develops and commercializes Serration Remodeling Therapy (SRT). Its flagship product, the Serranator PTA Serration Balloon Catheter, embeds stainless-steel serrated strips into a semi-compliant angioplasty balloon to create linear, interrupted micro-fissures along the artery wall, producing controlled lumen expansion at lower pressures when treating peripheral artery disease (PAD) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). The Serranator is FDA 510(k) cleared and CE marked, and the portfolio has expanded to include Serranator SL-PRO and the Serranator SONIC intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) system. Cagent Vascular is a device manufacturer rather than a software or platform company: it publishes clinical data, case studies, webinars and reimbursement material on its website, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Clarapath
providers.description: Clarapath is a medical robotics company headquartered in Hawthorne, New York that automates the tissue sectioning step of the clinical histopathology workflow. Its FDA-registered SectionStar platform pairs patented tape-transfer sectioning with precision robotics, integrated optics and sensors, and computational quality control to turn paraffin blocks into standardized slides with quantitative quality metrics. The company also ships the TrimStar Pro trimming system, a HistoStation data repository for sample and image traceability, remote Telehistology operation, and histology consulting services for hospital, reference, and veterinary laboratories.

providers.name: ClearNote Health
providers.description: ClearNote Health (formerly Bluestar Genomics) is a US cancer detection company with offices in San Diego and San Mateo, California. Its proprietary 5hmC epigenomic platform combines cell-free DNA sequencing from a standard blood draw with machine learning to identify DNA-based alterations as cancer develops. The company commercializes Avantect, a suite of early-detection liquid biopsy tests for pancreatic and ovarian cancer that clinicians order through its laboratory, and Virtuoso, a research-use-only epigenomics platform sold to biopharma for drug discovery, therapy response and resistance research. ClearNote Health publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification: the clinician ordering path is a hosted intake form, and its public GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source bioinformatics tooling.

providers.name: Digital Diagnostics
providers.description: Digital Diagnostics is a healthcare AI company based in Coralville, Iowa, founded by Dr. Michael Abramoff. It builds autonomous artificial-intelligence diagnostic systems that make a medical diagnosis at the point of care without requiring a physician to interpret the result. Its flagship product, LumineticsCore (formerly IDx-DR), was the first FDA-cleared autonomous AI diagnostic system and detects diabetic retinopathy from fundus images in about 30 seconds, reimbursed under CPT code 92229 and integrated with EHR systems such as Epic. A companion product, SphereDx, provides securely hosted diagnostic result management. The company is a portfolio company of 8vc and is researching additional indications including glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative disease detection via retinal imaging. Digital Diagnostics emphasizes ethical, equitable AI ("AI the right way") and holds ISO 13485:2016 quality-management certification. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Eleanor Health
providers.description: Eleanor Health is a value-based, whole-person addiction and mental health care provider delivering virtual and in-person treatment for substance use disorders — including opioid, alcohol, stimulant, and prescription drug use — through medication for addiction treatment (MAT), therapy, peer recovery support, and health coaching. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, the company partners with health plans and Medicaid programs across multiple U.S. states to deliver measurement-based, outcomes-driven behavioral healthcare. Eleanor Health is backed by General Catalyst. It does not publish a public developer API program; member scheduling and clinical records run on athenahealth, and its public GitHub organization holds internal engineering tooling rather than a first-party API.

providers.name: Embark
providers.description: Embark Veterinary is a dog genetics company that sells at-home canine DNA testing kits for breed identification, health condition and genetic-risk screening, trait analysis, and relative matching, alongside supplements and breeder/veterinary testing programs. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, the company operates a direct-to-consumer storefront, a help center, and a resources/blog library, but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced from VC-portfolio data; no machine-readable API surface (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP) was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Evident Vascular
providers.description: Evident Vascular, Inc. is a San Jose, California medical device company developing the Evident Vascular Guidance System, an AI-powered intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) platform purpose-built for peripheral vascular image-guided therapy, with future capability intended for coronary procedures. The company came out of stealth in 2023 with a $35M Series A led by Vensana Capital and closed a Series B in March 2025 with Shangbay Capital and strategic investors, funding work toward FDA 510(k) clearance and a U.S. launch. The platform pairs an IVUS catheter and console with machine-learning image interpretation intended to improve vessel assessment and streamline the interventional workflow. Evident Vascular is pre-commercial and publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface on its public web surface.

providers.name: Gabit
providers.description: Gabit is a one-stop health and wellness platform on a mission to add more healthy years to people's lives. Headquartered in Gurugram, India and founded in 2022 by Gaurav Gupta (ex-Zomato cofounder) and Arpana Shahi, Gabit treats health as an interconnected system across four pillars — fitness, nutrition, sleep, and mindfulness. Its consumer ecosystem spans the titanium Gabit Smart Ring, a smart body-composition scale, at-home Blood Work diagnostics, a continuous glucose monitor (CGM), the Sweden-born Näck nutrition supplement line, all-good-no-harm skincare, and coached Fitness & Nutrition Plans — all unified in the Gabit app, which tracks 150+ biomarkers and includes the free PEP AI health coach. India is the primary market, with Ring-only storefronts in the UAE and UK and an informational US/global page.

providers.name: Galvanize Therapeutics
providers.description: Galvanize Therapeutics, Inc. is a Redwood City, California medical device company founded in 2015 by Jonathan Waldstreicher, MD and William Krimsky, MD, and created and incubated by Apple Tree Partners (ATP). Galvanize develops pulsed electric field (PEF) therapies that deliver high-voltage, short-duration energy locally to alter the transmembrane potential of targeted cells, inducing non-thermal regulated cell death without denaturing cellular proteins or the extracellular matrix. Its Aliya PEF System is cleared for surgical ablation of soft tissue and is being studied in non-small cell lung cancer, while RheOx addresses chronic bronchitis in the airway. The company received FDA 510(k) clearance for the Aliya EX Generator in May 2026. Galvanize is a privately held, clinically-focused device manufacturer and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Gameto
providers.description: Gameto is a female-led clinical-stage biotechnology company redefining women's health across the reproductive lifespan. Using proprietary induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) engineering, Gameto develops ovarian cell lines that mimic the biology of the female reproductive system. Its lead product, Fertilo, is an engineered line of ovarian support cells that mature immature eggs outside the body to reduce the hormonal burden of IVF and egg freezing, and is in a Phase 3 clinical trial (FIRST). Additional programs include Deovo, an organoid of the female reproductive system for drug discovery, and Ameno, a cell-based therapeutic targeting menopause and primary ovarian insufficiency. Gameto is backed by Insight Partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Gameto publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Geltor
providers.description: Geltor is a biodesign company founded in 2015 by Alex Lorestani and Nick Ouzounov that engineers animal-free designer proteins, peptides and polypeptides and manufactures them through precision fermentation. Its Biodesigner AI computational biology platform is used to imagine, screen and optimize novel protein sequences, which are then scaled commercially as ingredients for beauty and personal care, specialty nutrition and medical/life-science applications. The portfolio includes HumaColl 21 (biomimetic human collagen), HumaColl 21 Select (a matrikine peptide complex), Elastapure (biomimetic human elastin), Collume and Caviance (vegan collagens) and PrimaColl, a Type XXI signaling collagen and the first biotech-derived collagen to receive an FDA GRAS "no questions" letter for ingestible use. Geltor sells business-to-business to brand formulators and manufacturers; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Glow
providers.description: Glow (glowing.com) is a women's health and reproductive-health technology company whose consumer mobile apps track periods, ovulation, fertility, pregnancy, and early baby development for a community of more than 25 million members. Its app suite spans Glow (ovulation and fertility), Eve by Glow (period tracking), Glow Nurture (pregnancy), and Glow Baby (infant development), and it layers AI-powered health insights through GlowGPT along with a Glow Premium subscription and a companion Glow Shop for hardware such as basal thermometers, test strips, and a smart breast pump. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network, Glow is a consumer app business with no public developer program: no API portal, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: Grail
providers.description: GRAIL, Inc. is a healthcare company headquartered in Menlo Park, California, focused on detecting cancer early, when it can be cured. Its flagship product, the Galleri multi-cancer early detection (MCED) test, uses a single blood draw and methylation-based genomic sequencing to screen for a signal shared across more than 50 types of cancer, many of which lack any recommended screening today. GRAIL runs large clinical programs including the PATHFINDER, PATHFINDER 2, and NHS-Galleri studies, and distributes Galleri through health plans, employers, and partners such as Quest Diagnostics and Junction. GRAIL is a portfolio company of investors including GV and SV Angel. It does not publish a first-party public developer API; programmatic access to Galleri ordering is offered through third-party diagnostic infrastructure partners.

providers.name: HD
providers.description: HD is an AI-native healthcare marketplace and patient-navigation platform for emerging Southeast Asia, headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand. Its consumer surface, HDmall, is a health, dental, aesthetics, and surgery marketplace that lets patients compare transparent pricing and book online across 30,000+ services from 3,000+ clinics and hospitals in Thailand (hdmall.co.th) and Indonesia (hdmall.id). AI-powered navigation turns patient symptoms into personalized, safety-checked care recommendations, and HDcare adds human-led, AI-assisted concierge support for complex surgical cases. The platform has navigated over 500,000 patients. HD is a consumer-facing healthtech operator with no public developer API or portal; the strongest machine-readable surface it publishes today is an llms.txt guiding LLMs to its canonical content. HD is a portfolio company of Partech, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Illuminate Education
providers.description: Illuminate Education is a K-12 education technology company providing assessment, data analytics, and Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) tools to schools and districts. Its platform serves roughly 17 million students across 5,200 schools and districts in all 50 states, taking a "whole child" approach that combines academic and social-emotional-behavioral data. Marquee products are FastBridge (universal screening and progress monitoring), DnA (standards-based assessment creation and scoring), and eduCLIMBER (MTSS collaboration and district data management). Illuminate does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI; data exchange runs through education-interoperability standards (LTI 1.0/1.1 Certified, OneRoster, Ed-Fi 2.5+, QTI) and partner/SIS/LMS integrations. It is a portfolio company of Insight Partners, headquartered in Irvine, California.

providers.name: Infinant Health
providers.description: Infinant Health (formerly Evolve Biosystems) is a privately held life-sciences company in Sacramento, California, spun out of the Foods for Health Institute at the University of California, Davis after more than a decade of research into the infant gut microbiome. Its foundational discovery is B. infantis EVC001, a strain of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis that metabolizes human milk oligosaccharides and has largely disappeared from infants in industrialized countries. The company commercializes that strain as Evivo, a consumer infant probiotic sold direct-to-consumer and through retail, and is developing INF108 as a drug candidate intended to reduce necrotizing enterocolitis in premature infants. Infinant Health is a biotechnology and consumer-health manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes clinical trials, peer-reviewed publications and investor material, but no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract could be found on any of its hosts.

providers.name: Internet Brands
providers.description: Internet Brands is a KKR-owned digital media and software company, founded in 1998 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, that operates a portfolio of vertical franchises across health, dental, legal, and auto/home/travel markets. Its brands include WebMD and Medscape (health), WebMD Ignite and PulsePoint (health engagement), Henry Schein One and Dentrix (dental SaaS), FindLaw and Avvo (legal), and CarsDirect and Fodor's (auto, home, and travel). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The holding company does not publish a single unified public developer API; developer surfaces live with its individual operating brands.

providers.name: Junomedical
providers.description: Junomedical (now Qunomedical) is a Berlin-based digital health company founded in 2015 by Dr. Sophie Chung that connects patients with professionally-vetted doctors and clinics for high-quality medical treatments at home and abroad. The consumer platform (qunomedical.com) offers free assessments, price matching, 24/7 patient support, and personalized treatment matching across specialties including plastic surgery, hair transplants, dentistry, oncology, orthopedics, reproductive medicine, and weight-loss surgery, serving roughly 10,000 patients a month. The company also builds Qunosuite, a patient-relationship-management (PRM) SaaS for healthcare providers. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a consumer marketplace and a provider SaaS but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Kouper Health
providers.description: Kouper Health (Kouper) is a healthcare technology company building an AI-agent orchestration layer for care navigation, deployed on top of a provider organization's existing EHR. The platform spans the full patient journey through three named agents: PRIMUS for patient access and inbound coordination (appointment scheduling, intake, insurance verification, missed-call recovery), ARCHIE for inpatient and post-acute navigation (discharge planning, home health attachment, LUPA risk), and CURA for ongoing care coordination and management (proactive outreach, reminders, check-ins, escalation). Kouper sells to health systems, independent and specialty provider groups, clinically integrated networks, risk-bearing entities, and payers, with multilingual patient engagement, human escalation, and HIPAA-compliant workflows. The company emerged from stealth in May 2025 with a $10M seed round led by General Catalyst with 25Madison and CVS Health Ventures, and operates out of New York, San Francisco, and Nashville. As of this profile Kouper publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, API reference, or machine-readable API artifacts — the product is delivered as a managed EHR-integrated service rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Lina
providers.description: Lina is a medical coworking company providing space, community, and support for independent healthcare practitioners in private practice. Founded by Vicrum Puri and Rachel Puri, Lina offers turnkey private office suites alongside on-demand medical, therapy, and bodywork spaces that are HIPAA and OSHA compliant and bookable by the hour or by the day. Locations operate in NoMad and Grand Central in New York City and Aventura, Florida, with expansion announced for Washington DC, West Palm Beach, the Upper West Side, and Brooklyn. Lina is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company. It operates a Webflow marketing site and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Mira
providers.description: Mira is a San Francisco-based consumer hardware startup building AI-powered smart glasses positioned as an always-on "second brain." Founded in 2024 by Harvard builders AnhPhu Nguyen and Caine Ardayfio (rebranded from Halo), the camera-free glasses pair a dual-waveguide display, microphone, and iOS companion app to deliver live transcription, real-time translation across 60+ languages, hands-free AI assistance, and searchable memory of everyday conversations. Mira raised a $6.6M seed round led by General Catalyst and began shipping its first devices in January 2026. It is a privacy-first consumer wearable with an iOS companion app and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: New Lantern
providers.description: New Lantern is a cloud-native, AI-native radiology platform that unifies the worklist, PACS/DICOM viewer, and AI-powered reporting into a single browser-based workspace, replacing the fragmented multi-system software stack most radiology practices run today. Its cloud-native DICOM viewer offers 3D/MPR/MIP reconstruction, mammography and PET/CT modes, and AI hanging protocols; its Curie AI reporting assistant drafts reports that a licensed radiologist reviews, edits, and signs; and NL-Vox provides radiology-tuned speech recognition, alongside intelligent worklist and case distribution, analytics, and native Epic/Oracle Health EHR integration. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco, New Lantern is backed by a $19M Series A led by Benchmark and is FDA registered as a Class I medical image communications device (21 CFR 892.2020). New Lantern does not currently expose a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and public web/security posture.

providers.name: Nix
providers.description: Nix (Nix Biosensors) develops wearable biosensor technology that analyzes sweat to deliver real-time hydration and electrolyte data. Its lightweight single-use biosensor patch continuously measures fluid and electrolyte losses and provides personalized hydration guidance to athletes, service members, and laborers. The company ships two consumer/enterprise offerings: Nix Solo, an individual app for self-monitoring hydration, and Nix Pro, a group-monitoring platform that lets coaches and supervisors track multiple users. Nix is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it operates a direct-to-consumer commerce and mobile-app business with no public developer program, API documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Nym
providers.description: Nym is a healthcare technology company providing autonomous medical coding for health systems, hospitals, and physician groups. Its proprietary Clinical Language Understanding (CLU) engine reads clinical documentation and assigns accurate medical codes (ICD-10, CPT, and E/M) without human intervention, combining machine reading with transparent, rules-based coding logic rather than generic natural language processing. Nym automates revenue cycle management to reduce coding costs, accelerate billing, and improve charge capture across 400+ US healthcare facilities, and is used by health systems including OSF, Ochsner Health, Inova, and Henry Ford. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Nym does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Onco.com
providers.description: Onco.com is a comprehensive cancer care platform operated by Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd that connects cancer patients across India with oncologists and treatment services. The platform offers priority expert oncology consultations, pan-India cancer medicine delivery at discounted rates, diagnostic testing and imaging, curated treatment packages with negotiated hospital rates, and the CanWin peer support group for survivors and caregivers. Onco.com reports a network of 400+ oncologists and 23+ treatment centers, having served more than 100,000 patients. It also publishes extensive patient-education content covering many cancer types (breast, lung, blood, prostate, colon, and others) through its About Cancer library and blog. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company; the platform is consumer/patient facing and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Pattern Bioscience
providers.description: Pattern Bioscience is a privately held in vitro diagnostics company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, developing a culture-free Single-Cell Microbiology system for rapid bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing (ID/AST). The platform isolates individual bacterial cells in picoliter-scale droplets and reads the metabolic patterns those cells produce over time, using machine learning to identify the pathogen and determine phenotypic susceptibility in hours instead of the days a culture workflow requires. The company holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for its Pneumonia Action Panel, raised $43M in Series D financing in November 2025 to pursue FDA clearance, and is backed by Illumina Ventures, Omnimed Capital, CARB-X, the AMR Action Fund and a $22.5M BARDA contract. Pattern is pre-commercial: it publishes a marketing and news site at pattern.bio and no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE)
providers.description: Pedestal Health, formerly Target RWE (and NoviSci), is a Durham, North Carolina real-world evidence and health-data company serving life sciences organizations and health systems. It generates regulatory-grade real-world evidence from large-scale observational data and longitudinal patient cohorts across hepatology, dermatology, and gastroenterology (including the TARGET-NASH, TARGET-Derm, and TARGET-Gastro registries), supporting clinical development, regulatory strategy, and care delivery. The company operates as a data, research, and services provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched from the company's public website (targetrwe.com now redirects to pedestalhealth.com).

providers.name: Pluro
providers.description: Pluro is India's fertility and IVF platform, built as a co-creation model with doctors for patients. It delivers personalised, evidence-based reproductive care through a growing network of 15+ clinics across India, combining advanced clinical science, AI-assisted embryology, standardised treatment protocols, and transparent pricing. Founded by Dr. Bhaskar Shah, Dr. Jaydeep Tank, and Dr. Parikshit Tank, Pluro raised a Rs 125 crore Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners in 2025. It offers IVF/ICSI, IUI, ovulation induction, and a range of diagnostic and surgical fertility treatments. Pluro publishes an llms.txt for AI agents but exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Repertoire Immune Medicines
providers.description: Repertoire Immune Medicines is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company (with a site in Schlieren, Switzerland) building immune medicines grounded in the human T cell repertoire. Its proprietary DECODE platform characterizes the immune synapse by identifying T cell receptor (TCR) and antigen (peptide-MHC) pairs together with T cell function and HLA presentation, and uses that map to rationally design treatments across oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease. Backed by Flagship Pioneering and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It publishes no public developer API; its only public technical surface is a small research GitHub organization.

providers.name: Second Nature
providers.description: Second Nature is a UK-based digital weight-loss programme that combines NHS-trusted, CQC-regulated clinical care with dietitian-led coaching and behaviour-change support. The service pairs weight-loss medication (including Wegovy, Mounjaro, oral semaglutide and Orlistat programmes) with personalised medication reviews, a mobile app for tracking, and a science-based content library of guides and member stories. It operates as a registered pharmacy, supports NHS referrals and partnerships, and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Speedinvest. As of this enrichment pass Second Nature publishes a consumer marketing site and an llms.txt discovery file but exposes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Sensorum Health
providers.description: Sensorum Health is a healthcare technology company that provides home-based, fully passive sensor technology and integrated clinical services to identify and triage the earliest signs of health decline in older adults living with chronic conditions. The platform monitors patients 24/7 in their own homes without requiring wearables, smartphones, or WiFi, then coordinates clinical interventions when concerning health patterns emerge — with the goal of preventing avoidable hospital admissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). Added to the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record; no public API, specification, or developer program has been published as of this profile.

providers.name: Synapsor
providers.description: Synapsor (legal entity Ottai Technology (Wuxi) Co. Ltd.) is a Chinese medical-device company based in Wuxi, Jiangsu that develops AI-powered, medical-grade smart wearable devices. Its flagship product is the Ottai continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system - a waterproof, calibration-free wearable sensor paired with a mobile app and AI assistant for 24/7 glucose tracking and diabetes management, sold in China and internationally via ottai.com. Investors include Qiming Venture Partners, Huatai Zijin Investment, Wuxi Industry Development Group, YuanBio Venture Capital, and Shunwei Capital. Synapsor publishes no public developer API, portal, or machine-readable API specifications as of July 2026.

providers.name: Tembo Health
providers.description: Tembo Health is a telemedicine practice (founded 2018) that partners with skilled nursing facilities and senior living communities to deliver 24/7 virtual specialty and urgent care to elderly residents. Its board-certified clinicians provide treat-in-place emergency medicine, psychiatry, cardiology, and dementia care, reducing avoidable ER transfers by roughly 75 percent, and the company works with senior-care operators and EHR platforms such as PointClickCare. Tembo Health is a healthcare services provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Waymark
providers.description: Waymark is a healthcare technology and services company that scales value-based, community-based care for people enrolled in Medicaid. In partnership with health plans and primary care providers, Waymark trains and employs local care teams — community health workers, care coordinators, licensed therapists, and pharmacists — and equips them with predictive technology that identifies high-risk patients and coordinates interventions addressing the social determinants of health such as housing, food security, transportation, medication management, and behavioral health. The model is designed to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and emergency room visits, and Waymark operates community-based care across Ohio, Virginia, and Washington. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), NEA, Lux Capital, and CVS Health Ventures. Waymark publishes no public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its public web presence.

providers.name: Amera
providers.description: Amera (Amera Health Solutions) is a Seattle-based, Y Combinator (Fall 2025) healthcare technology company that automates claims processing workflows for health insurance payers, third-party administrators (TPAs), and self-insured employers. Its normalization engine ingests messy claim inputs from any source — EDI, PDFs, paper, fax, and proprietary/non-standard formats — and turns them into adjudication-ready, structured data that plugs into existing claims cores via API, EDI, or SFTP. The platform automates validation, reconciliation, stop-loss reporting, and real-time visibility and analytics, reducing plan administration costs and cutting carrier submission times from weeks to minutes while keeping full audit trails and HIPAA compliance. Founded in 2025 by Louise Tanski and Deep Kapur (both formerly of Rupa Health), Amera already works with payers and plan administrators representing roughly 100,000 members. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Amera does not yet publish a public developer portal or API specification.

providers.name: Conceivable Life Sciences
providers.description: Conceivable Life Sciences is a fertility technology company founded in 2021 that builds AURA, an AI-powered, end-to-end automated in vitro fertilization (IVF) laboratory. AURA combines six integrated robotic workstations, advanced optics, machine vision and AI inference to automate more than 200 manual embryology steps — sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, dish preparation, embryo culture and vitrification — so that embryologists supervise rather than perform each micromanipulation. The company raised a $50M Series A in September 2025 (bringing total funding to $70M), opened the first automated IVF lab in Mexico City, and has partnered with IVI RMA Global to deploy AURA in a US clinic. Its public surface is a corporate and scientific one — research papers, patents, press and clinical trial registrations — with no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Nuevo Método
providers.description: Nuevo Método (NUME) is an international digital-health and corporate-wellness platform, headquartered in Mexico City and operating across 17 countries in Latin America and Europe. It helps insurers and enterprises deliver personalized wellbeing benefits to employees, customers, and their families across three pillars: mental health (psychology sessions, mindfulness, meditation, sleep tracking), physical health (24/7 virtual medical consultations, fertility guidance, menstrual-cycle tracking, health workshops), and lifestyle (personal-finance courses, financial advisory, and inspirational talks). The company runs a fully remote workforce and reports measurable client outcomes such as improved sleep, productivity, and employee retention. Founded and led by Dr. Ingrid Briggiler (CEO). No public API or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures the company's identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Reliance Health
providers.description: Reliance Health (formerly RelianceHMO) is a healthtech company making quality healthcare accessible and affordable across emerging markets, with operations centered in Nigeria and expanding across Africa and the Middle East. It offers employer-sponsored and individual health plans covering preventative, emergency, and chronic care, telemedicine and doctor consultations through its mobile app, and a network of 3,800+ healthcare partners (hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and diagnostic centers). Reliance Health combines insurance, its own clinics, and technology to deliver an end-to-end care experience for businesses and their employees. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; the reliancehmo.com application backend (api.reliancehmo.com) is an internal web-app origin, not a documented public API.

providers.name: Wellxai
providers.description: Wellx (Wellxai) is a Dubai-based health insurtech company that transforms health insurance from reactive to proactive through AI-driven behavior change. Its consumer mobile app pairs behavioral science and gamification with wearable integrations (Fitbit, Apple Watch, Whoop) so members earn xCoins rewards by hitting health goals, step and sleep challenges, and wellness programs, then redeem them with marketplace partners. Wellx also sells to corporates and SMEs and partners with brokers and insurers, positioning healthier behavior as the driver of better-value health insurance. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company exposes consumer iOS/Android apps backed by a private API but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Aculys
providers.description: Aculys Pharma, Inc. is a Japanese clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on neurological and psychiatric diseases where there is high unmet medical need. The company works to eliminate Japan's drug lag and drug loss by bringing innovative medicines already approved in Western markets to Japanese patients as early as possible. Its lead product is Spydia (diazepam nasal spray), Japan's first domestically developed intranasal anti-seizure agent, approved in June 2025 and administrable outside medical facilities. Originally funded by SoftBank Vision Fund (Series C, March 2025), Aculys was acquired by and became part of the Viatris Group in October 2025. Aculys publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained for network completeness and identity.

providers.name: Calviri
providers.description: Calviri is a Phoenix, Arizona biotechnology company, founded in 2017, that develops multi-cancer diagnostic tests and therapeutic and preventative cancer vaccines for dogs and people. Its science rests on RNA-Error Derived Neoantigens (REDNs) — abnormal proteins thrown off by the error-prone RNA processing of tumor cells — which Calviri builds as peptides on semiconductor chips and then queries against an individual's blood for antibody responses, using those antibodies as sensitive biomarkers of cancer. Its lead product, StageOne Plus, is a canine multi-cancer blood test designed to detect stage 1 disease before signs appear, alongside a pipeline of canine and human therapeutic and preventative vaccines and a preventative-vaccine trial (VACCS) that enrolled 800+ dogs. Calviri is a life-sciences company with no developer program, no product API and no developer portal; the only machine-readable surface on calviri.com is the Wix-platform-generated llms.txt and the anonymous site MCP endpoint it advertises.

providers.name: Clinikk
providers.description: Clinikk (Clinikk Health Hub) is a Bangalore, India-based primary healthcare provider offering membership-based access to unlimited doctor consultations, free prescribed medicines and lab tests, 24/7 teleconsultation, and optional group health insurance in partnership with IndusInd General Insurance. Clinikk operates in-person Health Hubs across Bangalore alongside a consumer mobile app, and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Abbott Laboratories
providers.description: Abbott Laboratories is a global healthcare company that develops, manufactures, and markets pharmaceuticals, medical devices, diagnostics, and nutritional products. Abbott's digital health portfolio includes the FreeStyle Libre continuous glucose monitoring system, cardiac monitoring devices, and connected diagnostics platforms that enable data sharing between patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers.

providers.name: Ambient Clinical Analytics
providers.description: Ambient Clinical Analytics is a Rochester, Minnesota clinical decision support company spun out of Mayo Clinic in 2013 and operating from the Mayo Clinic Business Accelerator. Its AWARE Patient Surveillance and AWARE Sepsis DART products are FDA Class II cleared, EMR-agnostic "bolt-on" dashboards that apply more than 1,200 licensed Mayo Clinic rules and algorithms to live patient data, delivering point-of-care data visualization, situational awareness of a patient's total condition, and smart notifications for conditions such as sepsis across ICU, tele-ICU and remote patient monitoring settings. Deployment is carried out by third-party EMR data-integration partners rather than by hospital IT; the company publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: BetterNight
providers.description: BetterNight is a San Diego, California virtual-care sleep health company that diagnoses and treats obstructive sleep apnea end to end: telemedicine consults with sleep physicians, home sleep testing devices shipped to the patient, board-certified interpretation and therapy recommendation, home delivery of PAP and oral appliance therapy, and ongoing coaching by sleep specialists and respiratory therapists. It also offers a cognitive behavioral therapy program for insomnia and remote patient monitoring of PAP adherence. The company sells to individuals as well as to physicians, cardiologists, ENT practices, clinics, health plans and ACOs, employers, and DOT/commercial transportation programs.
